name: Walker S2
desc: The UBTech Walker S2 is a full-size industrial humanoid (about 1.76 m, 70 kg, 52 degrees of freedom) and the headline successor to UBTech's factory-deployed Walker S line, which works on NIO and BYD assembly lines. Its standout feature is a world-first autonomous battery-swap system: the robot walks to a docking station and swaps its own depleted pack for a charged one in about three minutes using dual-battery dynamic balancing, enabling near 24/7 operation. A high-torque waist (±162° rotation) and fourth-generation bionic hands give sub-millimetre manipulation and up to 15 kg dual-arm payload across a ~1.8 m workspace. It runs UBTech's ROSA 2.0 stack on Ubuntu with the Co-Agent and BrainNet 2.0 dual-loop AI system for task planning, semantic VSLAM navigation and exception handling, fusing dual-RGB stereo vision, six-axis force sensing and IMU on x86 + NVIDIA Jetson Orin compute. Walker S2 entered mass production in late 2025, making it one of the first humanoids to reach genuine series production.
cameras: Multiple RGB cameras and depth cameras

desc: The Franka Research 3 (FR3) is the reference force-sensitive robot of the AI and robot-learning research world — the successor to the Franka Emika Panda, engineered and made in Germany, and adopted by leading universities and labs worldwide. Its foundation is a 7-DoF torque-controlled arm with a link-side torque sensor in every joint, giving fine estimation of external contact forces, compliant hand-guiding at ~2.5 N, and the sensitivity to be stopped by a balloon. The 3 kg / 855 mm arm (17.8 kg, IP40) exposes both easy and deep control: the browser-based Desk UI with no-code Apps for rapid setup, and the 1 kHz Franka Control Interface (FCI) via libfranka for real-time torque control that made it the standard research platform — with official franka_ros/ros2 and MATLAB/Simulink integration. It's TÜV SÜD-certified to PL d Cat. 3 with a full safe-motion function set (SLP, SLS, SLD, SEEPO), runs from a compact 80 W controller, and continuously improves via free OTA system images. Franka Hand and vacuum grippers integrate plug-and-use.

Built on a well-known vineyard crawler design (68 cm width, 3 m U-turn), JO operates fully autonomously for 8+ hours using 3-4 swappable Iron-Phosphate Lithium batteries. Carries the same tools as conventional vineyard crawlers, with 250 kg lift capacity and electrical power output for plugging in electrical tools. Two 3000 W 48 V motors drive the crawler tracks.
cameras: Vision system for crop and obstacle detection
autonomy_level: Full autonomy with bumper safety + geo-fencing

name: TED
desc: First autonomous straddler robot for vineyards — drives over the tops of vineyard rows with full inter-row and intra-row management capability (weeding with blades/disks/plows, canopy management). 6-foot platform, ~1 mph travel speed, 8-hour battery life. Currently deployed in vineyards across Europe and reaching commercial scale in California wine regions.
cameras: Multiple cameras for navigation and obstacle detection
autonomy_level: Full autonomy with safety bumpers + geo-fencing
compatible_tools: Blades, disks, plows for inter-row weeding; canopy management tools

name: Burro Original
desc: Burro is an autonomous wheeled transport robot that carries harvested produce and supplies through orchards and vineyards, following workers or running learned routes (~230 kg class) - reducing manual carrying labour with vision-based autonomy.

name: Burro Grande
desc: Burro's most powerful labor-saving autonomous robot — pallet-scale vehicle handling 680 kg (1,500 lb) payload and towing 2,268 kg (5,000 lb). Features Burro Operation System Software 5.0 with LiDAR-based localization for autonomous movement across indoor and outdoor operations. 24 km (15 mi) range, all-electric. Pairs with Atlas Mission Autonomy online route platform. Won 2024 World Ag Expo Top-10 New Product (3rd consecutive year). 18-22 inch tires with R1/R3/R4 tread options; LiDAR sees 40 m / 120 ft, 360°.
cameras: Multiple cameras for navigation and mapping
navigation: LiDAR-based localization + RTK-GPS + computer vision + AI
awards: 2024 World Ag Expo Top-10 New Product

name: Burro XL
desc: Wider-wheelbase variant of the standard Burro for improved stability on uneven terrain. Same Burro plug-and-play AI/RTK-GPS autonomy stack but with a 36-inch wider XL kit that improves handling on slopes and rough ground. Compatible with Burro's standard top trays and accessory ecosystem.

name: Vulcan Triple-Bed
desc: Triple-bed configuration of the Vulcan precision weeder — three 80–84 inch beds (combined ~6 m total width) accommodating up to 18 crop rows in a single pass. Designed for large-scale specialty vegetable operations where throughput matters. Same Intelligent Plant System AI/IPS engine as the single-bed.
cameras: Multiple computer vision cameras for crop and weed identification

name: Vulcan Single-Bed
desc: Single-bed configuration of the Vulcan precision weeder — 80–84 inch (2.03–2.13 m) bed accommodating 1 to 6 crop rows. Lighter than triple-bed model (~3,500 lb / 1,588 kg) which allows weeding in wetter field conditions with less soil compaction. Pulled by Cat II 3-point hitch on ~150 HP tractor.
cameras: Multiple computer vision cameras for crop and weed identification

name: Max
desc: Iron Ox's first-generation autonomous greenhouse robot — a UR10-derived robotic arm 'Max' that worked alongside the mobile module 'Angus' to transplant, harvest, and care for plants in Iron Ox's San Carlos greenhouse. Demonstrated the company's vision of fully robotic indoor agriculture, with computer vision plant-by-plant care. Replaced in later Iron Ox systems by the more capable Phil/Sage/Olive arms with custom designs. Operational at Iron Ox's pilot greenhouse 2018-2022.
cameras: Multiple computer vision cameras for plant monitoring and navigation
pricing_model: Not commercially sold (operated as a service via Iron Ox-run greenhouses)
ai_capabilities: Plant-level computer vision, plant identification, ripeness detection
navigation: Worked with mobile module Angus for travel
manipulation: Custom end effectors for transplanting, harvesting, plant care
successor: Iron Ox Phil, Sage, Olive (custom-built next-gen arms)

name: Joby S4-T Hybrid Demonstrator
desc: Military-focused hybrid variant developed with L3Harris Technologies, integrating gas-turbine generator with electric VTOL platform for extended range and military applications.
cameras: Multi-spectral imaging systems for surveillance and navigation

name: Volocopter 2X
desc: Volocopter's production-intent two-seat eVTOL multicopter, unveiled at AERO Friedrichshafen in 2017 as the successor to the VC200. Its signature look is 18 electrically driven rotors on a circular frame (~9.15 m across) above the cabin, powered by nine lithium-ion batteries. It carries two people at up to 100 km/h (cruising ~70 km/h) for about 27 km / 27 minutes, on a carbon-fibre fuselage with fixed skids, and can be flown by joystick or autonomously with a forgiving control system that holds altitude and position on its own. A whole-aircraft ballistic parachute and redundant distributed propulsion back its safety case. The 2X made high-profile public flights - including carrying Intel's CEO at CES 2018 and an early flight in Dubai - and served as the stepping stone to Volocopter's certified air taxi, the VoloCity.

name: VoloRegion
desc: Volocopter's winged, longer-range eVTOL (unveiled in 2021 as the VoloConnect and renamed VoloRegion in October 2022), meant to extend urban air mobility from the city core out to the suburbs. Its lift-plus-cruise layout uses six lift rotors on twin booms spanning tandem wings (a forward-swept front wing and a rear gull-wing/V-tail) for vertical takeoff, then two rear electric ducted fans for efficient winged forward flight - eight electric motors in all. It carries four passengers up to 100 km at a 180 km/h cruise (250 km/h top speed) with a 300-400 kg payload, on an all-electric battery-swap system, a carbon-fibre fuselage and retractable tricycle gear, using fly-by-wire controls (piloted first, autonomous later) with multiple redundant systems toward EASA SC-VTOL enhanced certification. Its prototype first flew in May 2022; the program's future is uncertain following Volocopter's 2025 insolvency and acquisition by Diamond Aircraft (Wanfeng).
config: 6 lift rotors (twin booms) + 2 rear EDF cruise; 8 motors, tandem wings

name: Titan FT-35
desc: FarmWise's original driverless mechanical weeder — named one of TIME magazine's 'Best Inventions of 2020' and the first-ever automated weeder to use machine learning. Diesel-powered, originally offered exclusively as a Robot-as-a-Service (RaaS) at <$500/acre. Used computer vision and ML to identify crops vs weeds, then robotic blades actuated around plant stems with sub-inch accuracy. Production was discontinued after 2023, succeeded by the lighter, buyable Vulcan implement. Crops served: lettuce, broccoli, celery, cauliflower, radicchio, artichokes.
cameras: Multiple RGB CMOS (1 per row, ~6 total)

name: VoloXPro
desc: Volocopter's first product under new owner Diamond Aircraft (Wanfeng), unveiled 22 April 2026 at AERO Friedrichshafen. The VoloXPro is a fully electric, two-seat ultralight multicopter with 18 rotors and fly-by-wire controls, pitched mainly as a low-cost trainer and powered-lift transition platform (its eVTOL architecture lets pilots qualify toward types like Joby or Archer) as well as a sightseeing and, outside Europe, air-taxi aircraft. It reuses components from Volocopter's VoloCity air taxi for airliner-grade safety in the ultralight class, cruises at 70 km/h with up to ~40 km of range (26-36 km single-pilot, less as an air taxi, across three battery variants), and carries a 154 kg payload within a 600 kg European ultralight max takeoff mass (620 kg elsewhere). Base price is EUR490,000, with German ultralight certification targeted for the end of 2026.
range_note: 26-36 km single-pilot; less as air taxi (3 battery variants)

name: VoloCity
desc: Volocopter's flagship air taxi and the aircraft it has taken furthest toward certification - the fifth-generation design first unveiled in 2019. Its signature 18 electrically driven rotors sit on a circular frame above a two-seat cabin (one pilot plus one passenger), all-electric on nine swappable battery packs. It's built for short urban hops: ~35 km range at a 90 km/h cruise within a ~900 kg max takeoff mass, and it's about four times quieter than a small helicopter because all 18 rotors run in a narrow frequency band that largely cancels out. Multiple redundant systems (rotors, motors, batteries, avionics and displays all at least doubled) and fly-by-wire controls - piloted first, autonomous later - back its safety case, and it's being certified in EASA's demanding SC-VTOL 'enhanced' category (Design Organisation Approval already earned, type certification in progress) after 2,000+ test flights in cities like Hamburg, Dubai, Singapore and Paris. Development continues under new owner Diamond Aircraft (Wanfeng).
cert: EASA SC-VTOL enhanced (DOA earned; TC in progress)

name: VoloDrone
desc: Volocopter's unmanned, fully electric heavy-lift utility drone - the cargo cousin of its air taxis, first demonstrated in October 2019. It reuses the same 18-rotor multicopter platform (9.2 m rotor diameter, 2.3 m tall) and swappable lithium-ion batteries, but instead of a cabin it has a standardized rail attachment system between its landing gear that accepts a wide range of payloads - boxes, slings, nets, containers, sprayers or spreaders - sized for Euro-pallet loads. It lifts up to 200 kg over 40 km at up to 110 km/h (about 30 minutes of flight), flown remotely or autonomously on pre-set routes (with BVLOS work via Near Earth Autonomy). Aimed at logistics, agriculture (a crop-spraying variant was developed with John Deere), infrastructure and public services, it targets missions where ground transport struggles with access.
payload_options: Box, sling, net, container, sprayer, spreader
control: Remote-piloted or autonomous (BVLOS w/ Near Earth)

name: Wingcopter 198 LiDAR Surveying
desc: The long-range LiDAR-surveying configuration of Wingcopter's flagship 198 - the same patented tilt-rotor eVTOL used for delivery, re-purposed (from Feb 2025) with a high-end laser scanner and camera system to map linear infrastructure at scale. The tilt-rotor airframe (198 x 152 x 65 cm, 25 kg max takeoff weight, eight rotors of which four tilt, plus winglets) hovers to launch then cruises efficiently at 90 km/h, carrying a ~4.5 kg sensor payload up to 60 km of infrastructure in a single BVLOS mission. Its LiDAR offers a 100-degree field of view and up to a 2.4 MHz pulse rate, firing the beam in three directions (nadir, +10 and -10 degrees) for complete capture of vertical surfaces, canyons and power lines, yielding up to 570 points/m2 at 10 mm accuracy / 5 mm precision - covering 10.3 km2 (~2,500 acres) in about 42 minutes. Redundant flight controls (dual airspeed/heading/GNSS, eight motors and ESCs, two hot-swap smart batteries) and a 5,000 m ceiling suit it to inspecting power lines, pipelines, railways and roads and mapping hard-to-reach terrain.
cameras: High-resolution RGB camera for visual inspection
survey_range: Up to 60 km linear per mission

name: eBee
desc: Professional autonomous mini-drone weighing less than 700g. Features integrated autopilot, no piloting skills required, and includes eMotion flight planning software and Postflight Terra 3D processing software.
cameras: Integrated RGB camera, supports various payload cameras

name: Joby S4-T Hybrid
desc: The Joby S4-T is a tactical/hybrid variant of Joby Aviation's S4 eVTOL - a six-tilt-rotor aircraft carrying four passengers plus pilot at up to ~322 km/h. All-electric with a hydrogen-electric hybrid demonstrator extending range well beyond the baseline ~240 km, it is being evaluated by the US DoD under the Air Force's Agility Prime programme.
cameras: Multiple cameras for navigation and surveillance

name: Joby S4 Hydrogen-Electric
desc: A hydrogen-electric version of Joby's S4 tilt-rotor air taxi, built to show that liquid hydrogen could unlock emissions-free regional flying without a runway. Joby converted a retired pre-production battery-electric S4 (prototype N542BJ) in a matter of weeks - keeping ~90% of the aircraft the same - by adding a Joby-built 40 kg liquid-hydrogen tank (cryogenic, ~22 K, vacuum-jacketed) and an H2FLY H2F-175 fuel-cell system that produces electricity, water and heat; the fuel cell powers the six tilting rotors while a small supplemental battery adds takeoff/landing power and is recharged in cruise. On 24 June 2024 it flew a record 523 miles (842 km) non-stop in 4h47m - believed to be the first forward flight of a liquid-hydrogen-powered VTOL - landing with 10% fuel remaining, and later reached 561 miles, with water vapor as the only emission. Internally nicknamed 'SHy4' (S4 + H2FLY's HY4), it reuses Joby's ElevateOS software, landing pads and operations model, and the program is backed by the USAF's Agility Prime.
shared_systems: ~90% shared with battery S4; ElevateOS, same pads/ops

name: Joby S4 (JAS4-1)
desc: Joby's flagship battery-electric air taxi, the production-prototype S4 (FAA type designation JAS4-1). It's a tilt-rotor eVTOL with six tilting propellers driven by dual-wound electric motors, carrying a pilot plus four passengers at up to ~200 mph over roughly 100 miles (including reserves) while staying notably quiet. Public/regulatory figures put empty weight around 1,950 kg, useful payload near 454 kg, and FAA maximum gross takeoff weight at 2,177 kg (rotor diameter ~2.9 m is a best-available estimate). It flies on Joby's ElevateOS operating software and is one of the furthest-along aircraft in FAA type certification - reaching Type Inspection Authorization in late 2025 and beginning flight testing of its first FAA-conforming aircraft in 2026 - backed by investors including Toyota, Delta, Uber and SK Telecom, with an early launch planned in Dubai.
cert: FAA type cert in progress (TIA late 2025)

name: eBee Classic
desc: The original eBee - senseFly's foam-airframe fixed-wing mapping drone that helped popularize professional drone surveying. Hand-launched and belly-landed with no need for a runway, the ~96 cm wingspan, ~0.69 kg aircraft flew up to 50 minutes and could map as much as 12 km2 in a single high-altitude flight at cruise speeds of 40-90 km/h, producing imagery down to a few centimeters per pixel. It carried a compact ~16MP RGB camera and flew autonomously via senseFly's eMotion planning software with a linear-landing approach and obstacle detection. A workhorse for land surveying, agriculture and GIS, it was later superseded by the modular eBee X line (now under AgEagle).
cameras: Fixed RGB camera for aerial photography and mapping

name: eBee Plus
desc: Fixed-wing photogrammetric mapping drone featuring RTK/PPK upgradeability for survey-grade accuracy, larger airframe without added weight, and S.O.D.A. sensor with 2.8 cm GSD at 400 feet

name: Albris
desc: Sensor-rich quadcopter optimized for inspection with triple-sensor head (RGB, HD video, thermal), 180° camera tilt, five dual-sensor modules for situational awareness, and TripleView imaging system
cameras: RGB camera, thermal camera, HD video camera with 180° tilt capability

name: eBee Geo
desc: Affordable fixed-wing mapping drone with 45.7 inch wingspan, designed for surveyors and GIS professionals with rugged airframe and S.O.D.A. camera for precise mapping
cameras: S.O.D.A. RGB camera with global shutter, 20MP resolution

name: eBee X
desc: Professional fixed-wing mapping drone with 45.7 inch wingspan, multiple sensor compatibility, RTK/PPK support for 3cm accuracy, and advanced Steep Landing technology for challenging sites
cameras: Supports multiple sensors including RGB, multispectral, thermal cameras

name: Wingcopter 178 Heavy Lift
desc: The heavy-lift version of Wingcopter's 178, reinforced with glass- and carbon-fibre layers and a more powerful propulsion system to carry heavier professional payloads and sensors while keeping high commonality with the base aircraft. Measuring 48 x 178 x 146 cm and weighing 8.4 kg empty (up to an 18 kg max takeoff weight with four batteries), it lifts up to 6 kg, flies up to ~120 minutes / 120 km (unladen) at up to 150 km/h, and in 2018 set a Guinness World Record for the fastest tilt-rotor aircraft at 240.6 km/h. It runs on 2-4 lithium-polymer packs with a rich sensor set (dual-GNSS, dual magnetometer, IMU, pitot, LiDAR altimeter, ADS-B) and triple-redundant telemetry (RC radio, 4G cellular and Iridium satellite), delivering by winch slow-drop or landing. It has flown high-profile humanitarian missions with DHL and UNICEF - vaccine and medical delivery in Vanuatu, Malawi and Tanzania.
cameras: HD camera for monitoring and navigation
sensors: Dual-GNSS, dual magnetometer, IMU, pitot, LiDAR altimeter; ADS-B
deployments: DHL, UNICEF vaccine delivery (Vanuatu, Malawi, Tanzania)

name: Wingcopter 178
desc: Wingcopter's first mass-produced delivery drone and the platform that established its patented tilt-rotor design, where the same propellers hover for vertical takeoff then tilt forward for efficient fixed-wing cruise (the '178' is its 178 cm wingspan). Roughly 178 x 132 x 52 cm, it carries up to 6 kg and flies about 100 km with a 2 kg payload at up to 150 km/h, operating beyond visual line of sight. It can deliver either by winching a package down for a slow-drop without landing, or by landing to enable two-way transport of medical samples and supplies. Widely used for last-mile medical delivery as well as mapping and surveying, it laid the groundwork for the later triple-drop Wingcopter 198.
cameras: HD camera for navigation and monitoring

name: Wingcopter 198
desc: Electric tilt-rotor VTOL drone with triple-drop delivery capability, 8 motors for redundancy, 198cm wingspan, 94km range, designed for Level 4 autonomous operations
cameras: Multiple cameras for navigation and monitoring

name: eBee TAC Public Safety
desc: Public safety variant of the eBee TAC designed for emergency response and law enforcement applications

name: eBee VISION
desc: First surveillance drone in the eBee series with NDAA compliance for commercial surveillance operations

name: eBee TAC
desc: The senseFly-branded eBee TAC (senseFly was acquired by AgEagle in 2021) is the same hand-launched fixed-wing tactical mapping/ISR drone: 90-minute endurance, ~28 km range, AES-256 security and RTK/PPK 1.5 cm accuracy. Designed and assembled in Switzerland and used by defense agencies globally.
cameras: RGB camera with tactical imaging capabilities

name: eBee TAC Government
desc: The government configuration of the AgEagle eBee TAC, cleared on the DoD Blue UAS list for federal procurement. It pairs the 90-minute fixed-wing mapping platform with cyber-secure features - AES-256 radio, encrypted storage, log suppression and silent mission mode - for tactical mapping and ISR in disconnected or contested environments.

name: eBee TAC
desc: A cyber-secure, tactical version of AgEagle's (senseFly) eBee X fixed-wing mapping drone, aimed at public-safety and defense users. Carried in a backpack, hand-launched and deployed in 3 minutes by one person, it delivers 2D, 3D and thermal aerial data over large areas - up to 500 ha (1,235 ac) in a single 90-minute flight with a 55 km range - at 1.5 cm accuracy using optional RTK/PPK. Its ~1.16 m wingspan airframe weighs just 1.3-1.6 kg, and it's built for discreet operation: an AES-256-encrypted radio link, encrypted SD card, silent radio mission and flight-log suppression, plus a low visual and acoustic signature that makes it nearly undetectable at 300 m AGL. It's Blue UAS registered (cleared for US DoD procurement), is among the only UAVs FAA-approved for Operations Over People, integrates with CivTAK and NATO's MGRS grid via eMotion software, and is trusted by users like the US Army Corps of Engineers and the French Navy.
security: AES-256 radio, encrypted SD, silent mission, log suppression
signature: Low visible + acoustically undetectable at 300 m AGL
certification: Blue UAS registered; FAA OOP approved
operators: US Army Corps of Engineers, French Navy

name: Percepto Base
desc: The industrial docking station at the heart of Percepto's drone-in-a-box system - the 'box' that lets a Percepto Air drone operate fully autonomously, 24/7/365. It shelters and charges the drone between missions and handles automatic data upload and pre-flight checks, with an on-board module guiding the drone's takeoff and return. Built for the harshest sites, it's waterproof and weatherproof (heavy rain, snow, high winds, dust) and tested to hurricane-force-5 winds, with an HVAC unit and weather station to keep the drone mission-ready in extreme conditions. It plugs into Percepto's AIM (Autonomous Inspection & Monitoring) platform for optimized visual-data management and AI analytics, and underpins Percepto's FAA BVLOS-approved remote operations across oil & gas, utilities, mining and heavy industry.
function: Charge, shelter, data upload, pre-flight checks
data: Auto secure upload to AIM cloud

name: eBee TAC
desc: The AgEagle eBee TAC is a hand-launched fixed-wing tactical mapping and ISR drone with 90-minute endurance, ~28 km range and 1.6 kg weight, deployable in three minutes by one operator. NDAA-compliant and Blue UAS-cleared, it adds AES-256 encryption, a silent/covert mode, digital camouflage and RTK/PPK 1.5 cm mapping accuracy; the US Army has procured units.
cameras: RGB camera with optional thermal imaging

name: eBee Ag
desc: Affordable fixed-wing agriculture drone from AgEagle (which acquired senseFly in 2021). Combines a dual-purpose RGB + 4-band multispectral camera (Duet M) to generate NDVI, NDRE, and DSM maps for crop scouting. Up to 55-minute flight time with endurance battery, covers 160 hectares (395 acres) in a single flight. With optional RTK, achieves 2.5 cm (1 in) absolute accuracy. Light weight (1.6 kg) qualifies for BVLOS and Operations Over People in many regulatory frameworks. Compatible with major FMIS — Climate FieldView, My John Deere, PIX4D, DroneDeploy, Trimble Ag, AGCO Fuse, xarvio, etc.
made_in: Switzerland (senseFly heritage; AgEagle USA brand since 2021 acquisition)
landing_method: Automatic linear landing (5 m accuracy, 20° angle cone)
frame_material: Reinforced polypropylene woven mesh underbelly (shock absorbent)
manufacturer_history: Originally senseFly (Swiss, founded 2009). Acquired by AgEagle 2021. senseFly brand officially retired 2023.

name: eBee Geo
desc: An affordable fixed-wing mapping drone from AgEagle's senseFly eBee line, aimed at surveyors, civil engineers and GIS professionals. Built on the eBee X airframe (~1.16 m wingspan) but kept light at ~1.3 kg - under the 2 kg line for easier regulatory approval and FAA Remote ID compliant - it hand-launches, belly-lands and maps up to 160 ha (395 ac) in a single 45-minute flight at 120 m. Its senseFly S.O.D.A. photogrammetry camera captures sharp RGB imagery that processes into georeferenced orthomosaics, digital surface/elevation models and dense point clouds, with optional RTK for ~2.5 cm accuracy without ground control points. A rugged airframe and ultra-tough under-body skin let it work in harsh conditions, and it flies via senseFly's eMotion planning software, backed by 10+ years of eBee mapping heritage.

name: eBee VISION
desc: The AgEagle eBee VISION is a backpackable fixed-wing ISR drone delivering real-time full-motion video for situational awareness, launchable in under three minutes with a silent stealth mode. Blue UAS-cleared and NDAA-compliant, it fills the gap between short-endurance quadcopters and large military fixed-wing UAS for tactical reconnaissance.
cameras: RGB camera with 32x zoom, thermal imaging sensor

name: eBee X
desc: Professional mapping drone with RTK/PPK capabilities, BVLOS operations approved, compatible with multiple cameras including S.O.D.A. 3D, covers up to 500 ha in single flight
cameras: Compatible with S.O.D.A. 3D photogrammetry camera, RGB, and multispectral sensors

name: Percepto Sparrow (Legacy)
desc: Percepto's original autonomous drone-in-a-box - the first-generation industrial inspection drone (introduced around 2017) that launched the company's fully autonomous inspection-and-monitoring approach. It lived in a weatherproof base station, taking off on pre-programmed BVLOS missions to inspect and monitor industrial sites, carrying an HD RGB camera and a FLIR thermal imager, with data managed through Percepto's Core/AIM software. Deployed worldwide for perimeter security and asset inspection across mining, oil & gas and utilities, the Sparrow was upgraded and rebranded as the Percepto Air Max in 2021, so the 'Sparrow' name is now legacy.

name: Proscenic X1
desc: The Proscenic X1 is a robot vacuum and mop from Proscenic that autonomously navigates and cleans home floors, returning to its dock to recharge.

name: Percepto Air Mobile
desc: Compact and lightweight drone-in-a-box system weighing 4.2kg. Designed for smaller sites, linear inspections like pipelines and power lines, and temporary deployments. IP55 rating for rain operation, equipped with emergency parachute. Base station measures 100x100x75cm for easy mobility.

name: Percepto Air Max OGI
desc: Percepto's autonomous industrial inspection drone in its gas-detection configuration - billed as the only drone-in-a-box with an integrated OGI (Optical Gas Imaging) camera for spotting methane and other fugitive emissions. Alongside the OGI sensor it carries a 24MP RGB camera and a radiometric (FLIR) thermal camera, with an onboard Nvidia GPU running AI in real time so leaks can be flagged during the flight rather than after. It launches from and returns to the weatherproof Percepto Base, carries an FAA-compliant parachute and autonomous failsafes (low battery, GPS loss), is tested to hurricane-5 winds, and feeds all data into the Percepto AIM platform for analytics and reporting. Deployed at scale with operators such as Chevron (Permian Basin, Colorado), it earned EPA approval (Alternative Test Method MATM-14) for federal oil-and-gas methane emissions inspections in late 2025.
cameras: Integrated OGI (Optical Gas Imaging) camera, RGB camera, thermal camera
distinction: Only drone-in-a-box with integrated OGI camera

name: Percepto Air Max
desc: Percepto's flagship autonomous inspection drone (the 2021 successor to the Sparrow), built for inspecting and mapping the most complex industrial environments where accuracy and durability matter most. Living in its weatherproof Percepto Base, it launches on fully autonomous, nationwide FAA BVLOS missions carrying a 24MP RGB camera and a radiometric thermal camera, with customizable lens configurations and optional multispectral or OGI (gas-imaging) payloads. Onboard AI processes data in real time, an FAA-compliant parachute and autonomous failsafes (low battery, GPS loss) keep it safe, and it's tested to hurricane-force-5 winds. All data flows into the Percepto AIM platform for AI-powered analytics and reporting, with API integrations into systems like IBM Maximo and SAP OSIsoft - used for pipeline monitoring, transformer and flare-stack inspection, mining, heavy industry and perimeter security.
cameras: High-resolution RGB and thermal imaging cameras with zoom capabilities

desc: The RealMan RMC-DA Dual Arm Compound Robot is a humanoid-inspired mobile manipulation platform mounting two of RealMan's 7-DoF RM75 ultra-lightweight arms (5 kg payload, 610 mm reach, ±0.05 mm repeatability, 180°/s joint speed each) on an autonomous chassis — 1,350 mm tall with a 2,070 mm maximum arm span. The 8-wheel base combines mecanum wheels, differential drive and active suspension driven by twin 250 W hub servo motors, with a sensing stack of 10 m laser-ranging LiDAR, depth camera and ultrasonic sensors feeding laser-plus-visual obstacle avoidance. Onboard compute is a Jetson-class NVIDIA module (384-core Volta GPU with 48 Tensor Cores, 6-core Carmel CPU, 8 GB) running Ubuntu, and safety layers include force sensing on the arms and a hardware e-stop. Built entirely on RealMan's in-house controllers, drivers, motors and harmonic reducers, the RMC-DA targets bimanual research, embodied-AI training, education and service-automation demonstrations.

desc: The Flexiv Moonlight is the world's first force-controlled parallel robot — a 3-DoF delta platform that fuses Flexiv's adaptive force sensing and control with the speed of a parallel kinematic structure. Working across a Ø1,200 mm × 400 mm envelope at 1.5 m/s TCP speed and 15 m/s² acceleration with ±0.05 mm ISO 9283 repeatability, it brings compliant, force-guided behaviour to a robot class traditionally limited to rigid position control — enabling adaptive loading/unloading and delicate high-speed handling with superior vibration rejection. The 38 kg, IP65-rated unit mounts horizontally, vertically or at any angle from a Ø206 mm base, and its hollow ISO 9409-1-50-4-M6 flange routes tooling and vision cabling internally. It shares Flexiv's ecosystem: the Hesper controller, Flexiv Elements visual programming, jogging/floating teach modes, the C++/Python RDK, and CE & ETL certification for safe human-robot interaction.

name: Grav
desc: The Flexiv Grav is a force-controlled robotic gripper announced in February 2023 and shipping from Q2 2023, bringing the same industrial-grade force control as Flexiv's Rizon adaptive arms to the end effector. Its composite sensor module senses resistive forces in the sub-gram region, letting it hold a constant, precisely modulated grip on delicate or fragile objects at speed, while a gecko-foot-inspired adhesive material adds contigutive grasping for oddly shaped or uneven-surfaced items — including spheres that defeat conventional parallel grippers. Rated IP67 against dust and water immersion, meeting or exceeding ISO/TS 15066 collaborative safety standards, and rated for tens of millions of open/close cycles, it attaches plug-and-play to Flexiv's universal end-of-arm socket with no coding required, and was adapted for standard cobots after customer demand. Control runs through Flexiv Elements primitives, a dedicated Grav UI, or Modbus RTU Official specs: 50 mm stroke per jaw, 1–100 N optimal gripping force with 1 N force-control accuracy, 1–200 mm/s gripping speed, 0.1 mm finger position repeatability, 202×159×84 mm at 0.9 kg, −20 to +45 °C operating range, ISO 9409-1-50-4-M6 mechanical interface.

desc: The Flexiv Rizon 4s is the high-sensitivity variant of the Rizon 4 adaptive robot, adding a 6-DoF flange-mounted force/torque sensor on top of the series' torque sensing in all seven joints. The result is 0.03 N force sensing accuracy — sensitivity Flexiv describes as surpassing human touch — enabling multi-contact force control for delicate work like FPC/FFC insertion and micro-component placement where end-effector feedback is critical. It keeps the 4 kg payload while extending reach to 919 mm (21 kg mass, ±0.05 mm ISO 9283 repeatability, 150 N max TCP force), retains IP65 protection with any-angle or AMR/AGV mounting, and shares the series' ISO 13849 PL=d dual-channel safety architecture with CE & ETL certification. Control runs through the Hesper controller with Flexiv Elements visual programming, hand-guided teaching, and the C++/Python RDK, with official ROS bridges available.

name: JAKA MiniCobo
desc: The JAKA MiniCobo, launched in mid-2021, is JAKA Robotics' smallest collaborative robot — a rounded, cable-free 6-axis arm weighing 9.4 kg with a 1 kg payload and 580 mm reach, designed for settings where appearance and quiet operation matter as much as capability. Its built-in communication port removes external tool cabling, and intelligent control algorithms plus near-silent running suit it to customer-facing work: robotic coffee and beverage stations, retail, education, hospitality and entertainment. It runs from a 24 VDC supply through the tiny MiniCab controller (180×128×47 mm), draws a typical 150 W, and mounts on panels, guide rails or at any angle from a 124 mm footprint. Teaching follows the standard JAKA pendant-free model — free-drive drag teaching and graphical programming over Wi-Fi from a phone or PC — with collision detection for fenceless ISO 10218-1 collaboration. A Mini 2 sibling doubles payload to 2 kg on a 48 VDC supply. Repeatability is ±0.1 mm, ample for its service-sector brief.

It anchors the top of AUBO's i-Series 6-axis line and leans on the company's open-integration philosophy: an open SDK supporting C, C++, C#, Lua and Python, open communication protocols spanning TCP/IP, Modbus, EtherNet/IP and PROFINET, and Linux/Windows/ROS support, so integrators aren't locked into a proprietary stack. Collision detection and hand-guiding enable fenceless collaboration to EN ISO 13849-1 / ISO 10218-1, and the huge working envelope suits palletizing to full pallet height and tending machinery a smaller cobot would need a rail to reach.

name: TX2-60
desc: The Stäubli TX2-60 is a compact, exceptionally fast 6-axis industrial robot from the Swiss precision-engineering firm — 4.5 kg payload across 670 mm reach at ±0.02 mm repeatability, with blistering joint speeds (up to 1,445°/s on axis 6) delivering an 8.4 m/s tool-centre speed that makes it one of the quickest arms in its class. Its defining trait is a fully encapsulated design built on Stäubli's patented JCS hollow-shaft smart gearbox with all cabling internal — no external cables to snag or contaminate — rated IP65/IP67 and available in an unusually broad set of sensitive-environment versions: cleanroom (ISO Class 5, down to Class 2 supercleanroom), ESD, humid, food-hygienic H1, and pharma grades (Stericlean+). Though catalogued as an industrial robot, the TX2 arm with its CS9 controller offers TÜV-certified SIL3/PL e modular safety functions (Safe Speed, Safe Tool, Safe Stop, Safe Zone) with SIL3 absolute encoders, enabling safe human-robot collaboration. It needs no battery in arm or controller (lower maintenance, no position recovery), the CS9 recuperates energy on every deceleration, and it programs in Stäubli's VAL 3 with real-time Ethernet fieldbuses. A long-reach TX2-60L (920 mm, 3.7 kg) completes the range.

Each KMP600 vehicle — developed jointly by Swisslog and KUKA — lifts and carries mobile racks up to 600 kg at a product mass of 209 kg, coordinated as a fleet by Swisslog's SynQ software with pick-by-light and pick-pointer guidance at the workstations to cut error rates. The standard racks customise to different article sizes and shapes (notably hanging garments for fashion), and the system needs only modest warehouse building requirements, letting operators react quickly to changing product ranges. desc: The Galbot G1 is the flagship wheeled semi-humanoid from Beijing's Galaxy General Robot (Galbot), first shown March 2025 — a human-scale upper body with two highly dexterous arms on a 360° omnidirectional wheeled base. At 1,730 mm and 85 kg with 47 total DOF (including 12-DOF dexterous hands) and a 1,900 mm arm span extended by a torso lift to a 2,400 mm reach, it deliberately trades bipedal terrain versatility for stability, reliability and endurance — roughly 10 hours of runtime versus the typical 2-4 hours for bipeds, since energy goes to manipulation and compute rather than constant balance. It's driven by Galbot's proprietary AstraBrain 'brain-cerebellum-neural control' AI for full-body and full-hand coordination, achieving a 95-97% grasping success rate across diverse materials. The G1 became nationally famous performing fully autonomous tasks — rolling walnuts in its palm, picking up glass fragments — on the 2026 CCTV Spring Festival Gala before ~679 million viewers. It's aimed squarely at commercial deployment: retail, warehouses, hospital corridors and factory floors. name: Clone Alpha Android
desc: Clone Alpha is a musculoskeletal android for the home from Clone Robotics, a startup operating out of the US (Bay Area) and Poland. Instead of conventional electric actuators, it is animated by Clone's proprietary 'Myofiber' artificial muscles — synthetic musculotendon units, water/hydraulically powered, attached to anatomically correct points on a polymer skeleton modelled on all 206 human bones. Each ~3 g fibre responds in under 50 ms, contracts over 30% and produces ~1 kg of force, with the full android using more than 1,000 fibres for fluid, human-like motion. An NVIDIA Jetson Thor processes a suite of depth cameras under Clone's 'Cybernet' foundation model (language, vision and motor control), with skills taught via its 'Telekinesis' training platform — pre-loaded abilities include memorising home layouts, folding laundry, vacuuming, pouring drinks and making sandwiches. Clone is releasing a limited first run of 279 units in its Alpha Edition; pricing is unannounced (likened to a 'limited-edition supercar') and many hardware specs remain unpublished as it is a development-stage platform.

name: Protoclone V1
desc: Protoclone V1, from Clone Robotics (Warsaw), is the viral research prototype behind the company's musculoskeletal approach — described by Clone as the world's first bipedal musculoskeletal android. It reproduces human skeletal, muscular, vascular and nervous systems with synthetic components: a biomimetic skeleton of 206 bones moved by around 1,000 water/pneumatically-actuated 'Myofiber' artificial muscles attached to precise bone points like tendons, with over 200 degrees of freedom and roughly 500 sensors (4 depth cameras, 70 inertial sensors, 320 pressure sensors). A 40-second early-2025 video of it suspended in a workshop, limbs twitching and flexing behind a reflective black mask, drew millions of views. The prototype currently uses pneumatics and is transitioning to hydraulics. IMPORTANT REALITY-FLAG: Protoclone cannot yet stand or walk on its own — it's an architecture demonstrator, not a functional walking robot; DOF and component counts are company claims. Conceptually comparable to the University of Tokyo JSK Lab's musculoskeletal Kengoro (2017), though Clone targets commercial use. Recorded as verified-manufacturer-claim with honest capability limits.

name: HUBO-2 Plus
desc: HUBO-2 Plus, from Rainbow Robotics, is the mass-produced commercial version of KAIST's HUBO-2 (KHR-4) — notable as the world's first commercialized full-size humanoid robot platform. Standing 1,250 mm and 45 kg with 40 DOF (3-DOF neck, dual 7-DOF arms, dual 5-DOF hands, 1-DOF torso, dual 6-DOF legs), it upgraded the original HUBO with 40 Maxon brushless DC motors and harmonic-drive reducers on an aluminium endoskeleton with polycarbonate frame, running real-time control on two PC/104 computers (dual Pentium III, Windows XP with Ardence RTX). It can walk, run and dance, imitate human sign language with five independently-moving fingers, and recognise faces/objects via two CCD head cameras. By 2012 Rainbow had produced 15 units — four for domestic Korean teams and eleven exported to research groups in the United States, Japan, Singapore and China — cementing HUBO as a global research platform. Its lineage led to the DARPA-winning DRC-HUBO+ and the rideable FX-2. Rainbow Robotics was later acquired by Samsung Electronics (2025). NOTE: full specs from Rainbow/KAIST + IEEE + Wikipedia — verified; commercial sibling of the HUBO-2 research entry.

Built by the KAIST-founded, publicly traded (KRX: 277810) company behind the DARPA-Challenge-winning HUBO humanoid, it reuses proven RB-cobot and AMR core components — BLDC/DC motors with harmonic-drive reducers — to deliver industrial-grade reliability rather than prototype fragility, with sub-millimetre repeatability and 3 kg payload per arm. The wheeled base travels at up to 2.5 m/s with high-speed turning and sudden acceleration stabilised by continuous centre-of-gravity control. Standing 1,400 mm tall on a 600×690 mm footprint at 131 kg, powered by a 50 V/25 Ah battery, it targets the embodied-AI era: programmed by master-slave demonstration (linking a data arm as master) with self-collision prevention, real-time teleoperation, LiDAR navigation and a simulation environment for AI learning. Rainbow positions it as a bridge between fixed cobots and full humanoids.

name: HUBO-2 (KHR-4)
desc: HUBO-2 (KHR-4, also 'Jaemi HUBO'), developed 2008-2009 by Professor Jun-Ho Oh's HUBO Lab at KAIST in South Korea, is a landmark full-size humanoid — one of the first advanced full-body humanoids developed outside Japan. At 1,250 mm and 45 kg with 40 DOF (3-DOF neck, dual 7-DOF arms, dual 5-DOF hands, 1-DOF torso, dual 6-DOF legs), it introduced a distinctive straight-leg walking gait that improved on the bent-knee posture most bipeds use to balance, consuming less energy and looking more natural. It's driven by 40 brushless DC motors with harmonic-drive reducers on an aluminium endoskeleton with polycarbonate frame, runs real-time control on Windows XP with the RTX extension across two PC/104 computers, and carries cameras plus 3-axis force/torque and inertial sensors. HUBO-2 could walk, run, dance and grasp for about two hours per charge, and its lineage led directly to DRC-HUBO+, which won the 2015 DARPA Robotics Challenge. Prof. Oh co-founded Rainbow Robotics in 2011 to commercialise the HUBO platform. NOTE: full DOF breakdown and specs from KAIST/IEEE Spectrum records; historic entry, verified figures.

name: RoboThespian
desc: The pioneering 'robot actor' from England's Engineered Arts (founded 2004), first built in 2005 and now installed at 250+ venues worldwide including NASA Kennedy Space Center and museums. RoboThespian is a life-size (1.75 m, 33 kg) interactive humanoid designed for public display: an aluminium chassis and PET body shell house an actuated upper body, arms, hands, head and jaw driven by Festo pneumatic actuators plus brushed DC motors across 26 DoF (30+ axes). LCD-screen eyes, RGB cheeks and a synchronised jaw bring expression; it speaks 30+ languages with 90 TTS voices, and runs Engineered Arts' Tritium software (Gentoo/Ubuntu) with scripted, API and TinMan telepresence control. It performed in the stage play 'Spillikin' and hosted the 2015 NatGeo film Robots 3D.

name: Ameca
desc: Ameca, from UK firm Engineered Arts (Falmouth, Cornwall), is widely regarded as the world's most expressive humanoid robot — the grey-skinned, deliberately gender- and race-neutral face that went viral for its unsettlingly lifelike expressions. First shown at CES 2022 (project began Feb 2021, Generation 3 launched at ICRA 2025 alongside the 'Ami' companion), it stands 1,870 mm at 62 kg and is built on Engineered Arts' proprietary Mesmer actuator technology for smooth, precise facial and upper-body articulation. Crucially it is a static interaction platform — no functional locomotion; it stands on a weighted base or stage mount — designed for public engagement, hospitality, museums and human-robot-interaction research. It's modular (head, arms and torso sold separately/upgradeable) and cloud-connected, running the Tritium OS with integration to AI systems including OpenAI's GPT models and human telepresence/avatar control, programmable in Python, C++ and block-based code. IMPORTANT: Engineered Arts deliberately does NOT publish payload, grip force, joint torque, or LiDAR/depth/IMU/tactile sensor specs — those fields are flagged as unpublished rather than estimated. Height/weight are from the official page (187 cm / 62 kg).

name: Type-X RCV
desc: Milrem's Type-X is a 12-tonne tracked robotic combat vehicle (RCV) that can mount up to a 50 mm autocannon plus a 7.62 mm machine gun, with STANAG 4569 Level 4 armour. Hybrid-electric and capable of 80 km/h, it is designed to fight alongside crewed armour as an expendable wingman carrying ~4.1 tonnes of payload.
cameras: Multiple electro-optical and thermal imaging cameras

name: THeMIS Support
desc: The THeMIS Support configuration adapts Milrem's tracked UGV for combat-support roles - mounting remote weapon stations, ISR sensors or mission payloads on the modular 1,200 kg platform to extend infantry capability while keeping soldiers at a safer standoff.
cameras: Multiple day/night cameras with thermal imaging

name: THeMIS Cargo
desc: The THeMIS Cargo is the logistics/CASEVAC configuration of Milrem's tracked UGV, carrying supplies, ammunition or wounded personnel up to 1,200 kg. A THeMIS in this role was the first UGV in service with the Ukrainian Armed Forces, deployed from August 2022.
cameras: Multiple cameras for navigation and situational awareness

name: ARCOS

name: MRCV

name: VECTOR RCV
desc: The Vector is the tracked counterpart to Milrem's HAVOC RCV, in development to share the company's unified autonomy ecosystem and hybrid-electric driveline while offering tracked mobility better suited to soft or northern-European terrain. (Concept/development stage - specifications to be confirmed.)
cameras: Multiple electro-optical cameras and thermal imaging systems

name: HAVOC 8x8 RCV
desc: Milrem's HAVOC is an 8x8 wheeled robotic combat vehicle (unveiled 2025) weighing ~15 tonnes with a 5-tonne payload. Its hybrid-electric driveline (near-silent, instant torque) delivers 110 km/h on road and 600 km range, with AI-driven navigation and electronic-warfare resilience, designed to support armoured formations and mount weapons up to 30 mm.
cameras: Multi-spectral sensor suite with thermal and night vision capabilities

name: THeMIS
desc: Milrem's THeMIS (Tracked Hybrid Modular Infantry System) is the world's most widely fielded tracked UGV - part of robotic programmes in 19 countries. A 1.63-tonne hybrid-electric platform carrying up to 1,200 kg, it supports infantry across Logistics, Combat, ISR and EOD configurations, climbs 60% slopes and has been combat-proven in Ukraine since 2022.

name: Multiscope
desc: MultiScope is a THeMIS-based multi-mission family from Milrem, configurable for tasks such as route clearance/demining, ISR and logistics by swapping mission modules onto the tracked 1,200 kg platform.
cameras: Multiple camera systems for navigation and surveillance

name: Carbon ATK (AutoTractor Kit)
desc: Retrofittable autonomy kit that transforms conventional tractors into driverless machines, monitored 24/7 in real time by trained Carbon Robotics operators at the Remote Operations Control Center (ROCC). Initially compatible with John Deere 6R and 8R Series tractors, installable in under 24 hours without permanent modifications. Performs LaserWeeder operations plus ground prep (tilling, plowing, cultivating, ripping, discing, listing, mulching, mowing). Pay-per-hour pricing model with no upfront purchase. Originally launched as 'Carbon AutoTractor', rebranded to 'Carbon ATK' in late 2025.
autonomy_level: Full autonomy with remote human supervision
remote_supervision_detail: 24/7 monitoring at Remote Operations Control Center (ROCC), Richland WA. Operators can take over remotely for obstacles (debris, wildlife, irrigation pipes)

name: LaserWeeder G2 1800
desc: Largest LaserWeeder G2 model at 60 ft (18.3 m) wide, weighing 14,000 lbs (6,350 kg). Built for large-scale organic corn and soybean operations on farms standardized on 60-foot-wide farming equipment (common in the US Midwest). Same Carbon AI + 240W diode laser technology as the rest of the G2 family but at maximum throughput — 5-10 acres per hour of weed control without herbicides, mechanical cultivation, or soil disturbance.

name: LaserWeeder G2 1200
desc: First broadacre laser weeding solution from Carbon Robotics, specifically designed for organic corn and soybean operations. At 40 ft (12.2 m) wide and 12,000 lbs (5,443 kg) with 48x 240W diode lasers and corresponding camera/LED arrays, it's the first weed control system that doesn't disturb crops or soil — a key advantage in row crop farming where mechanical cultivation damages plants and tillage disrupts soil health. Particularly impactful for organic corn/soy producers.
use_cases: Row crop weed control without tillage

name: LaserWeeder G2 600
desc: Flagship LaserWeeder G2 model — the next generation of Carbon Robotics' industry-leading 20-foot laser weeder. 25% lighter than the original LaserWeeder (Gen 1) at 7,200 lbs / 3,266 kg with 24x 240W diode lasers, 36 cameras, and 240 LED bedtop lights. Twice the throughput of Gen 1, sub-millimeter accuracy, and 99% weed kill rate. Designed for the wide range of specialty vegetable and herb crops where Carbon Robotics has its largest installed customer base.

name: LaserWeeder G2 400
desc: Mid-sized LaserWeeder G2 model designed for diverse crop types and field layouts. At 13.3 ft (4.0 m) wide with 16x 240W diode lasers, 24 cameras, and 160 LED bedtop lights, it's the versatile workhorse of the G2 line. Sub-millimeter weed targeting accuracy with 5,000+ weeds shot per minute and up to 99% kill rate. Pairs with mid-size row crop tractors.

name: LaserWeeder G2 300
desc: Six-module LaserWeeder G2 variant configured for diverse global field layouts and wheel spacings. Uses 12x 240W diode lasers, 18 cameras, and 120 LED bedtop lights. Covers 0.75–1.50 ac/hr (0.30–0.61 ha/hr) with up to 5,000 weeds shot per minute and sub-millimeter accuracy. Designed for specialty crops on farms with non-standard track widths or row spacing.

name: LaserWeeder G2 200
desc: Smallest, lightest unit in the LaserWeeder G2 modular product line. At 6.6 ft (2.0 m) wide and 4,250 lbs (1,928 kg), it's designed for small specialty crop farms and easy transport between fields. Uses 8x 240W diode lasers (upgraded from 150W in Gen 1) for faster shoot times, plus dual NVIDIA GPUs and high-resolution cameras for sub-millimeter weed targeting accuracy. Twice the throughput of the original LaserWeeder per module.
camera_detail: Enhanced optics, high-resolution for sub-millimeter detection

name: Spot+Scrub AI

name: ArmMotus EMU

It delivers gravity-compensated, multi-directional movement training with haptic feedback and gamified exercises (table tennis, cooking, fishing), and supports bilateral mirror training. Award-winning (Red Dot 2022, iF 2022, IERA 2023).

name: ExoMotus X2

name: MetaMotus Galileo

Award-winning (Good Design Award, Shanghai Design 100+).

name: CycleMotus A4
desc: Fourier's CycleMotus A4 is an active-and-passive cycling trainer for upper and lower limbs with motor-assisted resistance and a touchscreen interface, used for early mobilisation and endurance training in stroke, spinal-cord-injury and Parkinson's patients.

name: AnkleMotus
desc: Fourier's AnkleMotus (M1-A) is an ankle-joint rehabilitation robot providing active and passive movement training, strength and proprioception exercises for patients recovering ankle function after stroke or injury.

name: BalanceMotus KINE-SIM

name: HandyRehab

name: ExoMotus M4

Powered by NEURA's AURA cloud AI and the Neuraverse app ecosystem (skills added like phone apps), it performs tasks such as vacuuming, unloading a dishwasher, tidying, beverage service and health monitoring for home, care and retail settings.

name: MAV
desc: Multi-Sensing Autonomous Vehicle for indoor intralogistics, built to move larger, heavier goods than conventional AMRs — up to 1.5 tonnes on four lifting units for pallets. Navigates with 360° laser scanners at ±5 mm accuracy, supports hand-gesture control via 3D vision, shows status on side LEDs, and pairs with NEURA's LARA cobot or MAiRA for mobile manipulation.

name: LARA 10
desc: The NEURA Robotics LARA 10 heads the LARA collaborative line — 10 kg payload across 1,000 mm reach while holding the family's ±0.02 mm repeatability, a precision figure that undercuts most 10 kg-class cobots. Joint torque sensors throughout drive a PL d Cat. 3 / SIL 2 safety architecture (safe position, speed, torque and I/O monitoring) for cage-free operation, and IP66 sealing suits dusty or wet industrial floors across 0–40 °C. Commissioning leans on ZeroG manual guidance, motion-path recording, flange-mounted programmable controls and a high-resolution teach pendant, with graphical programming and NEURA's pre-configured application library on top. The controller integrates over EtherNet/IP, PROFINET, Modbus TCP/RTU and RS-485 with 8 high-speed GPIO, and NEURA's in-house motors and encoders anchor the accuracy story.

desc: The NEURA Robotics LARA 5 is the mid-compact model of the LARA collaborative family, pairing a 5 kg payload with the line's signature ±0.02 mm repeatability — industrial-robot precision in a cage-free collaborative package. Like its siblings it carries joint torque sensors throughout, a PL d Cat. 3 / SIL 2 safety architecture with safe position/speed/torque monitoring, and IP66 sealing for harsh environments over 0–40 °C. NEURA's own motors and high-precision encoders underpin the accuracy claim, and the operator experience centres on graphical visual programming, ZeroG hand-guiding, path recording and a ready-to-run application library. Connectivity spans EtherNet/IP, PROFINET, Modbus TCP/RTU and RS-485 with 8 high-speed GPIO. NEURA's published English one-pager omits the LARA 5's exact reach figure — logged as a manufacturer-outreach item rather than estimated.

Its cognitive stack is the differentiator: integrated 3D vision with AI object recognition and point clouds, a 360° microphone array for 3D voice commands, a 6-DoF force/torque sensor and NEURA's 6-DoF Smart Skin giving whole-arm contact sensing and fingertip-precise hand guiding. Deployment is no-code — programs build in minutes through the graphical interface, Smart Skin teaching or voice. The controller carries EtherCAT, Modbus, CAN bus, IO-Link and GPIO plus 3× compressed-air feed-through; the IP65 body works across 0–50 °C in any mounting orientation.

Targeted at mining, search-and-rescue and rugged industrial inspection, it was recognised with a CES 2026 Innovation Award.

name: Diana 7 (by Agile Robots)
desc: The Diana 7, from Agile Robots, is a 7-axis collaborative robot arm with torque sensors in every joint, a 7 kg payload, ~923 mm reach and ~0.05 mm repeatability. Its full force/torque sensing enables compliant, contact-rich manipulation, making it a popular platform for research and precision assembly.

name: Franka Hand 3

It offers an 80 mm stroke and roughly 70 N continuous grip force, with interchangeable fingertips that adapt to different object shapes and materials, making it the default end effector for the research and assembly tasks the FR3 platform targets. As part of Franka's Apps ecosystem, gripping actions drop into visual workflows for rapid behaviour prototyping.

controller: Fully integrated into Franka arm software (plug-and-use)

name: Tactile Mobile Robot (TMR)
desc: Mobile robot base built for teleoperation, mobile manipulation and physical-AI research, natively compatible with the Franka Research 3 (FR3) arm. Pre-configured mechanical, electrical and software interfaces integrate it with FR3 Duo setups, and standardized mounting points let researchers add sensors and actuators. Supports 1 kHz control via the Franka Control Interface and is fully integrated with ROS 2.
highlights: 1 kHz control via Franka Control Interface

name: Mobile FR3 Duo
desc: The Mobile FR3 Duo pairs two 7-axis torque-sensing Franka FR3 arms on a mobile base for bimanual mobile manipulation, a research platform for compliant two-handed tasks.
cameras: Multiple RGB cameras and depth sensors integrated into mobile platform

name: CECIL (Consolidated Edison Combined Inspection and Lancing)
desc: CECIL (Consolidated Edison Combined Inspection and Lancing) is a specialized industrial robot for inspecting and lancing (cleaning) boiler tubes and confined industrial spaces, keeping workers out of hazardous maintenance environments.
cameras: Multiple inspection cameras for steam generator tube monitoring

name: Robotic Applique Kit (RAK-3)
desc: QinetiQ's Robotic Applique Kit (RAK) is a bolt-on system that converts manned military ground vehicles into optionally-manned/unmanned platforms. RAK-3 adds drive-by-wire actuation, teleoperation and waypoint autonomy so existing vehicles can be operated remotely for dull, dirty and dangerous missions such as route clearance, resupply and ISR.
cameras: Multiple day/night cameras for situational awareness

name: RCV-L (Robotic Command Vehicle - Light)
desc: QinetiQ's RCV-L (Robotic Combat Vehicle-Light), developed with Pratt Miller, is a ~3.9-tonne diesel-electric hybrid, rubber-tracked unmanned combat vehicle for the US Army's RCV programme. With a modular payload architecture carrying ~3,175 kg at over 60 km/h, it can be remotely controlled or driven semi-autonomously and is air-transportable to remote locations.
cameras: 360-degree situational awareness cameras, thermal imaging, electro-optical sensors

name: MAARS (Modular Advanced Armed Robotic System)
desc: QinetiQ's MAARS (Modular Advanced Armed Robotic System) is a tracked unmanned ground robot designed for reconnaissance, surveillance and target acquisition, able to mount a remote weapon station (such as an M240B machine gun or 40 mm grenade launcher). It lets forces apply firepower and ISR from forward positions while crews stay protected.

name: TALON V
desc: Fifth-generation TALON — a rugged, lightweight tracked robot in continuous military service since 2000, when it was first used in Bosnia for grenade disposal. TALON V was the first man-portable robot to complete the US Army's TARDEC Interoperability Profile (IOP). Configurable with more than 60 mission packages for EOD, reconnaissance, CBRNE and communications, controlled over RF or fibre-optic link. More than 4,000 TALONs operate with the US and allied forces.

name: RT-7 (ROCU)
desc: The RoboTeam RT-7 is a ground robot operated via RoboTeam's ROCU controller, applied to inspection and industrial/security tasks. (Detailed specifications worth verifying against RoboTeam.)

name: RT-20 (MTGR)
desc: RoboTeam's MTGR (Micro Tactical Ground Robot, RT-20) is a rugged ~9 kg backpackable tracked robot with high manoeuvrability indoors and out. Widely used by the IDF in urban and tunnel environments, its intuitive ROCU control and modular payloads make it a go-to for military, law-enforcement and SWAT reconnaissance.
cameras: 360° PTZ camera with day/night vision, thermal imaging

name: RT-200 (TIGR)
desc: RoboTeam's TIGR (Transportable Interoperable Ground Robot, RT-200) is a medium two-man-carried UGV with best-in-class day/night vision and a 5-DOF manipulator with 2 m reach for EOD render-safe operations, IED search and CBRN survey. Its modular design accepts advanced manipulators and EOD/CBRN payloads.
cameras: 360-degree panoramic camera system with day/night vision capabilities

name: RT-1000 (PROBOT)
desc: RoboTeam's PROBOT (RT-1000) is a lightweight heavy-payload UGV that carries up to about three times its own weight (~750 kg) across sand, water and rubble on wheels or optional tracks. Operated via the ROCU controller, it supports logistics carry, casualty evacuation, CBRN and ISR missions while keeping soldiers at standoff.
cameras: Multiple HD cameras for navigation and surveillance

name: RT-2000 (ROOK)
desc: RoboTeam's ROOK (RT-2000) is a modular tracked UGV that hosts mission payloads for logistics, ISR and EOD/route-clearance tasks. Part of RoboTeam's interoperable family controlled from the ROCU, it brings heavier payload capacity than the backpackable MTGR while keeping rapid deployability.
cameras: Day/night vision cameras with thermal imaging

name: Intelligent Power Inspection Robot
desc: An intelligent power-inspection robot (a Teledyne FLIR partner product) that autonomously patrols electrical substations and power facilities, using thermal and visual imaging to detect hot spots and faults. (Partner product; detailed specs worth verifying.)
cameras: Thermal imaging camera, visible light camera

name: Guardian DX (Dexterous)
desc: The Sarcos Guardian DX (Dexterous Robotic System) is a teleoperated, highly-dexterous dual-arm robot that combines human control with robotic strength and precision — an operator drives the robot remotely through a haptic control station, feeling force feedback as if their own hands were performing the task, while onboard AI augments and can learn from the operator's demonstrations. It targets manipulation in hazardous or hard-to-reach environments — industrial inspection and maintenance, construction, energy, aviation and defense — where human dexterity is needed but human presence is dangerous. Sarcos (which also developed the Guardian XO exoskeleton) positions it to blend teleoperation with growing autonomy. RECATEGORISATION FLAG: teleoperated dual-arm system — could sit in Industrial, but arguably Disaster Response or a Teleoperation category; flagged for Shane. OUTREACH: Sarcos publishes limited hard specs for Guardian DX (payload, reach, DOF, weight) — development-stage; specifics logged for outreach, not invented.
cameras: Multiple HD cameras for operator vision and task monitoring

ft_sensor: Force-feedback haptic teleoperation (operator feels what robot touches)
ai_model: AI + human-in-the-loop control; learns from operator demonstration (combines teleoperation with autonomy)

name: C200 RoboShuttle
desc: Bin-carrying RoboShuttle robot for high-density tote-to-person storage in narrow-aisle layouts. Lifts totes from mezzanine racking up to ~2.9 m and delivers them to picking stations. Certified 'Best of Intralogistics 2020' by the IFOY award.
cameras: Navigation cameras and QR code readers

name: P500R (P-Series)
desc: P-Series goods-to-person robot that lifts and moves racks and shelves to operators in automated warehouses. Compact body with a fast lifting response and inertial + QR-code navigation; adapts to varied floor and temperature conditions and is reported to cut manual labor by 50–70%.
cameras: Multiple cameras for navigation and positioning

name: Porter
desc: Heavy-duty pallet-moving autonomous mobile robot that extends the 6 River / Ocado Mobile Robot System beyond picking, handling cross-docking, bulk-item picking, putaway and palletized inventory moves. Works the floor alongside Chuck under Ocado IQ system-directed orchestration.
highlights: Pairs with Chuck on the floor
cameras: 3D vision system with Fork Insertion Depth System (FIDS)

name: Chuck
desc: Chuck, from 6 River Systems, is a person-to-goods autonomous mobile robot (AMR) built for e-commerce order fulfillment — it works alongside human pickers, shuttling totes and containers and intelligently guiding workers through pick paths to cut walking distance and lift productivity. It carries up to 90.7 kg, drives at up to 1.3 m/s, and measures 1067×600×1600 mm at 75 kg, using 3D SLAM for accurate localisation with 2D-plus-3D front obstacle detection and cloud-based fleet software that groups orders to maximise task density. An integrated touchscreen and globally-recognised status lighting speed operator training, and cloud updates let the fleet improve continuously without physical infrastructure changes. Co-founded by former Kiva Systems (now Amazon Robotics) executives, 6RS was acquired by Shopify and later by Ocado Group. It's CE/TÜV/UL-1740 certified and won two Red Dot design awards. RECATEGORISATION FLAG: this is an AMR, not a collaborative arm — recommend moving to an AGV/AMR or Service/Delivery category; sub updated to 'Fulfillment AMR' pending Shane's category decision.
navigation: 3D SLAM localization; cloud-based fleet software groups orders to maximise task density
safety_functions: EU Machinery Directive 2006/42/EC, UL 1740 Ed.4-2018 compliant; TÜV certified

name: Max
desc: The heavyweight LocusBot, designed for safe autonomous transport of large and heavy payloads — pallets, pallet-sized containers, cartons, totes and boxes. An industrial-strength chassis and omnidirectional mobility move up to 3,000 lb smoothly across industrial and material-handling facilities, coordinated as part of a multi-bot LocusOne fleet.
cameras: Multiple stereo cameras for navigation and obstacle detection

name: RightPick
desc: RightPick, from RightHand Robotics, is one of the world's first autonomous piece-picking systems — an AI 'brain' plus a distinctive hybrid gripper (three compliant fingers combined with suction) that together perceive, plan, grasp and learn to pick a wide SKU range with minimal human intervention. Its philosophy is hardware-agnostic: RightHand focuses on the AI software and the gripper 'hand', integrating them with industrial arms from makers like Universal Robots and FANUC, so customers keep hardware flexibility. RightPick 3 introduced a dual-GPU architecture for denser, damage-free picking and a Suction Cup Swapper for automated tool changes, with well-defined APIs, international compliance and fleet-management dashboards that make it integrator-friendly at scale (RightPick 4 is the current generation). In a warehouse it acts as the intelligent hand at the end of an AS/RS-and-conveyor flow. RECATEGORISATION FLAG: this is a picking system/gripper-plus-AI, not a standalone arm — recommend a Service/Logistics or 'Picking Systems' category; sub updated pending Shane. OUTREACH: RightHand publishes pick-rate ranges and capabilities but not a fixed spec table (system varies by integrated arm).

ft_sensor: Fine-tuned sensor suite; hand-eye coordination

name: Coco Delivery Robot v3
desc: The third-generation Coco delivery robot continues Coco Robotics' remotely-piloted urban delivery approach with incremental autonomy and sensing upgrades for dense city food delivery.

name: Coco 1
desc: Coco 1 is Coco Robotics' purpose-built last-mile delivery robot. Unlike fully autonomous competitors, Coco's pink cargo bots are remotely piloted by human operators, focusing on reliable short-range food delivery in dense urban areas such as Los Angeles.

name: Kiwibot Warehouse Robot
desc: The Kiwibot Warehouse Robot is an autonomous mobile robot adapting Kiwibot's navigation stack for indoor warehouse material transport.
cameras: Multiple RGB cameras for navigation and object detection

name: ROSA Knee with OptimiZe
desc: The Zimmer Biomet ROSA platform assists in knee and hip replacement (and, in ROSA Brain/Spine versions, neurosurgery), providing data-driven planning and intraoperative guidance for implant positioning.
cameras: Multiple intraoperative cameras for real-time surgical field visualization and bone tracking

name: OTTAVA Robotic Surgical System
desc: J&J MedTech's OTTAVA is a general-surgery soft-tissue robotic platform with four arms integrated into the operating table for a low profile and flexible setup, differentiated by deep digital integration (Polyphonic ecosystem). Aimed at procedures like cholecystectomy, hernia repair and colorectal surgery, it was in FDA IDE clinical trials rather than commercially cleared.

name: Flex360 Robotic System
desc: The Medrobotics Flex Robotic System uses a steerable, articulating flexible scope to navigate non-linear anatomical pathways the rigid instruments of other systems cannot reach, enabling minimally invasive transoral (ENT) and colorectal procedures with surgeon-guided flexible access.
cameras: High-definition endoscopic camera with articulating tip

name: Burro Verde
desc: Purpose-built Burro variant for autonomous transport to and from greenhouses. Seamlessly transitions between narrow indoor pathways and outdoor roadways using LIDAR. Can tow up to 907 kg (2,000 lb) and carry up to 227 kg (500 lb) on flat concrete. Designed as a collaborative robot for greenhouse farmworkers, replacing manual transport using tractors, gators, or golf carts.
cameras: Multiple RGB cameras for navigation and obstacle detection

name: eBee TAC Government
desc: The senseFly-branded government configuration of the eBee TAC tactical mapping drone (senseFly is now part of AgEagle). Built in Switzerland with cyber-secure encryption and silent operation for government and defense mapping and ISR missions.
cameras: RGB camera for photogrammetry and mapping

name: M330
desc: The M330 is a robot vacuum and mop from Lefant that autonomously navigates and cleans home floors, returning to its dock to recharge.

name: Yeedi Vac 2 Pro
desc: Features 3,000Pa suction, oscillating mopping system that imitates manual mopping, 3D obstacle avoidance with structured light technology, smart visual mapping & navigation, carpet detection, and optional auto-dustbin empty station compatibility.
cameras: RGB camera for visual navigation and mapping

name: yeedi C12 Plus
desc: The yeedi C12 Plus is a robot vacuum and mop from Yeedi that autonomously navigates and cleans home floors, returning to its dock to recharge.

name: Grav Enhanced
desc: The Flexiv Grav Enhanced is a two-in-one force-controlled gripper that operates in two grasping modes: a precision two-finger force-control pinch (P-mode) for small items like M1 bolts and coins, and a gecko-inspired superfriction grasp (V-mode) whose passive adhesive film lifts objects up to 5 kg — basketballs, magnums, boxes, sneakers — with minimal squeezing force and no vacuum pumps or energy input. Built on the Grav's single-driver, composite-sensor architecture with sub-gram force sensing, it can hold a water balloon without rupture yet handle mixed-SKU pallet loads, making it a genuine multi-role end effector that cuts tool-change frequency. IP67-rated, ISO/TS 15066 compliant and rated for tens of millions of cycles, it mounts plug-and-play on Flexiv's universal socket (standard cobots supported) and pairs with the automated Cleaning Station (April 2024) that restores the gecko film's grip after dusty handling. Control is via Flexiv Elements primitives, the Grav UI, or Modbus RTU Official specs: 52 mm stroke per jaw, 1 N force-control accuracy, 1–200 mm/s gripping speed, 0.1 mm finger repeatability, 1 kg unit weight (211×180×84 mm in V-mode, 211×210×84 mm in P-mode), −20 to +45 °C, ISO 9409-1-50-4-M6 interface.

name: JAKA Ai 18
desc: The JAKA Ai 18 is the heavy-payload flagship of JAKA's All-in-one collaborative series — 18 kg capacity on a 1,073 mm reach with ±0.03 mm repeatability, in a compact 35 kg body that undercuts most arms in its payload class. Like all Ai models it integrates a JAKA Lens 2D vision system (5 MP at 24 fps, 8 mm or 16 mm optics, 0.04 mm precision) controlled entirely within JAKA's own software, and runs from the MiniCab — one of the smallest control cabinets on the market — making vision-guided heavy handling deployable in tight cells or on mobile bases. The deliberately shorter reach concentrates rigidity for its 18 kg rating, aimed at dense pick & place, tending and palletizing of heavier workpieces. The collaborative toolkit is standard JAKA: wireless pendant-free drag/graphical teaching, collision detection for fenceless ISO 10218-1 operation, ISO 9409-1 flange, four industrial fieldbus protocols, 80,000-hour MTBF and any-orientation mounting.

As part of the All-in-one series designed to JAKA's S³ principle (Smart, Simple, Small), it pairs with the ultra-compact MiniCab controller for confined or mobile installations, and keeps the signature pendant-free wireless workflow: free-drive drag teaching plus graphical drag-and-drop programming from any phone, tablet or PC. Collision detection permits fenceless collaborative operation under ISO 10218-1; connectivity spans TCP/IP, Modbus TCP/RTU, PROFINET and EtherNet/IP; and the ISO 9409-1 flange takes standard grippers. At 41 kg with a 188 mm footprint and 500 W typical draw, it targets vision-guided tending, sorting and palletizing at medium payloads.

It pairs the Zu 3's mechanicals (3 kg payload, 626 mm reach, ±0.02 mm repeatability, 12 kg mass) with a built-in JAKA Lens 2D camera — 5 MP at 24 fps with selectable 8 mm or 16 mm optics resolving to 0.04 mm — whose control and configuration live entirely inside JAKA's own software, no third-party vision licence required. name: JAKA Zu 20
desc: The JAKA Zu 20 is the long-reach heavy-lifter of the Zu collaborative series — 20 kg payload across a class-leading 1,780 mm reach, with ±0.05 mm repeatability and TCP speeds up to 5 m/s, the fastest in the JAKA lineup. Its IP65-sealed body (a step above the IP54 of its smaller siblings) suits dusty or wet production environments, and at 68 kg with a 246 mm footprint it still mounts floor, wall, ceiling or at any angle. The joint architecture trades J1–J3 speed (120°/s) for torque while keeping fast 220°/s wrist axes, matching its palletizing, welding and heavy machine-tending brief. It retains the full JAKA collaborative toolkit: pendant-free wireless teaching by drag or graphical app programming, collision detection for fenceless ISO 10218-1 operation, an ISO 9409-1 flange, and the standard IP44 cabinet with 16/16 I/O and four industrial fieldbus protocols. Typical draw is 750 W; MTBF is rated at 80,000 hours.

name: JAKA Zu 5
desc: The JAKA Zu 5 is the volume workhorse of JAKA's Zu collaborative-robot family — a 5 kg-payload, 954 mm-reach 6-axis arm hitting ±0.02 mm repeatability and TCP speeds up to 3 m/s from a 23 kg body. Like all Zu cobots it is built on JAKA's unified integral joints and taught wirelessly — free-drive drag teaching plus graphical drag-and-drop programming on any phone, tablet or PC, with no teach pendant required. It runs fenceless beside operators via its collision-detection module (ISO 10218-1), mounts in any orientation on a 158 mm footprint, and is rated for cleanroom use to ISO Class 5, opening semiconductor and pharma applications. Typical consumption is 350 W through the IP44 control cabinet, which carries 16/16 digital I/O and TCP/IP, Modbus, PROFINET and EtherNet/IP. An 80,000-hour MTBF and the force-sensing Zu 5s variant round out a platform aimed squarely at machine tending, assembly and finishing work.

name: JAKA Zu 3
desc: The JAKA Zu 3 is the entry point to JAKA Robotics' flagship Zu series of collaborative robots — a 3 kg-payload, 626 mm-reach 6-axis arm weighing just 12 kg, making it one of the lightest full-function cobots in its class. Built around JAKA's integral joint modules (motor, drive and encoder unified in each joint), it delivers ±0.02 mm repeatability at TCP speeds up to 1.5 m/s while drawing a typical 150 W. Its defining trait is JAKA's wireless, pendant-free workflow: the arm is taught by physically dragging it (free-drive) or via drag-and-drop graphical programming on a phone, tablet or PC over built-in Wi-Fi. Collision detection allows fenceless operation alongside workers per ISO 10218-1. With an IP54 body, any-orientation mounting and a 129 mm footprint, the Zu 3 targets 3C electronics lines — screwdriving, small assembly and precision pick & place — with an 80,000-hour MTBF and a Zu 3s variant adding an integrated force/torque sensor.

name: LARA 8
desc: The NEURA Robotics LARA 8 slots between the LARA 5 and LARA 10 with an 8 kg payload at the family's ±0.02 mm repeatability, targeting machine tending and handling work that outgrows 5 kg-class arms. It shares the LARA platform end to end: torque sensors in all six joints, PL d Cat. 3 / SIL 2 integrated safety with safe position/speed/torque monitoring for fenceless collaboration, IP66 protection across 0–40 °C, NEURA in-house motors with high-precision encoders, ZeroG hand-guided teaching, graphical programming with pre-built application packages, and a controller speaking EtherNet/IP, PROFINET, Modbus TCP/RTU and RS-485 with 8 high-speed GPIO. The exact reach figure for the LARA 8 isn't in NEURA's published English materials — flagged for manufacturer outreach.

name: R1
desc: The Unitree R1 is billed as the most affordable capable humanoid ever from a major manufacturer, unveiled in July 2025 from about US$4,900 (R1 Air) / $5,900 (standard) — a fraction of the company's $16,000 G1. The child-sized 1.23 m, ~25 kg robot packs 26 joint modules (6 per leg, 5 per arm, 2 waist, 2 head) driven by low-inertia permanent-magnet synchronous motors, giving it striking agility: it runs, cartwheels, does handstands and spin-kicks and recovers from falls autonomously. A backpack compute module runs Unitree's UnifoLM multimodal large language model on-device for voice and image interaction, with a Linux SDK and ROS 2 interfaces on the EDU variant. A quick-release battery gives roughly one hour of mixed activity. Named a TIME Best Invention of 2025, the R1 began phased global deliveries in April 2026, including a landmark retail launch on AliExpress.

name: Zenmuse L2
desc: DJI Enterprise's integrated aerial LiDAR mapping payload, combining a frame LiDAR, a self-developed high-accuracy IMU, a 20MP 4/3 CMOS RGB mapping camera and a 3-axis gimbal for precise true-colour point clouds. It detects out to 250 m (10% reflectivity, bright light) or 450 m (50% reflectivity, low light), with a 500 m maximum, from a recommended 30-150 m altitude, and delivers 5 cm horizontal / 4 cm vertical accuracy at 150 m. It fires up to 240,000 points/s single-return (1,200,000 with multiple returns), supports up to five returns for canopy penetration, and cuts the laser spot to about one-fifth of the L1's for finer detail. A single flight covers up to 2.5 km2; the ~905 g, IP54-rated unit mounts on the DJI Matrice 300/350/400 RTK and pairs with DJI Terra for turnkey point-cloud post-processing. Around $15,700, used for land surveying, power-line modeling, forestry and infrastructure inspection.
