name: Zenmuse P1
desc: DJI Enterprise's benchmark aerial-surveying payload, pairing a 45MP full-frame sensor (35.9x24mm, 4.4um pixels, 8192x5460 stills) with interchangeable DL-mount fixed lenses (24, 35 and 50mm F2.8) on a 3-axis stabilized gimbal. A global mechanical shutter (1/2000s) plus TimeSync 2.0 microsecond synchronization across camera, RTK, flight controller and gimbal let it hit 3 cm horizontal / 5 cm vertical accuracy without ground control points. It captures a photo every 0.7 s and covers up to 3 km2 per flight (7.5 km2 in a workday using Smart Oblique Capture, where the gimbal auto-rotates to grab only the angles reconstruction needs). The ~800 g unit mounts on the DJI Matrice 300/350/400 RTK and pairs with DJI Pilot 2 and DJI Terra for topographic mapping, cadastral survey, AEC and disaster-site modeling.

name: Zenmuse H30 Series
desc: DJI Enterprise's flagship all-weather, multi-sensor gimbal payload (released May 2024), sold in two models: the H30 with four modules and the H30T which adds an infrared thermal camera for five. Together the modules cover a 48MP 1/1.3in wide-angle camera (24mm, 82.1-degree DFOV), a 40MP 1/1.8in zoom camera (34x optical / 400x digital), the H30T's 1280x1024 radiometric thermal camera (measuring -20 to 1600C), a laser rangefinder good to 3-3000m, and an NIR auxiliary light for night work. It shoots 4K/30fps, weighs ~920g, is IP54-rated, and adds Night Scene mode, UHR infrared, electronic dehazing, foreground stabilization, pre-recording, Click-to-Aim and AES-256 encryption. It mounts on the DJI Matrice 300, 350 and 400 RTK aircraft and integrates with DJI Pilot 2 and FlightHub 2 - a big step up from the H20 series - for public safety, powerline/energy inspection, search-and-rescue, forestry and firefighting.

name: Zenmuse L3
desc: DJI Enterprise's first long-range, high-accuracy aerial LiDAR system (released November 2025), a major step up from the L2. Its self-developed 1535nm LiDAR reaches 950 m even on 10%-reflectivity targets while keeping strong penetration, with 5 mm ranging repeatability at 150 m and microsecond time synchronization. Improved vertical accuracy (3 cm at 120 m, 5 cm at 300 m, 10 cm at 500 m) supports 1:500, 1:1000 and 1:2000 mapping scales, and a 0.25 mrad beam divergence shrinks the laser spot to about one-fifth of the L2's to resolve fine objects like power lines and branches. Dual 100MP 4/3 CMOS RGB cameras with a mechanical shutter and up to 107-degree horizontal FOV deliver 3 cm GSD even at 300 m. Mounted on the Matrice 400 it covers up to 10 km2 per flight (100 km2 a day), capturing LiDAR and RGB together to generate DOM, DEM and more from a single flight, and integrates with the D-RTK 3 station, DJI Terra, DJI Modify and FlightHub 2.

name: MenteeBot (Base Model)
desc: MenteeBot, from Israeli firm Mentee Robotics (founded 2022 by AI, computer-vision and machine-learning experts), is an AI-first, vertically integrated humanoid designed for both household and industrial use. The base model stands 175 cm at 70 kg with a 25 kg payload and moves at 1.5 m/s, running on dual NVIDIA Jetson Orin AGX processors with 360° fisheye vision, depth sensors, a 9-axis IMU and motor-driven tactile sensors in the arms. Its differentiator is AI across every layer: a novel Real2Sim2Real / Sim2Real machine-learning approach trains locomotion and tasks extensively in simulation before adapting to reality with minimal real-world data, paired with vision-language-action models, real-time 3D mapping and natural-language task planning for autonomous execution from heavy lifting to household chores. The company was reported to be acquired by Mobileye for ~$900M. It takes off in under 60 seconds, flies up to 31 minutes on hot-swappable batteries (~45-minute charge, so three sets keep it flying continuously), and has radar-based front collision avoidance (to 30 m) plus ground detection and return-to-home. The IP54-rated, backpack-portable aircraft and its 1000-nit IP54 controller store imagery only on an onboard microSD card with no cloud connection or online profile, protecting the data chain of custody. It was designed and built with Coretronic (CIRC) in Taiwan with payload integration and QC in the USA, and targets industrial/utility inspection, firefighting, law enforcement and search & rescue.

note: Most deployment-proven industrial humanoid; Walker series orders >¥800M (~$112M) by late 2025

name: Alpha 1E
desc: UBTECH's Alpha 1E (2018) is a 39 cm desktop educational humanoid with 16 servo joints, programmable for walking, dancing and choreographed routines via app or visual coding - an affordable platform for teaching robotics and programming.
os: ROSA 2.0 (UBTECH Robot OS Architecture, ROS 2 integration)
use_cases_note: STEM education, dance/motion programming

name: IRON
desc: XPENG's IRON (Next-Gen, 2025) is a lifelike bipedal humanoid with a human-like flexible spine, full-body touch-sensing soft skin, up to 82 degrees of freedom (22 per hand) and three proprietary Turing AI chips (~2,250 TOPS) running XPENG's Physical World model. Built with solid-state batteries, XPENG targets mass production for retail, guidance and inspection roles.
ai_model: Physical-AI foundation model (VLT + VLA + VLM); Tianji AIOS
frame_material: Bionic bone-muscle-skin with soft outer skin (tactile-sensing)
manufacturer_history: Unveiled at XPENG's 2025 AI Day; skin cut on-stage to prove no human inside. Mass production targeted late 2026.

name: K2
desc: Kepler's Forerunner K2 (Shanghai Kepler, 2024) is a full-size industrial humanoid - 178 cm, 85 kg, 52 DOF with 100 TOPS of compute and a 2.33 kWh battery good for an ~8-hour shift. Its tactile hands (96 fingertip sensors) handle ~15 kg per hand / 30 kg dual-arm, and a cloud cognitive model plus imitation/reinforcement learning drive autonomous task completion. Marketed as the company's fifth-generation design, also branded 'Bumblebee'/'Hornet'.
use_cases_note: Factory/manufacturing 'volume play' — orderable today (vs unavailable Western flagships)
note: Positioned alongside UBTECH Walker S2 as the order-now industrial option

name: 4NE-1
desc: NEURA Robotics’ flagship cognitive humanoid and Europe’s first humanoid designed for series production. Standing 180 cm and 80 kg, the Gen 3.5 lifts up to 100 kg — the highest among general-purpose humanoids — via ~490 N·m leg joints. Co-designed with Studio F.A. Porsche, powered by NVIDIA Thor T5000 and Isaac GR00T, with full-body artificial skin for safe human collaboration. Premiered at Automatica 2025; Gen 3.5 from €98,000.
funding: Up to $1.4B raised led by Tether (Jun 2026, ~$7B valuation) — Europe's biggest humanoid bet
note: Reservation system + published pricing on neura-robotics.com; Europe's flagship humanoid program

name: MiPa Gen 3
desc: NEURA Robotics' MiPA Gen 3 (2026) is the latest generation of the cognitive household/service mobile-manipulator, demonstrated at CES 2026 unloading dishwashers and monitoring vital signs. Powered by AURA AI and the Neuraverse app ecosystem, with global reservations open.

name: Sophia
desc: Sophia, from Hanson Robotics (David Hanson), unveiled in 2016, is the world's most famous social humanoid robot — the machine that became a global icon of AI and, in 2017, the first robot granted honorary citizenship (by Saudi Arabia). At 1,670 mm and 20 kg with 83 DOF (36 in head/neck, 15 per arm/hand, 3 torso, 14 in a mobile base), her expressive face is built from Hanson's patented Frubber actuated skin over 30+ head motors, producing 60+ lifelike facial expressions. She perceives via Intel RealSense eye cameras and a 1080p chest camera for face detection and body tracking, with microphones, audio-localization arrays, arm force sensors, finger touch sensors and an IMU, running on an Intel Core i7 (32 GB RAM, Ubuntu Linux). Her intelligence blends the Hanson AI SDK with OpenCog for general reasoning, decision-tree dialogue and deep-neural-net-driven expressions, with CereProc text-to-speech that even lets her sing. Designed for research, education, entertainment and public discussion of AI ethics, Sophia spawned a family including Little Sophia (STEM education), Albert HUBO, BINA48 and Han. NOTE: full technical breakdown cross-verified from Hanson + IEEE Spectrum + databases — museum-grade for a social humanoid.
shell_material: Frubber (patented actuated skin) + carbon fiber, CNC aluminum, steel, Delrin, polycarbonate, 3D-printed
actuator_type: Dynamixel XM430/MX64/MX106 + Xpert + Hitec HS-65MG servos (30+ motors in head)
vision: Intel RealSense (eyes) + 1080p chest cam — face detection, body tracking
ai_model: Hanson AI SDK + OpenCog (general reasoning); decision-tree dialogue; deep neural nets for expressions
capabilities: World's most famous social humanoid: 60+ lifelike Frubber expressions, NLP dialogue, face/emotion recognition, visual tracking, singing; first robot granted citizenship (Saudi Arabia 2017)
developed_by: Hanson Robotics (David Hanson)

name: TIAGo
desc: PAL Robotics' TIAGo (2018) is a mobile manipulator on a differential-drive base with a liftable torso and a 7-DOF arm - a modular, ROS-based research platform for service robotics, mobile manipulation and assistive applications rather than a bipedal humanoid.

name: TALOS
desc: PAL Robotics' TALOS (2017) is a 175 cm, 95 kg fully electric, torque-controlled humanoid built for research and industrial manipulation. With 32 DOF and EtherCAT torque-sensing joints, it can lift 6 kg per arm and serves as a high-end ROS research platform.
sensors: Force/torque per joint + IMU + stereo vision
use_cases_note: High-performance bipedal research (universities/labs across EU)

name: CyberOne
desc: Xiaomi's CyberOne (2022) is a 177 cm, 52 kg full-size bipedal humanoid with 21 DOF, emotion recognition and Xiaomi's self-developed actuators. Unveiled as a technology demonstrator showcasing Xiaomi's move into humanoid robotics.

name: STAR1
desc: RobotEra's STAR1 (2024) is a 171 cm, 55-DOF bipedal humanoid that set a world record for bipedal running at 3.6 m/s outdoors, with joints up to 400 N.m torque and direct-drive 12-DOF hands. Paired with RobotEra's ERA-42 AI model, it executes high-precision commercial tasks.
speed: 3.6 m/s — world record at the time (Gobi Desert run, in sneakers, Oct 2024)
ai_model: ERA-42 (100+ precision operations from minimal data)
note: CORRECTION for spec sheets: STAR1 (3.6 m/s) and L7 (4 m/s) records are DIFFERENT robots/gaits — often conflated

name: L7
price: POA (circulating $50k–120k figures are guesses — no published price)
desc: RobotEra's L7 (2025) is a next-generation full-size humanoid from the Chinese maker of the record-setting STAR1, advancing locomotion and whole-body manipulation. (Recent release - detailed specifications still being confirmed.)
hands: XHAND1 — 12 active DoF, fully direct-drive, five-finger
ai_model: ERA-42 end-to-end VLA (vision-language-action); 'group intelligence' multi-robot coordination
deployments: Thousands-of-units scale into 10+ logistics centers with China Post + SF Express
funding: SF Group-led ~¥2B round (May 2026); orders claimed from 9 of world's 10 largest tech firms; 200+ shipped 2025
note: Sister M7 = fixed-base upper-body variant

name: S1
desc: Astribot's S1 (Stardust Intelligence, 2024) is a wheeled-base bimanual humanoid with 36 DOF (7 per arm) and exceptional manipulation speed, trained via imitation learning to cook, clean, pour drinks and play instruments. Launched at the World Robot Conference, it targets home, lab and hospitality tasks.

name: EM02
desc: EngineAI's EM-02 (Shenzhen, 2024) is an agile humanoid robot notable for dynamic motions including a demonstrated front flip, part of the wave of Chinese humanoid developers pushing athletic locomotion. (Detailed specifications worth verifying against EngineAI.)
note: Earlier EngineAI full-size platform (pre-SE01); per-model specs not published — verified platform only

name: DR01
desc: DEEP Robotics' DR01 (2024) is an agile quadruped from the Hangzhou-based maker of the Lite3 and X-series inspection robots, built for dynamic, high-speed legged locomotion and research. (Some detailed specifications for this record are limited and worth verifying against DEEP Robotics.)

name: N1
desc: Noetix Robotics' N1 (2024) is a humanoid from the Chinese maker known for aggressively low-priced humanoids, aimed at research, education and developers entering the field. (Detailed specifications worth verifying against Noetix.)
manufacturer_history: First-generation Noetix short humanoid, unveiled at WAIC 2024; predecessor to the N2.
note: Debuted WAIC 2024

name: Promobot V4
desc: Promobot V.4 (2018) is a wheeled service humanoid with an expressive animatronic face, speech interaction and autonomous indoor navigation, deployed for reception, customer service, promotion and public information in malls, banks and airports.

name: Sprout
desc: Sprout, from Fauna Robotics, is a lightweight, approachable, developer-ready humanoid built to fill a specific gap: most humanoids are either closed industrial systems or hard-to-deploy academic prototypes, leaving few platforms safe and expressive enough for long-term operation around people. At just 1,070 mm and 22.7 kg with 29 DOF (6-DOF arms with floor-to-countertop reach, 5-DOF compliant legs for low-impact walking, 2-DOF neck for expressive gaze), Sprout prioritises safety and accessibility: back-drivable motors, deliberately limited joint torques, a soft deformable exterior and a dedicated safety subsystem let it work in shared human spaces — it can even be squeezed by a child's hand safely. It runs NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin compute with ZED 2i stereo vision, time-of-flight sensors, IMU and a microphone array, and sports a full-color 360° facial LED array with motorized eyebrows for social expression. Out of the box it does mapping, navigation, voice interaction, walking, kneeling, crawling, jumping, dancing and fall recovery, with integrated grippers and VR-based teleoperation in a unified hardware-software stack and swappable batteries. Fauna published a full technical report in January 2026. NOTE: all specs from Fauna's official technical report — museum-grade sourcing.
actuator_type: Back-drivable motors, compliant control, limited joint torques (safety-first)
display_face: Full-color 360° facial LED array + motorized eyebrows
ai_model: Whole-body control + manipulation; unified HW/SW stack
capabilities: Safe, expressive developer humanoid: mapping, navigation, voice interaction, walking, kneeling, crawling, jumping, dancing, fall recovery, high-five; soft exterior + dedicated safety subsystem for shared human spaces
developed_by: Fauna Robotics (published full technical report Jan 2026)

name: T-HR3
desc: The Toyota T-HR3, introduced in November 2017, is Toyota's third-generation humanoid — a 1,540 mm, 75 kg, 32-DOF platform built around whole-body teleoperation with force feedback. Its defining technology is the Torque Servo Module, giving flexible, compliant joint control across 29 body points and 3 at the base, paired with force sensors at every joint. An operator wearing Toyota's Master Maneuvering System — a wearable exoskeleton rig plus a head-mounted display — moves naturally, and T-HR3 mirrors those movements in real time while transmitting the forces it feels back to the operator, enabling delicate remote manipulation. Toyota positioned it for the home, healthcare, disaster-relief and space applications, and as a platform for studying safe, smooth human-robot force interaction. NOTE: figures from Toyota's official announcements; historic/development entry to verified specs.
actuator_type: Torque Servo Modules (flexible joint control at 29 body + 3 base points)
ft_sensor: Torque sensors + force feedback at every joint
teleoperation: Master Maneuvering System — operator wears wearable exoskeleton + HMD; robot mirrors operator, operator feels force feedback
capabilities: Whole-body teleoperated mirroring with bidirectional force feedback; self-balancing; designed for home, healthcare, disaster-relief, and remote-presence use

name: ASIMO
desc: Honda's ASIMO (2000-2018) was the world's most famous bipedal humanoid for two decades - 130 cm tall, it could walk, run at ~9 km/h, climb stairs, hop and recognise faces and gestures. A landmark in dynamic bipedal locomotion, it was retired in 2018 with its technology feeding Honda's later robotics work.
achievements: World's most famous humanoid for two decades; first credible dynamic bipedal walking/running at scale
note: Historic benchmark robot — encyclopedic anchor entry

name: Pepper
desc: Pepper (SoftBank/Aldebaran, 2014) is a 120 cm social humanoid on a wheeled omnidirectional base with a chest tablet, designed to read emotions and interact in retail, reception and hospitality. Hugely visible in stores and research, production was paused in 2021.

name: NAO
desc: NAO (Aldebaran, later SoftBank Robotics) is a 58 cm, 25-DOF programmable humanoid that became the world's most widely used educational and research robot. With cameras, microphones and the NAOqi platform, it teaches coding and serves HRI research, autism therapy and classrooms globally.

name: Delivery Robot Gen 5
desc: Starship's six-wheeled autonomous sidewalk delivery robot - the most-deployed in the world with 10M+ deliveries. It travels at pedestrian pace (~6 km/h) within ~2-3 km of a store, carrying up to 10 kg (about three shopping bags) in an app-locked insulated compartment. A bogie/six-wheel system climbs curbs; perception uses 12 cameras plus ultrasonic, radar and GPS. Operates at L4 with remote human assist and runs ~18 hours on a charge.

name: Delivery Robot Gen 6
desc: The sixth-generation Starship delivery robot refines the six-wheeled sidewalk platform with upgraded compute, sensing and world-first onsite wireless charging (overnight, no plug). It carries up to 10 kg in an insulated, app-locked compartment at pedestrian speed, operating ~18 hours per charge with winter wheels for snow. Part of the fleet that makes ~125,000 road/driveway crossings daily worldwide at L4 autonomy.

name: R1
desc: Nuro's R1 was the company's first-generation passengerless autonomous delivery vehicle, launched in Scottsdale, Arizona in December 2018 with Kroger - the first-ever unmanned delivery service for the general public. A compact, electric, road-going pod with no driver or passengers, built purely to carry goods.

name: R2
desc: The Nuro R2 was the first vehicle granted a USDOT/NHTSA self-driving exemption (no mirrors, pedals or steering wheel), debuting in Houston in 2020. A narrow, passengerless electric delivery pod (1150 kg, ~190 kg payload), it carries food, groceries and parcels at up to 40 km/h with a 360-degree suite of 12 cameras, top lidar plus 14 side lidars, dual IMUs and ultrasonics, with heating/cooling cargo bays.

name: R3
desc: Nuro's third-generation vehicle (2022) is its production-ready, passengerless delivery pod. About 20% narrower than an average car, it runs up to 72 km/h with double the R2's cargo - dual ~27 cu ft compartments holding ~227 kg / 24 grocery bags with modular heating and cooling. A pedestrian-protecting external front airbag is a world-first safety feature. Built for mass production with BYD.

name: Serve Gen 1
desc: Serve Robotics' first-generation low-emission sidewalk delivery robot, spun out of Postmates/Uber. A four-wheeled L4 bot with fail-safe mechanical braking and autonomous collision avoidance, it delivers food on sidewalks with remote human assist, deployed initially with Uber Eats in Los Angeles.

name: Serve Gen 2
desc: Serve Robotics' second-generation sidewalk delivery robot - the workhorse of its commercial Los Angeles fleet with Uber Eats. L4 autonomy with fail-safe mechanical braking, a multi-camera-plus-lidar sensor suite, and an app-locked cargo compartment for food and convenience orders.

name: Serve Gen 3
desc: Serve Robotics' third-generation sidewalk delivery robot, built for national scaling with 2,000 units rolling out from 2025. It moves roughly twice as fast and twice as far as Gen 2, adds ~6 hours of daily field time, and runs 5x more AI on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin module with Ouster's REV7 digital lidar. Emergency braking stops 40% more quickly, at roughly half the prior manufacturing cost.

name: Kiwibot 5.0
desc: Kiwibot 5.0 (2024) is the latest generation of Kiwibot's four-wheeled sidewalk delivery robot, with improved autonomy, sensing and cargo capacity over the 4.0, continuing the company's campus and urban last-mile food-delivery deployments.

name: Model C
desc: Cartken's six-wheeled Model C is a camera-SLAM autonomous delivery robot (a Google Area 120 spin-off) that operates both outdoors on sidewalks and indoors with elevator/multi-floor capability. It runs L4 autonomy with instant remote-operator override, carries ~20 kg / 30 L, and is assembled by Magna in Michigan. Deployed for food and campus delivery with Uber Eats and Grubhub, and increasingly for in-facility logistics.

name: Courier
desc: Cartken's Courier is the outdoor last-mile configuration of its six-wheeled, camera-SLAM delivery platform. Built for sidewalk food and grocery runs within a ~3-mile radius, it uses vision-only autonomy with remote-operator backup and is manufactured with Magna.

name: Coco 2
desc: Coco 2 (2024) is the next generation of Coco Robotics' urban delivery bot, adding more driver-assist autonomy on top of its remote-piloted model while keeping the insulated cargo compartment for food delivery across cities including Los Angeles and Miami.

name: REV-1
desc: Refraction AI's REV-1 is a three-wheeled delivery robot designed for bike lanes rather than sidewalks or full roads, giving it a speed-and-flexibility advantage. Running up to ~24 km/h with a camera-and-radar suite (no lidar) and remote supervision, it was piloted for grocery and meal delivery in Ann Arbor and Austin.

name: Tinymile
desc: Tinymile is a Toronto-based sidewalk delivery robot operated by remote human pilots, delivering food on city sidewalks. Its small, insulated cargo bot focuses on dense downtown restaurant delivery.

name: Tortoise
desc: Tortoise builds low-speed, remotely-managed delivery and repositioning robots for retail and residential communities. Its devices, tested by Walmart, are human-piloted remotely rather than fully autonomous, handling neighbourhood grocery delivery and shared-cart repositioning.

name: Avride Robotaxi
desc: Avride's robotaxi runs the company's Level 4 autonomy stack (spun out of the former Yandex self-driving group) on production EV platforms, partnered with Uber. Avride also operates a large Uber Eats delivery-rover fleet across Dallas, Austin and Jersey City, with robotaxi expansion planned into Munich.
manufacturer_history: Autonomy team spun out of Yandex self-driving group

name: Clevon 1
desc: Clevon 1 (from Estonia's Clevon, formerly Cleveron Mobility) is a compact, road-legal autonomous delivery carrier. Electric and passengerless, it carries modular cargo at up to ~50 km/h under L4 autonomy with teleoperation oversight, targeting grocery and retail last-mile.

name: Meituan RB1
desc: Meituan's RB1 is the autonomous delivery vehicle of China's largest food-delivery platform. An electric, passengerless L4 pod with lidar-and-camera perception, it handles food and community grocery delivery in Chinese cities, integrated directly into Meituan's order network.

name: JD X
desc: JD.com's autonomous delivery robot (from its X division / JD Logistics) is an electric, passengerless L4 vehicle for last-mile e-commerce parcel delivery. Lidar-and-camera guided, it carries multiple lockered parcels to neighbourhoods and was among the first deployed at scale in China, including during the COVID period in Wuhan.

name: Cainiao Xiaomanlv
desc: Cainiao's Xiaomanlv ('Little Donkey') is Alibaba's L4 autonomous last-mile delivery robot, developed with Alibaba's DAMO Academy. Carrying dozens of parcels per trip (around 100 km of routes per charge), it serves campuses and residential communities across China and has delivered tens of millions of packages.

name: BellaBot
desc: Pudu's BellaBot is the iconic cat-faced restaurant delivery robot - a 4-tray food runner (40 kg load, 10 kg per layer) with expressive multi-modal interaction. It uses dual Laser + Visual SLAM with three RGBD depth cameras and lidar, stopping within 0.5 s on obstacles, and runs 12-24 hours on a swappable battery. Up to 20 units coordinate via PUDU SCHEDULER for busy dining rooms.

name: BellaBot Pro
desc: BellaBot Pro upgrades Pudu's flagship with VSLAM+ multi-modal, marker-less navigation and a 65 cm path clearance tuned for tight spaces, retaining the 4-tray 40 kg cat-faced design. It runs ~11 hours per swappable battery with enhanced perception and interaction.

name: KettyBot
desc: Pudu's KettyBot is a slim delivery-and-reception robot with a large built-in advertising/interaction screen. Designed to welcome and guide guests as well as run food, its narrow body suits tight restaurant aisles, navigating by SLAM with vision-based obstacle avoidance.

name: KettyBot Pro
desc: KettyBot Pro refines Pudu's reception-and-delivery robot with upgraded navigation, more tray capacity and a larger interaction display, combining guest greeting, advertising and food running in one slim chassis.

name: PuduBot 2
desc: PuduBot 2 is Pudu's enclosed-cabinet delivery robot for higher-capacity transport (up to ~60 kg) in restaurants, hotels and facilities. With dual SLAM navigation and multi-floor elevator integration, it shuttles dishes, supplies and goods between zones.

name: PuduBot 3
desc: PuduBot 3 (2025) is the latest generation of Pudu's enclosed-cabinet delivery robot, upgrading navigation, payload handling and reliability for high-throughput restaurant, hotel and facility delivery across multiple floors.

name: CC1
desc: Pudu's CC1 is a commercial cleaning robot that combines four cleaning modes (sweeping, vacuuming, mopping and scrubbing) with autonomous SLAM navigation, bringing Pudu's service-robot autonomy to floor care in restaurants, malls and offices.

name: DinerBot T1
desc: KEENON's DinerBot T1 (2016) was among the first widely-deployed restaurant delivery robots - a multi-tray food runner using lidar-based indoor navigation, helping pioneer the now-ubiquitous category of dining-room service robots.

name: DinerBot T8
desc: The KEENON DinerBot T8 is a high-capacity 4-tray restaurant delivery robot with laser SLAM navigation and 3D obstacle avoidance, built for food running and table bussing in busy dining venues.

name: DinerBot T9
desc: The KEENON DinerBot T9 is one of the most widely deployed restaurant delivery robots worldwide - a modular multi-tray runner with laser SLAM, 3D obstacle avoidance and expressive interaction for food delivery and bussing.

name: DinerBot T9 Pro
desc: The DinerBot T9 Pro upgrades KEENON's best-seller with improved navigation, sensing and interaction while keeping the modular 4-tray layout for restaurant food running and bussing.

name: DinerBot T10
desc: The KEENON DinerBot T10 is a larger-capacity service robot for bigger venues, combining higher payload and tray volume with laser SLAM navigation for restaurant, hotel and large-venue delivery.

name: DinerBot T11
desc: The DinerBot T11 (2025) is KEENON's latest-generation restaurant delivery robot, advancing navigation, payload and human-robot interaction for high-throughput dining and hospitality service.

name: ButlerBot W3
desc: The KEENON ButlerBot W3 is an enclosed-cabinet hotel delivery robot that brings guest items and room-service orders directly to rooms. It autonomously calls and rides elevators, navigates corridors by laser SLAM, and notifies guests on arrival with secure compartments.

name: S100
desc: The KEENON S100 is a heavy-duty autonomous delivery robot for larger payloads and demanding environments such as hotels, hospitals and facilities, using laser SLAM navigation with elevator integration for multi-floor bulk transport.

name: Carti
desc: Bear Robotics' Carti is an autonomous heavy-duty delivery and bussing cart from the maker of the Servi server robot. Built as a high-capacity flat/cart platform rather than a tray runner, it hauls bulk dishes, supplies and goods around restaurants and facilities with lidar-and-vision SLAM navigation.

name: Relay
desc: The Relay robot (from Relay Robotics, formerly Savioke - which pioneered hotel delivery as 'Botlr' at Aloft in 2014) is a compact enclosed-bin delivery robot. With a ~10-gallon secure compartment, it delivers room-service items in hotels and lab specimens, medications and supplies in hospitals, autonomously calling and riding elevators and returning to its dock to recharge between trips.

name: Relay Plus
desc: Relay Plus is the larger-capacity version of Relay Robotics' autonomous delivery robot, adding compartment volume for bigger or multiple-item deliveries while retaining elevator integration, auto-docking and secure compartments for hotel and hospital service.

name: Yeti 2.0
desc: Yeti 2.0 (2024) is the next generation of Ottonomy's multi-surface delivery robot, upgrading its Contextual AI navigation and sensing for more robust autonomous indoor/outdoor delivery across airports and retail.

name: RoboCoffee
desc: OrionStar's RoboCoffee is an automated robotic barista kiosk - a robotic arm system that makes and serves coffee unattended. Unlike the company's mobile delivery robots, it is a fixed beverage-preparation station for cafes, offices and public spaces.

name: Lucki Pro
desc: OrionStar's Lucki Pro is a multi-tray restaurant delivery robot with laser SLAM navigation and voice interaction, used for food running and guest service across dining and hospitality venues.

name: Flash
desc: Reeman's Flash is a cost-effective multi-tray restaurant delivery robot using laser SLAM navigation, aimed at affordable food running and hospitality service.

name: RoboShuttle
desc: YOGO Robot's RoboShuttle is an enclosed-compartment delivery robot for office buildings, integrating with elevators and access control to autonomously transport documents, parcels and supplies between floors and zones.

name: Relay Pharmaceutical
desc: Swisslog Healthcare's autonomous courier robot transports medications, lab specimens and supplies through hospitals in secure compartments. Part of Swisslog's healthcare automation portfolio, it integrates with elevators and hospital workflows to move time-sensitive pharmaceutical items between pharmacy, labs and wards.

name: Moxi
desc: Diligent Robotics' Moxi is a hospital mobile-manipulation robot: a wheeled base topped with a robotic arm (Kinova) and gripper that fetches and delivers supplies, lab samples, PPE and medications so nurses can focus on patients. It weighs 136 kg, carries ~15 kg, and uses social-aware navigation to open doors, ride elevators and move politely among people. The fleet has completed 1.25M+ deliveries across 25+ US hospitals; Moxi 2.0 (2025) adds NVIDIA-powered AI.

name: Vector
desc: Industrial-strength autonomous mobile robot for warehouse material handling, part of the LocusBots family orchestrated by LocusOne. Mecanum wheels give omnidirectional movement and precise positioning, with a compact chassis suited to almost any environment. Sold under Locus's all-inclusive Robots-as-a-Service model.

name: Freight500
desc: Heavy autonomous mobile robot base for cases and smaller palletized loads — carries up to 500 kg on a 1265×838 mm surface (fits EUR6 pallets) through 40-inch-wide aisles. Maps and plans its own routes with dynamic obstacle avoidance and a certified hardware safety system, configured via the FetchCore cloud platform. Now part of Zebra Technologies.
api: FetchCore cloud robotics platform; WMS integration

name: UDA
desc: Unity Drive Innovation's UDA is an L4 autonomous electric delivery/logistics vehicle from the Shenzhen-based developer, built for unmanned urban distribution and parcel delivery with lidar-and-camera perception.

name: DroneSentry
desc: Asylon's DroneSentry is an autonomous robotic perimeter-security system pairing self-charging security drones (DroneCore) with ground robots for automated patrol and monitoring of large sites. Its focus is robotic physical security rather than consumer delivery, though it shares the autonomous-fleet and docking technology of delivery platforms.

name: Mini 2
desc: The DJI Mini 2 (2020) is a sub-250 g folding drone with a 1/2.3-inch 12MP sensor, 4K/30fps video and a 3-axis gimbal, flying 31 minutes with OcuSync 2.0 transmission to 10 km. Its light weight made high-quality aerial photography accessible with minimal registration requirements.

name: Mini 4K
desc: The DJI Mini 4K (2024) is a budget sub-250 g drone delivering 4K/30fps video on a 3-axis stabilised gimbal with a 1/2.3-inch sensor, 31-minute flight time and 10 km OcuSync transmission - an affordable entry point into stabilised aerial footage.

name: Mini 5 Pro
desc: The DJI Mini 5 Pro (2025) packs a 1-inch 50MP sensor, 4K/60fps HDR video and a 225-degree rotating gimbal with true-vertical shooting into a sub-250 g body. It adds forward LiDAR and night omnidirectional obstacle sensing, flies 36 minutes (52 with the Plus battery) and transmits via O4+ - flagship imaging in a registration-light travel drone.

name: Air 3S
desc: The DJI Air 3S (2024) is the versatile mid-range dual-camera drone: a 1-inch 50MP wide camera plus a 1/1.3-inch 48MP 3x medium-tele camera, 4K/120fps video, 45-minute flight time and omnidirectional sensing with forward LiDAR for night flight. ActiveTrack 360 tracks subjects at up to 15 m/s.

name: Mavic 4 Pro
desc: DJI's Mavic 4 Pro (2025) is the flagship consumer camera drone: a triple-camera Hasselblad system led by a 100MP 4/3 sensor plus 48MP and 50MP telephoto lenses, shooting 6K HDR video on a 360-degree-rotating Infinity Gimbal. It flies up to 51 minutes, transmits via O4+ to ~30 km, weighs 1.06 kg and adds omnidirectional sensing and intelligent tracking.

name: Avata
desc: The DJI Avata (2022) is a compact cinewhoop FPV drone with built-in propeller guards for safe close-proximity and indoor flying. It shoots stabilised 4K/60fps video with RockSteady, flies via goggles with motion control, and recovers to a hover with its emergency brake - FPV cinematography for beginners.

name: Avata 360
desc: The DJI Avata 360 (2026) builds on the cinewhoop FPV concept with upgraded imaging and omnidirectional awareness, adding 360-capture capability and longer flight time while keeping the prop-guarded, goggle-flown design for safe immersive cinematography. (Newer model - some specifications still being confirmed.)

name: FPV
desc: The DJI FPV (2021) brought immersive first-person-view flying to the mainstream, pairing low-latency goggles with a 4K/60fps single-axis-stabilised camera. It hits ~140 km/h in Manual mode yet keeps GPS, obstacle sensing and an emergency brake-and-hover for safety, making FPV accessible to newcomers.

name: Neo
desc: The DJI Neo (2024) is a tiny ~135 g fully prop-guarded selfie drone that launches from and lands in your palm, shooting stabilised 4K video. Designed for creators, it flies pre-set QuickShots autonomously without a controller and can also be flown manually or in FPV with optional accessories.

name: Flip
desc: The DJI Flip (2025) is a sub-250 g creator drone with full propeller guards for safe close-range flight, a 1/1.3-inch 48MP sensor and 4K/60fps HDR video on a 3-axis gimbal. It combines palm-launch simplicity and forward LiDAR with longer 31-minute flights, bridging the Neo and Mini lines.
frame_type: Folding quad with full prop guards

name: Lito X1
desc: The DJI Lito X1 (2026) is a recently introduced DJI drone; detailed and verified specifications are limited at this time and should be confirmed against DJI's official spec sheet.

name: Inspire 3
desc: The DJI Inspire 3 (2023) is a full-frame 8K cinema drone with the Zenmuse X9-8K Air gimbal camera, shooting 8K/25fps CinemaDNG RAW and Apple ProRes RAW. It adds omnidirectional sensing, RTK precision, dual-operator control and O3 Pro transmission to ~15 km, with a transforming airframe for unobstructed cinematic moves.

name: Inspire 2
desc: The DJI Inspire 2 (2016) is a professional cinematography platform with interchangeable Zenmuse X5S/X7 cameras, recording up to 5.2K CinemaDNG RAW and Apple ProRes. Its transforming airframe raises the landing gear for unobstructed 360-degree shots, and dual-battery power gives ~27 minutes of flight with dual-operator control.

name: Phantom 4 Pro V2.0
desc: The DJI Phantom 4 Pro V2 (2018) is the classic fixed-arm professional camera drone with a 1-inch 20MP sensor and mechanical-shutter 4K/60fps video. Five-direction obstacle sensing, 30-minute flights and OcuSync 2.0 made it a long-standing workhorse for photography, mapping and inspection.

name: Matrice 350 RTK
desc: The DJI Matrice 350 RTK (2023) is a flagship enterprise drone platform: IP55-rated, 55-minute flight time, six-directional obstacle sensing and RTK precision, with O3 Enterprise transmission to ~20 km. It carries up to ~2.7 kg of interchangeable payloads (Zenmuse H30, L2, P1) for inspection, mapping, public safety and SAR.

name: Matrice 400
desc: The DJI Matrice 400 (2025) is DJI's next-generation enterprise platform, extending flight time to ~59 minutes, transmission range substantially, and adding onboard LiDAR and omnidirectional sensing with heavier payload capacity for demanding industrial inspection, mapping and public-safety missions. (Recent release - some specifications still being confirmed.)

name: Agras T40
desc: The DJI Agras T40 (2022) is a heavy agricultural spray drone with a coaxial twin-rotor design, a 40 L spray tank (50 kg spreading capacity) and a dual-atomising spray system. Spherical radar and binocular vision enable terrain-following and obstacle avoidance for automated spraying and spreading over large fields.

name: Agras T50
desc: The DJI Agras T50 (2023) upgrades the heavy-lift spray platform with a coaxial twin-rotor powertrain, 40 L spray tank and a high-flow dual sprinkler system. Active phased-array radar plus binocular vision give it robust terrain-following and obstacle sensing for efficient automated spraying and spreading.

name: Agras T100
desc: The DJI Agras T100 (2025) is DJI's most powerful agricultural drone: a 100 L spray tank, 150 L spreader and a 100 kg heavy-lift mode, flying up to 20 m/s with a 40 L/min flow rate and ~13 m spray swath. LiDAR, millimetre-wave radar and a Penta-Vision system deliver advanced safety, and twin 41 Ah batteries recharge in ~8 minutes via the DJI generator.

name: EVO II Pro V3
desc: The Autel EVO II Pro V3 (2023) is a 6K folding camera drone with a 1-inch 20MP Sony sensor and adjustable f/2.8-f/11 aperture. It offers 40-minute flights, 360-degree obstacle avoidance (19 sensors), SkyLink 2.0 transmission to ~15 km and Level 8 wind resistance - and notably enforces no geofencing, leaving launch authority with the operator.

name: EVO II Pro RTK
desc: The Autel EVO II Pro RTK V3 (2023) adds an RTK module for centimetre-level positioning to the 6K EVO II platform, enabling accurate photogrammetry, surveying and mapping. It keeps the 1-inch 20MP camera, 360-degree sensing and SkyLink transmission while delivering survey-grade georeferencing.

name: EVO II Dual 640T V3
desc: The Autel EVO II Dual 640T V3 (2023) pairs a 50MP 8K visual camera with a 640x512 radiometric thermal imager that records per-pixel temperatures. With 38-minute flights, 25 km transmission and Level 8 wind resistance, it is a strong-value thermal platform for inspection, search-and-rescue and public safety.

name: EVO II Enterprise V3
desc: The Autel EVO II Enterprise V3 (2023) is the rugged enterprise build of the 6K platform, with larger carbon-fibre arms and motors for ~42-minute flights, an ADS-B receiver for airspace awareness, secured storage and a bright 7.9-inch Smart Controller, aimed at inspection, mapping and public-safety teams.

name: Raptor T
desc: The Anzu Raptor T (2024) is the thermal variant of Anzu Robotics' US-data enterprise drone, adding a 640x512 thermal imager alongside a 48MP visual camera. Built on the DJI Mavic 3 Enterprise platform with Aloft software, it targets thermal inspection, public safety and search-and-rescue for security-focused operators.

name: Raptor
desc: The Anzu Raptor (2024) is a US-headquartered enterprise drone built on the proven DJI Mavic 3 Enterprise airframe under licence, paired with Aloft flight software and US-based data handling for security-conscious buyers. It offers a 4/3-class 20MP camera, ~45-minute flights, RTK and omnidirectional sensing for inspection and mapping.

name: X10D
desc: The Skydio X10D (2024) is the defense/government configuration of Skydio's flagship X10 - a US-built (NDAA-compliant) autonomous drone with AI-driven 360-degree obstacle avoidance, NightSense low-light flight, high-resolution visual and thermal payloads, and onboard autonomy for ISR, inspection and public-safety missions in GPS-denied environments.

name: RCR
desc: A Skydio autonomous drone configuration built on the company's AI-driven, vision-based flight autonomy for hands-free inspection and reconnaissance. (Model details for this specific record are limited and worth verifying against Skydio's specifications.)

name: LEMUR-S
desc: The BRINC LEMUR S is the first-generation public-safety drone that introduced indoor flight, two-way communication and a window-breaking glass breaker for tactical entry. Built for law enforcement to survey barricade and active-shooter situations from inside a structure before committing officers.

name: LEMUR 2
desc: BRINC's LEMUR 2 is a purpose-built public-safety drone for indoor, GPS-denied tactical missions. It carries a 4K camera, FLIR thermal, IR/white spotlights, two-way audio and a glass-breaker, with a 10-sensor Autonomy Engine and onboard LiDAR generating real-time 3D floor plans and a light/GPS-free 360-degree hover. AES-256-encrypted, mesh-networked and 4G-connected for live streaming via BRINC LiveOps.

name: Responder
desc: BRINC's Responder is a drone-as-first-responder (DFR) platform designed to launch autonomously in response to 911 calls and arrive on scene ahead of officers, providing live aerial situational awareness. Part of BRINC's integrated public-safety ecosystem with dock and LiveOps software.

name: Guardian
desc: BRINC's Guardian (2026) is a next-generation public-safety / drone-as-first-responder platform extending the company's autonomous response ecosystem. (Recent release - detailed specifications worth verifying against BRINC.)

name: Ghost X
desc: Anduril's Ghost-X is an expeditionary single-rotor VTOL autonomous ISR drone with dual batteries, vision-based navigation for GPS-denied environments and ~80-90 minutes of endurance carrying up to ~11 kg of modular payloads. Soldier-portable and powered by Anduril's Lattice autonomy, it was selected by the US Army's Medium-Range Reconnaissance program and the Replicator initiative.

name: Altius 700M
desc: Anduril's ALTIUS-700M is a tube-launched, fixed-wing loitering munition with ~75 minutes endurance, up to 160 km range and a 15 kg anti-armor warhead. Launchable from air, ground or maritime platforms, it supports autonomous coordinated-strike and collaborative teaming so one operator can control multiple vehicles.

name: Bolt
desc: Anduril's Bolt is a man-portable VTOL drone with 40+ minutes of endurance and ~20 km range; the Bolt-M variant is a loitering munition able to strike light vehicles, dismounted personnel and trenches. Powered by Lattice AI for autonomous behaviours, it was selected for the US Marine Corps' Organic Precision Fires-Light program.

name: Platform 1
desc: Zipline's Platform 1 is a catapult-launched fixed-wing delivery drone that flies long autonomous round-trips (up to ~160 km round trip) and air-drops packages by parachute. It pioneered national-scale medical delivery - blood, vaccines and medicines - across Rwanda, Ghana and beyond, logging tens of millions of autonomous miles.

name: Platform 2 (P2)
desc: Zipline's Platform 2 (P2 Zip) is a hybrid VTOL delivery drone that hovers high while lowering a small tethered 'droid' that steers itself to place packages precisely - on a doorstep, patio or table. Carrying up to ~3.6 kg within ~16 km, it brings quiet, accurate doorstep delivery to homes and businesses.

name: Hummingbird
desc: Alphabet's Wing delivery drone is a hybrid VTOL fixed-wing aircraft that hovers to lower packages on a tether without landing. The first drone operator certified by the FAA as an air carrier, Wing has completed 350,000+ deliveries (largely in Australia), carrying ~1.2 kg of food, pharmacy and retail goods on autonomous routes.

name: M2
desc: Matternet's M2 is an autonomous quadcopter delivery drone purpose-built for healthcare logistics, carrying up to ~2 kg over ~20 km between hospitals, labs and clinics. It loads and lands at the Matternet Station, an automated ground hub, and has run medical delivery networks in Switzerland and the US.

name: MK30
desc: Amazon Prime Air's MK30 (2024) is a hybrid VTOL fixed-wing delivery drone with six propulsors and staggered tandem wings. Smaller, quieter (~25% less perceived noise) and more durable than the MK27-2, it carries up to ~2.3 kg, cruises at ~33 m/s within ~12 km, flies in light rain, and drops packages from ~4 m without landing.

name: Teal 2
desc: The Teal 2, from Red Cat's Teal Drones, is a small NDAA-compliant ISR quadcopter built to 'dominate the night', integrating a Teledyne FLIR Hadron thermal/EO sensor for low-light reconnaissance. US-made for military and public-safety users needing secure short-range situational awareness.

name: Black Widow
desc: The Teal Black Widow (2025), from Red Cat, is a compact, backpackable squad-level reconnaissance drone designed for the US Army's Short-Range Reconnaissance program. NDAA-compliant and US-made, it provides dismounted soldiers with quick, secure ISR including low-light sensing.

name: Trinity Pro
desc: Quantum Systems' Trinity Pro is a fixed-wing VTOL mapping drone that takes off and lands vertically, then cruises on wings for ~90 minutes of efficient large-area coverage. With RTK/PPK precision and interchangeable high-resolution and multispectral payloads, it is built for professional surveying, mapping and agriculture.
payload_types: Sony RX1R II / MicaSense RedEdge-P / Altum PT / Qube 240 LiDAR

name: Vector
desc: Quantum Systems' Vector is a dual-use fixed-wing VTOL drone for ISR, mapping and security, with ~2 hours endurance and modular EO/IR payloads. Vertical takeoff and landing plus long winged endurance make it suited to both commercial survey and defense reconnaissance, including use in Ukraine.

name: WingtraOne Gen II
desc: The WingtraOne Gen II is a fixed-wing VTOL mapping drone that takes off and lands vertically yet covers large areas efficiently in winged flight (~59 minutes). With a 42MP full-frame Sony payload and PPK/RTK georeferencing, it delivers survey-grade, centimetre-accurate aerial mapping for surveying, mining and agriculture.

name: Commander 3 XL
desc: Draganfly's Commander 3 XL is a rugged Canadian/US-made modular enterprise drone for public safety, inspection and industrial use. It carries interchangeable EO/IR, mapping and delivery payloads with extended flight time and RTK precision, built by one of the longest-established commercial drone makers.

name: Typhoon H Plus
desc: The Yuneec Typhoon H Plus (2018) is a hexacopter with a 1-inch 20MP sensor and a 360-degree rotating gimbal camera shooting 4K/60fps. Its six rotors add redundancy (it can land on five), and Intel RealSense provides obstacle avoidance for photography and inspection.

name: H850 RTK
desc: The Yuneec H850 RTK (2023) is a survey-oriented hexacopter with RTK precision positioning for centimetre-accurate mapping and photogrammetry. (Detailed specifications for this record are limited and worth verifying.)

name: HS720E
desc: The Holy Stone HS720E (2022) is a popular budget GPS drone with a 4K camera, electronic image stabilisation, brushless motors and ~23-minute flight time. An affordable entry point for hobbyists wanting GPS return-to-home and follow modes.

name: HS900
desc: The Holy Stone HS900 (2024) upgrades the budget line with a sub-250 g body, a 3-axis mechanical gimbal, 4K video and ~36-minute flight time, bringing gimbal-stabilised footage to an affordable price point.

name: Tello
desc: The Ryze Tello (2018), powered by DJI flight tech and an Intel processor, is a tiny 80 g beginner drone with 720p video and electronic image stabilisation. Easy and safe to fly indoors via Wi-Fi, it became hugely popular as a first drone and STEM-education tool.

name: Tello EDU
desc: The Ryze Tello EDU (2019) is the programmable education version of the Tello, supporting Scratch, Python and Swift coding plus multi-drone swarm programming. Built to teach kids and students the fundamentals of flight and code in classrooms.

name: Zino Mini Pro
desc: The Hubsan Zino Mini Pro (2021) packs a 1/1.3-inch 48MP sensor, 4K video on a 3-axis gimbal, three-directional obstacle sensing and up to ~40-minute flight into a sub-250 g folding body - an unusually feature-rich budget alternative in the lightweight class.

name: Aibao FPV
desc: The Walkera Aibao is a 4K FPV quadcopter notable for its augmented-reality gaming modes, overlaying virtual elements onto the live video feed for interactive flying games alongside standard aerial photography.

name: Antigravity A1
desc: The Antigravity A1 (2026) is Insta360's debut drone under its Antigravity brand, built around an 8K 360-degree camera so footage can be reframed entirely in post with the drone effectively invisible in shots. (Recent announcement - detailed specifications still being confirmed.)

name: X1
desc: The HoverAir X1 (2023) is a tiny 125 g fully prop-guarded pocket selfie drone that launches from your palm and autonomously follows you for hands-free video. Controller-free and ultra-portable, it shoots stabilised 2.7K footage with preset cinematic flight paths.

name: X1 Pro
desc: The HoverAir X1 Pro (2025) upgrades the palm-launch selfie drone with a higher-resolution sensor (up to 8K), faster tracking and longer flight, while keeping the prop-guarded, controller-free, follow-me design for hands-free action and vlog capture.

name: Atom 2
desc: The Potensic Atom 2 (2024) is a sub-250 g folding drone with a 3-axis gimbal, 48MP sensor and 4K/120fps video, positioned as an affordable rival to DJI's Mini line with night-shooting modes and a long ~32-minute flight time.

name: SOTEN
desc: ACSL's SOTEN (Sky-Hawk) is a Japanese-made small drone developed as a security-conscious alternative to foreign drones for government and infrastructure use. With swappable 4K/thermal/multispectral payloads, encrypted data handling and domestic supply-chain assurance, it serves inspection, security and disaster-response roles.

name: PowerEgg X
desc: The PowerVision PowerEgg X (2020) is an egg-shaped convertible device that works as a 4K autonomous drone, a handheld AI camera, or - with a waterproof housing - a drone capable of landing on and taking off from water. Its AI camera tracks and frames subjects automatically.

name: Tango2
desc: Draganfly's Tango2 is a compact, portable drone for public-safety and inspection work, offering quick-deploy aerial situational awareness from the veteran North American drone manufacturer.

name: Edge 130
desc: Red Cat's Edge 130 is a US-made VTOL reconnaissance drone aimed at military and public-safety ISR. (Detailed specifications for this record are limited and worth verifying against the manufacturer.)

name: Puma 3 AE
desc: AeroVironment's RQ-20 Puma 3 AE is a hand-launched, all-environment fixed-wing ISR drone with a stabilised EO/IR gimbal, ~2.5 hours endurance (with long-endurance battery) and ~20 km range. Waterproof for land or maritime operations, it provides persistent tactical reconnaissance for ground forces.

name: Switchblade 300
desc: AeroVironment's Switchblade 300 is a man-portable, tube-launched loitering munition - a backpackable 'kamikaze' drone with ~15 minutes endurance and ~10 km range that streams video before diving onto a target with a small anti-personnel warhead and a wave-off/abort capability. Widely fielded by the US military and supplied to Ukraine.

name: V-BAT
desc: Shield AI's V-BAT is a ducted-fan VTOL fixed-wing drone that takes off and lands vertically from a small footprint (including ships) yet flies up to ~10 hours. Powered by the Hivemind AI pilot, it operates autonomously in GPS- and comms-denied environments for ISR and maritime surveillance without external operators.

name: Elios 3
desc: Flyability's Elios 3 is a collision-tolerant drone wrapped in a protective cage for inspecting confined and hazardous industrial spaces - tanks, boilers, tunnels and silos. Its FlyAware LiDAR-SLAM system builds real-time 3D maps in GPS-denied interiors, with a 4K camera and optional thermal payload for safe remote inspection.

name: Aero
desc: Exyn Technologies' Aero is an autonomous LiDAR-mapping drone built for GPS-denied environments like underground mines and complex industrial sites. Powered by ExynAI Level-4-class autonomy, it self-navigates and builds high-fidelity 3D point-cloud maps without a pilot or prior map.

name: Flytrex Drone
desc: Flytrex operates an autonomous food-and-retail delivery drone that lowers orders by wire into a customer's backyard without landing. Carrying a few kilograms over short suburban ranges, it runs FAA-approved delivery services in US neighbourhoods in partnership with restaurants and retailers.

name: EH216-S
desc: The EHang 216S is a two-seat autonomous passenger eVTOL with 16 rotors on eight arms. Pilotless and command-and-control flown, it carries ~220 kg (two passengers) at up to ~130 km/h over ~35 km for urban air mobility and sightseeing. EHang received a CAAC type certificate for the EH216-S, a milestone toward commercial autonomous passenger flight.

name: Waymo Driver (Jaguar I-PACE)
desc: Waymo's Level 4 robotaxi platform on Jaguar I-PACE. 2,000+ vehicles, 250,000+ weekly paid rides across SF/Phoenix/LA. Alphabet-backed.

name: Zeekr RT
desc: Purpose-built Waymo robotaxi by Zeekr (Geely). Replacing I-PACE fleet. 6-seat, longer range, no steering wheel. Phoenix launch 2025.
operational_design_domain: Geofenced urban, 360° to 500 m, day/night, most weather

name: Cybercab
desc: Tesla's purpose-built two-seat robotaxi with no steering wheel or pedals, butterfly doors and a single 20.5-inch display. Camera-only autonomy on Tesla's AI5 (HW5) computer - no lidar or radar. ~50-60 kWh battery for roughly 480 km range; charges via inductive wireless pad (no charge port, >90% efficient) and self-cleans between rides. Target price under US$30,000 with ~US$0.30/mile operating cost; production from Q2 2026 at Giga Texas.

name: Zoox Robotaxi
desc: The Zoox robotaxi (Amazon) is a purpose-built, bidirectional, steering-wheel-free vehicle with carriage-style seating for four, designed from scratch for autonomous urban ride-hailing. 360 deg LiDAR/radar/camera sensing; operating/testing in Las Vegas, San Francisco and Austin.
manufacturer_history: Acquired by Amazon (2020, ~$1.3B)
config: Bidirectional, no steering wheel, 4 carriage seats

name: Apollo Go RT5
desc: Baidu's commercial robotaxi. 17M+ rides completed, 240M+ km driven. Operating in Wuhan, Beijing, Shenzhen. Dubai expansion 2026.

name: Apollo Go RT6
desc: Baidu's sixth-generation Apollo Go robotaxi (Yichi 06) - a purpose-built L4 vehicle with no steering wheel and a five-lidar sensor suite. Manufacturing cost under US$29,000 lets Apollo Go scale aggressively; operating in Wuhan and Beijing and partnering with Uber to deploy globally.

name: Robotaxi GXR
desc: WeRide's robotaxi. 1,600+ vehicle fleet globally. Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Singapore, France, Belgium operations. Uber partner.

name: Robobus
desc: Autonomous Level 4 shuttle bus. Belgium's first federal L4 permit. Runs between Leuven station and corridor with safety officer.

name: PonyTaxi Gen 7
desc: Pony.ai's seventh-generation robotaxi system on BAIC and Toyota platforms, running L4 autonomy with a lidar-and-camera sensor suite. Operates across Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Beijing and Shanghai; the fleet reached ~1,159 vehicles in late 2025 with a target of 3,000+ by end-2026.

name: DiDi RoboRide
desc: DiDi Autonomous Driving's robotaxi, co-developed with GAC Aion on the Aion V SUV. The first mass-produced L4 model integrates 33 sensors in a 360° blind-spot-free fusion architecture, including four Hesai AT128 lidars (1.53M points/sec, 200 m range) and 4D imaging radar. Deployed via the DiDi app in Guangzhou with Beijing road-test approval.

name: IV.5 Robotaxi
desc: SAIC Mobility's robotaxi, built on SAIC's IM Motors EV platform and powered by Momenta's MSD Level 4 autonomy stack. Public trials run in Shanghai's Jiading district and Suzhou via the SAIC Mobility app, billed as the world's first pre-installed mass-produced unmanned robotaxi program with IM Motors.

name: Ioniq 5 Robotaxi
desc: Hyundai-Aptiv joint venture robotaxi on Ioniq 5. Las Vegas, LA service via Uber and Lyft.

name: Wayve Driver
desc: Wayve Driver is an embodied-AI, end-to-end driving system (an 'AV2.0' approach) that learns to drive from data rather than relying on HD maps or hand-coded rules. It is camera-first and hardware-agnostic, can run across different vehicle platforms, and is powered by Wayve's GAIA world model. UK-based, testing on London streets, with partnerships including Nissan (production automated driving from 2027) and Uber.

name: Momenta MSD
desc: Momenta's MSD (Momenta Self Driving) is a scalable Level 4 autonomy stack using a data-driven 'flywheel' approach. Deployed on SAIC IM Motors robotaxis in Shanghai and Suzhou (~60-vehicle pilot) and licensed to automakers including Toyota, Mercedes-Benz, GM, BYD, SAIC and GAC; Uber partnership targets European robotaxi launch in 2026.

name: Verne 2-Seater Robotaxi
desc: Verne is a Croatian robotaxi company spun out of hypercar maker Rimac, operating Europe's first commercial robotaxi service in Zagreb. The purpose-built two-seater uses Pony.ai's Level 4 autonomous driving technology and is an Uber platform partner.
manufacturer_history: Spun out of Rimac (electric hypercar maker)

name: May Mobility Shuttle
desc: May Mobility operates Level 4 autonomous microtransit shuttles built on the Toyota Sienna Autono-MaaS minivan, using its Multi-Policy Decision Making (MPDM) AI. Deployed in cities including Arlington (TX), Grand Rapids, Sun City and Detroit, integrated with Lyft and Uber for first/last-mile public transit.

name: Beep Shuttle
desc: Beep is a US autonomous mobility operator that designs and manages driverless, low-speed electric shuttle networks on fixed routes, with centralized fleet orchestration and remote supervision. Deployments include Lake Nona (Florida) and other planned-community and campus environments.

name: Aurora Driver
desc: The Aurora Driver is a Level 4 autonomous trucking platform that launched driverless commercial freight between Dallas and Houston in April 2024. Its multi-modal suite of 25+ sensors gives a 360 degree view, anchored by proprietary FirstLight FMCW long-range lidar that detects objects beyond 450 m (next-gen kit extends to 1 km), plus custom imaging radar and high-resolution cameras. Powered by Aurora's Verifiable AI and integrated onto Peterbilt 579 and Volvo VNL Class 8 trucks; 4.5M+ on-road miles with Sun Belt route expansion underway.
powertrain: Integrated on Peterbilt 579 (PACCAR) & Volvo VNL Class 8 trucks
lidar_brand: Aurora FirstLight FMCW (>450 m, next-gen 1 km) + conventional AM lidar
ai_model: Aurora Verifiable AI + Generative AI simulation

name: Kodiak Driver
desc: The Kodiak Driver is a Level 4 autonomous trucking system built around modular, serviceable SensorPods (lidar, radar and cameras integrated into the truck's mirror housings) and a redundant compute and actuation stack. Kodiak began driverless commercial operations in 2024, including rugged off-road oilfield hauling in the Permian Basin for Atlas Energy, alongside highway middle-mile freight.
operational_design_domain: Highway middle-mile + rugged off-road, Class 8 trucks
lidar_brand: Modular Kodiak SensorPods (lidar in mirror housings)
manufacturer_history: Public via Ares Acquisition Corp II (Kodiak AI, 2025)

name: Waabi Driver
desc: Waabi Driver is an AI-first Level 4 autonomous trucking system built on a single end-to-end generative-AI foundation model rather than a large hand-engineered stack. Founded by Raquel Urtasun, Waabi validates the Driver largely inside Waabi World, a generative-AI neural simulator, and is partnered with Volvo Autonomous Solutions on the VNL Autonomous platform; driverless Texas operations planned from 2025.

name: PlusCore
desc: Plus develops SuperDrive, an L4 autonomous-driving software stack delivered through PlusCore - a production domain controller designed to be factory-installed on OEM Class 8 trucks. Partnered with TRATON/Scania, IVECO and Hyundai, Plus uses a generative-AI foundation-model approach and NVIDIA DRIVE compute, targeting driver-out long-haul freight.

name: Gatik Class 6/7
desc: Gatik's Driver is a Level 4 autonomous system purpose-built for the middle mile - fixed, repeatable B2B routes between distribution centers and retail stores. Deployed on Isuzu medium-duty box trucks (multi-temperature compartments) with fully redundant braking, steering and sensing, NVIDIA DRIVE Thor compute and Velodyne lidar. Gatik launched the world's first driverless commercial transport service with Walmart in 2021 and runs daily revenue routes across Arkansas, Texas, Arizona and Ontario.
operational_design_domain: Fixed middle-mile routes (up to ~480 km), urban + highway

name: Torc Daimler Truck
desc: Torc Robotics, a majority-owned subsidiary of Daimler Truck, is developing the Torc Virtual Driver - a Level 4 autonomous system integrated onto the Freightliner Cascadia Class 8 truck. Targeting driverless hub-to-hub freight on Texas lanes (Laredo-Dallas, Dallas-Houston) with a commercial launch planned for 2027, leveraging Daimler's redundant chassis and partnerships with Google Cloud and NVIDIA.
manufacturer_history: Majority-owned by Daimler Truck AG

name: Einride Pod
desc: The Einride Pod is a cabless, all-electric autonomous freight vehicle - it has no driver compartment at all. Operating at Level 4 with a single remote operator able to supervise multiple Pods, it carries up to ~16 tonnes of cargo on battery-electric power (~180 km range) using NVIDIA DRIVE compute and a lidar-based sensor suite. Deployed on defined routes and in closed facilities across Sweden and the US for shippers including GE Appliances, Maersk and PepsiCo.
operational_design_domain: Defined routes, closed facilities + public roads
safety_driver: No (cabless; one remote operator supervises multiple Pods)

name: Stack AV Class 8
desc: Stack AV is an autonomous trucking company founded in 2023 by Argo AI co-founders Bryan Salesky and Peter Rander and backed by SoftBank. It is developing a Level 4 self-driving stack for Class 8 long-haul trucks, currently in testing.
manufacturer_history: Founded 2023 by ex-Argo AI founders Bryan Salesky & Peter Rander; SoftBank-backed

name: Xuanyuan
desc: Inceptio Technology's Xuanyuan is a full-stack, mass-production autonomous driving system for heavy trucks, factory-integrated with Sinotruk and Dongfeng Class 8 tractors. Operating commercial L3 highway trunk logistics across China's expressway network for shippers including AB InBev and Nestle, with an L4 driver-out roadmap.

name: Yardbot
desc: Outrider's system automates the distribution yard - an electric autonomous yard truck that moves, spots and hitches trailers, connects brake lines and handles repetitive yard tasks without a driver. Operating at low speed within geofenced private yards, it combines an electric yard tractor with Outrider's L4 autonomy and lidar-based perception.

name: AIMD
desc: Forterra (formerly Robotic Research) builds off-road autonomy that operates in GPS-denied, unstructured environments for defense and commercial applications. Its AutoDrive system enables autonomous off-road mobility and leader-follower convoy operations, integrated onto a wide range of military and commercial ground vehicles.
manufacturer_history: Formerly Robotic Research

name: EpicSim
desc: Applied Intuition's EpicSim is a high-fidelity simulation and validation environment for developing autonomous-vehicle software. It generates photorealistic sensor data (camera, lidar, radar) and large-scale scenario libraries so developers can test and validate self-driving stacks in software across billions of virtual miles before on-road deployment.

name: AT128 LiDAR
desc: Hesai's AT128 is an automotive-grade long-range hybrid solid-state lidar with genuine 128-channel VCSEL e-scanning. It delivers 1.53 million points/sec, a 120 deg x 25.4 deg field of view, 200 m range at 10% reflectivity and +/-3 cm accuracy, meeting AEC-Q automotive standards. Widely adopted for L3+ ADAS and robotaxi perception (e.g. Li Auto L9 and the DiDi/GAC Aion robotaxi).

name: Iris LiDAR
desc: Luminar's Iris is a long-range time-of-flight lidar using an eye-safe 1550 nm fiber laser, detecting low-reflectivity objects at ~250 m (and high-reflectivity targets far beyond). Designed for series-production passenger vehicles, it is integrated as the forward lidar on the Volvo EX90 and Polestar 3 to enable highway automated driving.

name: EyeQ6
desc: The Mobileye EyeQ6 High is a 7 nm automotive system-on-chip delivering roughly 34 TOPS for premium ADAS and L2+/L3 automated driving. It runs full surround-camera perception and sensor fusion in a single power-efficient SoC, succeeding the EyeQ5 in Mobileye's driver-assistance and autonomy platforms.

name: STORMRUNNER
desc: All-new 8-meter HDPE unmanned surface vessel (USV) from Sea Machines Robotics, designed for high-performance defense and commercial marine autonomy. Powered by the SM300-SP autonomous command and control system, it offers a 40+ knot top speed, 500-700 nautical mile range, and a 500 kg modular payload bay. Selected by Leonardo DRS in 2026 to demonstrate maritime counter-UAS (C-UAS) capability.

name: R2 Robotaxi
desc: Rivian's R2-based robotaxi running an in-house Level 4 autonomy stack on Rivian's third-generation platform - a multi-modal suite of 11 cameras, 5 radars and 1 lidar powered by two custom RAP1 inference chips. Part of an Uber partnership targeting up to 50,000 autonomous vehicles across 25 cities in the US, Canada and Europe by 2031.
operating_cities: Planned: US, Canada, Europe (25 cities by 2031)

name: Lucid Midsize Robotaxi
desc: A premium global robotaxi built on Lucid's software-defined EV platform with the Nuro Driver Level 4 autonomy system, created exclusively for the Uber network. Sensor suite combines high-resolution cameras, solid-state lidar and radar for 360° perception via a low-profile roof halo. Uber plans to deploy 20,000+ vehicles over six years, starting in the San Francisco Bay Area in 2026.

name: BlueROV2
desc: World's most popular sub-$10K ROV — open-source, Raspberry Pi-based, with thousands deployed globally for education, research, and inspection. 6 or 8 vectored T200 thrusters, 100 m depth (300 m heavy-config), neutrally buoyant tether. ArduSub firmware.
use_cases_note: THE standard open research/inspection ROV — thousands in universities & industry

name: Seaeye Falcon
desc: The Saab Seaeye Falcon is one of the world's best-selling electric observation-class ROVs - five thrusters for stability in strong currents, standard 300 m (deep-rated 1000 m) depth, two LED lights, a high-res colour camera and a nav pod with auto depth/heading, all driven by iCON intelligent control. Surface kit fits in a single flight case.
control_method: iCON intelligent control (auto depth / auto heading)

name: Seaeye Lynx
desc: Inspection-class ROV bridging observation-class (Falcon) and work-class systems. Six brushless-DC thrusters (4H + 2V) deliver high maneuverability, with single-mode fibre tether for long-range operation. 1,500 m depth rating, 200 kg modular polypropylene frame.

name: Seaeye Sabertooth
desc: Pioneering hybrid underwater vehicle that operates as either AUV (battery, autonomous) or ROV (tethered). 1,200 m operational depth (3,000 m crush), 5-knot top speed, ~10 kWh lithium polymer batteries. Used for subsea resident operations and deep-water inspection.

name: Seaeye eWROV (SR20)
desc: Saab Seaeye's electric work-class ROV — a Class III B vehicle with 560 kgf bollard pull from electric thrusters. Operates to 3,000 m depth with dual manipulator arms supporting 400 kg arm payload. All-electric design eliminates the hydraulic systems traditionally required for work-class operations.

name: Dive-LD
desc: Modular autonomous large-displacement undersea vehicle for long-endurance subsea operations. 6,000 m depth rating, 7-knot top speed, up to 10 days endurance, 580 km range. 1.2 m diameter, 2,720 kg displacement. Acquired with the 2021 Dive Technologies acquisition.

name: Dive-XL (Ghost Shark)
desc: Anduril's largest autonomous undersea vehicle, developed with the Royal Australian Navy as 'Ghost Shark'. Designed for extreme endurance — up to 3,704 km range — at 6,000 m depth. Modular payload bays enable ISR, ASW, or deployment of smaller assets like Copperhead effectors.

name: Copperhead
desc: Family of reusable undersea effectors — torpedo-form-factor UUVs (Copperhead-100 and Copperhead-500) launched from Dive-XL or Ghost Shark host platforms. 30-knot top speed. Designed as expendable or recoverable scouts/strikers.
launch_method: Launched from Dive-XL / Ghost Shark host platform

name: Seabed Sentry
desc: Subsea-resident sensor node providing persistent undersea surveillance. Deployed and periodically recharged by Dive-XL — eliminating need for ships or submarines to visit the deployment site. Forms a distributed undersea sensor network.

name: Boxfish AUV
desc: Autonomous variant of Boxfish's hard-anodised aluminium platform — same chassis as Luna ROV but battery-powered for autonomous missions. 8 vectored thrusters, 1,000 m depth.

name: Luna ROV
desc: Premium cinematography ROV used by major nature documentary productions (BBC, National Geographic). 8 vectored thrusters with proprietary control delivering stable, smooth motion for film work. 1,000 m depth, fibre-optic tether option to 3,000 m.

name: MOLA AUV
desc: Research-class AUV from MBARI featuring 6-DOF vectored thrusters for high-precision station-keeping and complex maneuvering. 1,000 m depth, 30 kg hard-anodised aluminium frame. Used for marine biology research.

name: Iver4
desc: Fourth-generation Iver AUV from L3Harris (formerly OceanServer). 300 m depth, 20-hour endurance, 74 km range, 100 kg (man-portable). Titanium and carbon fiber construction. Launchable from submarine torpedo tubes.
launch_method: Ship, pier, or submarine torpedo tube

name: Gavia AUV
desc: Modular AUV with swappable mid-sections enabling configurations from base survey vehicle to advanced multi-sensor systems. 1,000 m depth, 5.5-knot top speed, 200 mm diameter — small enough for one person to handle assembled.

name: Slocum Glider
desc: Iconic underwater glider using variable buoyancy (changing volume to sink/rise) for propulsion — no thrusters, extremely low power consumption. 1,000 m depth, 0.7-knot speed, multi-month endurance. Named after Joshua Slocum, first solo circumnavigator.

name: Wave Glider
desc: Unique wave-powered unmanned surface vehicle that uses ocean wave motion for propulsion (combined with solar panels for electronics power). Theoretically infinite endurance — Wave Gliders have completed multi-month transoceanic missions. Acquired by Boeing 2016, divested 2023.
manufacturer_history: Liquid Robotics founded 2007, acquired by Boeing 2016, sold to independent ownership 2023.

name: HUGIN Superior
desc: Premier deep-water survey AUV from Kongsberg, used by major oceanographic institutes and offshore survey contractors. 6,000 m depth, 72-hour endurance, 4-knot survey speed, 2,200 kg. HISAS 1032 synthetic aperture sonar enables 0.5×0.5 m resolution seabed mapping at 200 m altitude.

name: REMUS 100
desc: World's most widely deployed man-portable AUV — over 300 units sold globally. 100 m depth, 5-knot top speed, 10-hour endurance, 37 kg. Inertial navigation + DVL + acoustic modem. Used by US Navy, Royal Navy, RAN, and most NATO navies.

name: REMUS 6000
desc: Deep-water REMUS variant rated to 6,000 m depth. 22-hour endurance, 120 km range, 4-knot survey speed, 880 kg. Famously used in the search for Air France Flight 447 (found 2011 at ~3,900 m depth) and SS El Faro (2015, 4,500 m).

name: Revolution
desc: Deep Trekker's flagship inspection-class ROV with 6 vectored thrusters and Bridge Technology — rotates the entire camera/sensor pod independently of the body. 305 m depth, 700 m tether option, integrated DVL + USBL navigation.

name: FIFISH V6 Expert
desc: QYSEA's prosumer underwater drone with 6 vectored thrusters delivering omnidirectional movement. 4K UHD camera, 100 m depth, 100 m tether option. Lightweight at 4 kg, includes manipulator arm option. Popular for underwater cinematography and search & rescue.
battery_life: 1.5 h vs 1 m/s current; up to 6 h still water
payload_interface: Q-Interface (robotic arm 100 N grip, sonar, laser scaler, sampler)
use_cases_note: Inspection, research, media, salvage — best consumer-pro crossover ROV

name: FIFISH Pro W6
desc: Industrial-grade underwater ROV rated to 350 m, with six Q-Motor vectored thrusters delivering strong current-fighting performance up to 4 knots. Dual 4K UHD camera system with 12,000-lumen lighting; 388 Wh removable battery runs 6-8 hours and quick-charges to 70% in one hour. Five Q-interface payload ports support 2D/3D imaging sonar, claws, dozers and water samplers. Sonar array provides distance lock, altitude lock, collision avoidance and contour scanning. U-QPS positioning + Station Lock for 3D path recording and drift-free station keeping. VR goggle control with head tracking.
sonar: Sonar array (distance/altitude lock, collision avoidance, contour scan)
use_cases_note: Bridge/tank inspection, aquaculture, hydrographic industry platform

name: M2 Pro
desc: Chasing's light-industrial ROV with 8 vectored thrusters, 150 m depth rating, 4-knot top speed. 300 Wh battery, 200 m tether. Aimed at SMB inspection and commercial diving support.
app: Chasing GO2 (mission planning, GPS surface tracking, depth lock, telemetry)
use_cases_note: Offshore pipeline inspection, deep-reef survey, archaeology
note: FLAG — 'chasing-m2-pro' (brand 'Chasing Innovation', 15f) is a DUPLICATE of this entry; merge.

name: M2 S
desc: Compact entry-level inspection ROV from Chasing. 8 vectored thrusters in a 4.5 kg housing, 100 m depth, 200 m tether option. Targets budget-conscious inspection users.
use_cases_note: Compact pro inspection/imaging

name: OpenROV Trident
desc: Pioneering Kickstarter consumer ROV (2017) that helped popularise underwater drones. 3 thrusters, 100 m depth, 2-knot top speed, 25 m tether, 2.9 kg. Discontinued after Sofar Ocean acquisition shifted focus.

name: SwarmDiver
desc: Micro USV/UUV designed for swarming operations — multiple SwarmDivers operate coordinated as a fleet from a single operator interface. Twin-thruster propulsion, 50 m depth, 1.7 kg per unit.

name: 510 PackBot
desc: iRobot's 510 PackBot is one of the most battle-proven EOD robots ever built - over 4,500 delivered, used at 9/11, across Iraq and Afghanistan, and the first robots into the Fukushima reactors in 2011. Man-portable at under 24 kg and deployable in two minutes, its OmniReach manipulator reaches 2 m and lifts ~20 kg, climbs 45-degree stairs, is submersible, and carries LWIR thermal, FLIR Fido explosives detection and CBRN/HazMat kits. Now part of Teledyne FLIR.

name: Andros F6B
desc: Remotec's (Northrop Grumman) Andros F6B is a large, heavy-duty EOD platform with dual mobility - quick-release pneumatic wheels for a narrow profile plus patented articulating tracks for rough terrain and stairs. Its 7-degree-of-freedom manipulator arm offers high dexterity for render-safe procedures, making it a long-serving bomb-squad workhorse worldwide.

name: Titus
desc: Remotec's (Northrop Grumman) Titus is a newer-generation medium EOD robot emphasising modularity and ease of transport, with a manipulator arm and sensor payloads for explosive-ordnance disposal and CBRN reconnaissance for military and public-safety users.

name: CALIBER MK3
desc: ICOR Technology's CALIBER MK3 is a mid-size Canadian EOD robot with a powerful articulating manipulator arm, designed for affordability and ruggedness. A popular choice for police bomb squads, it handles IED render-safe procedures, remote inspection and disruptor deployment.

name: Bobcat
desc: Thales' Bobcat is a tracked unmanned ground vehicle for explosive-ordnance disposal and hazardous-environment reconnaissance, carrying a manipulator and sensor suite for remote inspection and render-safe tasks.

name: Quince
desc: Quince, developed by the Chiba Institute of Technology (with Tohoku University and others), is a tracked urban search-and-rescue robot with four articulated sub-track flippers for climbing rubble and stairs. It became known for entering the Fukushima Daiichi reactor buildings after the 2011 disaster to capture video and radiation/dosimetry data in areas too dangerous for humans.
robot_form: Tracked USAR robot with four sub-track flippers

name: WALK-MAN
desc: WALK-MAN, from the Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia (IIT), is a rugged full-size disaster-response research humanoid developed under an EU project launched in the wake of the Fukushima nuclear accident to explore humanoids that could intervene in hazardous, human-engineered environments. Standing about 1.85 m and 100 kg with roughly 33 DOF, it uses high-power series-elastic, torque-controlled actuators for compliant, forceful whole-body motion, with a stereo/depth perception head, force-torque sensing and an IMU. It was demonstrated performing DARPA-Robotics-Challenge-class tasks: walking over rubble, turning valves, removing debris, drilling and operating equipment in damaged settings. WALK-MAN advanced IIT's expertise in powerful compliant actuation that later fed into the institute's broader humanoid work. NOTE: specs from IIT/EU WALK-MAN project publications; verified research-grade figures, some flagged where sources vary.
dof_note: ~33 DOF whole body (torque-controlled)
capabilities: Rugged disaster-response humanoid: locomotion over rubble, valve turning, debris removal, drilling, driving; developed for EU post-Fukushima disaster-response research (DRC-class tasks)
developed_by: IIT (EU WALK-MAN project, post-Fukushima disaster-response research)

name: Centauro
desc: Centauro, from the Italian Institute of Technology (IIT), is a centaur-shaped disaster-response robot: a four-legged base with steerable wheels at each foot for hybrid driving/walking, topped by a humanoid torso with two highly dexterous arms. Built largely with lightweight 3D-printed parts (~93 kg), it manipulates debris, turns valves and handles tools in environments too dangerous for people.
robot_form: Centaur: four legs-on-wheels base + humanoid torso with two arms

name: Thermite RS1
desc: Howe & Howe's Thermite RS1 (now Textron Systems) is a compact tracked firefighting robot for tight and confined spaces - doorways, entries and hallways.
