desc: Dreame's Matrix10 Ultra is billed as the world's first robot vacuum with a Multi-Mop Switching dock - a three-solution compartment that swaps mop pads per room and keeps them heated while mopping, plus dual cleaning/pet-odour solution dosing and dirt detection that re-passes stains. 30,000 Pa suction and advanced threshold-climbing navigation. AU RRP A$3,499.
max_threshold: 80 mm tiered (ProLeap) / 42 mm single-layer / U-legs 30 mm
dock_type: Multi-Mop Switching Dock (auto-swaps pad per zone) + PowerDock

name: Flow 2
navigation: TwinAI dual HD RGB cameras + VLM (10 TOPS)
desc: The Narwal Flow 2 is Narwal's 2026 flagship robot vacuum-mop, built around its signature FlowWash mopping system: a continuously self-cleaning rolling track mop (treadmill-style) that rinses in real time with up to 140°F hot water, presses down at 12 N, and uses dual water tanks with 16 nozzles plus a scraper to separate dirty water — giving far more floor contact and dwell time than spinning pads or thin rollers. On the vacuum side it delivers 31,000 Pa of suction with a DualFlow dual anti-tangle brush system (dual short rollers + long-bristle side brush) for an SGS-certified 0% tangle rate and excellent pet-hair pickup. Navigation runs on TwinAI: dual HD RGB cameras and a VLM 'brain' on a 10-TOPS processor that recognise an effectively unlimited range of objects down to 5 mm (and even locate keys or wallets), with all visuals processed locally under TÜV-certified privacy. The 95 mm slim body crosses 40 mm thresholds and lifts its mop 12 mm on carpet. A maintenance-free dock self-empties to a reusable 2.5 L bag (up to 120 days), washes mops with heated water, warm-air dries, dispenses detergent, and offers an auto refill/drain plumbing option. Freo Mind 4.0, NarGPT voice, video call and Matter included. US price $1,499.99.
local_processing: Yes (on-device visual processing, TÜV Rheinland certified)
anti_tangle: Yes (DualFlow zero-tangle roller + reversing side brush)
edge_cleaning: Yes (EdgeReach mop extension, to 5 mm of walls)
dock_type: Multifunction (self-empty + mop wash + dry + auto-refill + detergent)

name: Freo Z10 Turbo
desc: The Narwal Freo Z10 Turbo (CES 2026) offers 25,000 Pa suction with CarpetFocus technology, upgraded obstacle avoidance and a fully self-cleaning dock, building on Narwal's Freo Z line.
carpet_boost: Yes (CarpetFocus: mop lift + brush cover, 182% boost, 2× pickup)
edge_cleaning: EdgeReach mop extension + swing; reversing side brush

name: Deebot X12 OmniCyclone
mop_type: OZMO Roller 3.0 (self-washing roller) + FocusJet high-pressure jet pre-wash
desc: The ECOVACS Deebot X12 OmniCyclone is Ecovacs' 2026 flagship robot vacuum-mop (launched April 2026, CES 2026 reveal), built around two standout ideas: a bagless OmniCyclone dock and FocusJet stain pre-dissolving. The PureCyclone 2.0 dock uses dual-stage cyclonic separation (under 1% suction loss) into a reusable 1.6 L bin for up to 48 days hands-free — no consumable bags. FocusJet detects dried-on stains and pre-sprays high-pressure heated water (arch-pattern jets) before the OZMO Roller 3.0 self-washing mop — a 10.6-inch roller, 50% longer than the prior gen, spinning at 220 RPM with 15 mm carpet lift and an auto-deploying carpet shield — scrubs them away. On the vacuum side a BLAST airflow system delivers 22 L/s airflow and up to 22,000 Pa suction with ZeroTangle 4.0 anti-tangle (100% pet-hair pickup, 0% tangles on 7-inch hair). PowerBoost GaN fast-charging restores 13% in 3 minutes for 200+ min effective runtime, and AGENT YIKO 2.0 handles voice, scheduling and adaptive cleaning. Matter, live video and TruEdge 3.0 edge cleaning included. US price $1,499.
brush_type: Anti-tangle main brush + Quick-clean Scraper Ring

name: Deebot T90 Pro Omni
desc: The Ecovacs Deebot T90 Pro Omni (CES 2026) brings the 26 cm OZMO Roller 3.0 self-washing mop and fast PowerBoost charging to a more accessible tier, with an automated Omni Station designed to cut maintenance.

name: Omni S2
desc: The Eufy Omni S2 is Eufy's (Anker) 2026 flagship robot vacuum-mop, a CES 2026 Home Appliance honoree built around long-lasting suction and roller-mop mopping. Its AeroTurbo 2.0 system delivers up to 30,000 Pa (100 AW) with multi-cyclone separation to hold suction over time, paired with a DuoSpiral split main brush and extending side brush for anti-tangle pet-hair pickup (perfect 7-inch hair test). The HydroJet 2.0 self-cleaning roller mop scrubs at 240 RPM with 15 N pressure using electrolyzed water, lifting up to 2 inches to keep carpets dry. CleanMind AI navigation (3D MatrixEye ToF + RGB camera) recognises 200+ obstacles down to ~1 cm, crosses 42 mm thresholds, and earned a flawless 24/24 obstacle test. The 12-in-1 UniClean station auto-empties to a 2.5 L bag (~68 days), hot-washes mops at 140°F, hot-air dries, refills, dispenses detergent, and sterilises with electrolyzed water (99.9% germ reduction). A built-in fragrance diffuser freshens rooms for up to 120 hours, and it's compatible with Eufy's MarsWalker stair-climbing platform for multi-floor cleaning. Matter, Alexa and Google supported. US price $1,599.

name: Mobius 60
desc: The MOVA Mobius 60 is the 2026 flagship robot vacuum-mop from MOVA (a Dreame sub-brand), the centerpiece of MOVA's CES 2026 lineup and its first model with an automatic mop-swapping dock. Its headline MopSwap system stores three specialized pads — ThermoHold (phase-change heat-lock for greasy kitchens), Plush (soft fibres for delicate wood floors) and HyperClean (all-around) — and swaps them automatically by cleaning zone to cut cross-contamination. It delivers a class-leading 30,000 Pa suction with a Dynamic Suction Retention baffle that seals over carpet for deep pickup, a TroboWave DuoBrush triple anti-tangle system (99.99% hair removal), and spinning mop pads at 12 N / 260 RPM with 10.5 mm carpet lift. StepMaster 2.0 robotic legs clear thresholds up to 80 mm, while FlexScope navigation uses a retractable dToF LiDAR plus AI SmartSight structured-light 3D scanner (240+ objects, LED fill light) — the turret drops to 89.5 mm to slip under low furniture and rises for panoramic mapping. The all-in-one dock auto-empties to a 3.2 L bag, refills, hot-washes pads at 100°C with JetSpray drying and UV sterilisation. Raw power and obstacle avoidance are top-tier (though real-world cleaning is around average and it's loud at 78 dB max). US price $1,599 (often ~$1,299).

name: X60 Max Ultra Complete
desc: The Dreame X60 Max Ultra Complete is Dreame's 2026 flagship robot vacuum-mop, unveiled at CES 2026 and ranked #1 overall by Vacuum Wars on launch. Its headline trick is a 3.13-inch (79.5 mm) ultra-slim body — Dreame's lowest-profile robot — that still climbs thresholds up to 88 mm via retractable robotic legs (ProLeap 2.0). It pairs 35,000 Pa of suction (through a retractable-plate sealed DuoBrush chamber) with dual AI cameras, retractable LiDAR and Proactive Illumination for 280+ object recognition down to 1 cm. Mopping uses dual spinning pads at 15 N pressure with 40°C warm water and a class-leading 21.5 mm mop lift plus an extending edge mop, scoring 89% carpet deep-clean and a rare 100% pet-hair pickup. The 10-in-1 dock self-empties (3.2 L, ~100 days), washes mops with 100°C water, hot-air dries, auto-refills and dispenses dual cleaning solutions. A 6,400 mAh battery gives ~180 min runtime (fast-charge 9-80% in 80 min) at a quiet 55 dB. Matter, Alexa/Siri/Google, pet care and rich app control round it out. US price $1,699.99.

name: PowerDetect UV Reveal
mop_type: HyperSonic mopping (7× scrubbing vs Matrix); flat pad extends to side
navigation: NeuroNav AI (RGB sensors + lasers + UltraRange camera)
desc: The Shark PowerDetect UV Reveal (model RV3020XE) is SharkNinja's 2026 flagship robot vacuum-mop and the first robot engineered with a UV light to detect invisible stains — UV Stain Detect spots sticky spills and dried-on pet messes, then concentrates HyperSonic mopping (a vibrating pad scrubbing ~100 times per minute, 7x the scrubbing power of earlier Sharks) to remove them. Its PowerDetect suite of sensors (Dirt, Edge, Floor, Stain, Obstacle) auto-adjusts suction, scrubbing and navigation in real time, while NeverStuck technology uses chassis lift to clear higher thresholds and raise the mop to protect carpets. NeuroNav AI mapping pairs RGB sensors, lasers and an UltraRange camera for obstacle avoidance (a best-ever 20/24 for a Shark robot). The bagless NeverTouch ThermaCharged Pro dock auto-empties (~60 days), self-refills, hot-washes the mop at 185°F and dries at 175°F, removing 99.99% of bacteria from the pad. Vacuuming scored 88% carpet deep-clean with strong pet-hair pickup; the main trade-offs are heavy mopping water use and single-floor mapping. US price $1,299.99.
mop_lift: Yes (auto-lift on carpet; auto-park in base)
stain_detection: UV Reveal (UV light exposes biological residue)

name: EksoNR
desc: The clinical standard for rehabilitation walking. EksoNR’s SmartAssist software adapts help to each patient, and it was the first exoskeleton FDA-cleared for stroke and acquired brain injury, later expanded to SCI and MS.

name: Ekso Indego Personal
desc: Notable for being modular and light: Indego breaks into five pieces that assemble around a seated user, weighs ~12 kg, and is FDA-cleared for both clinical rehabilitation and personal use. Originally developed at Vanderbilt University.

name: EksoEVO
desc: A passive industrial vest, not a powered medical device. Ekso EVO supports raised arms using spring tension — no motors or battery — transferring overhead-work load to the hips. Widely deployed in automotive and aerospace assembly.

name: ReWalk Personal 6.0
desc: The best-known personal exoskeleton, commercially available since 2012. The 6th-generation ReWalk Personal is custom-built to each user’s measurements, drops the shoulder backpack of earlier models, and reaches 0.71 m/s — the fastest of any exoskeleton of its era. FDA-cleared and adopted by the US Department of Veterans Affairs.
actuator_type: Electric hip + knee actuation, tilt-sensor gait triggering
control_method: Tilt-sensor gait initiation from center-of-gravity shifts (crutches required)

name: ReStore
desc: A lightweight soft exosuit rather than a rigid frame. ReStore uses textile components and a cable-driven actuator to assist ankle movement during post-stroke gait therapy, making it one of the lightest clinical rehabilitation exoskeletons. FDA-cleared in 2019.
actuator_type: Soft exo-suit, powered ankle plantarflexion assist

name: HAL (Hybrid Assistive Limb)
desc: The original wearable cyborg. Cyberdyne’s HAL reads faint bioelectric (EMG) signals on the skin before the muscle moves, then drives powered hip and knee joints to assist — the medical lower-limb suit weighs ~23 kg, runs ~2h40m per charge, and was the first robot certified to the ISO 13482 personal-care safety standard. FDA-cleared in the US in 2018.

name: Cray X
desc: The first fully connected industrial exoskeleton. The 5th-generation Cray X is a carbon-fiber power suit giving up to 30 kg of lift support plus active walking assistance, running a full 8-hour shift on hot-swappable 40 V batteries. IP54-rated, it streams ergonomic telemetry to German Bionic’s AI and is used at BMW, IKEA and DPD.
use_cases: Industrial lifting injury prevention (BMW, IKEA, DPD)
assist_force: Up to 30 kg (66 lb) per lift
control_method: Dual servo motors, AI-adaptive (Smart Safety Companion)

name: Apogee
desc: German Bionic’s 6th-generation suit, leaner and lighter than the Cray X, with dual-motor support for lifting (up to 30 kg) and walking. The Apogee Ultra shown at CES 2025 pushes assist to 80 lb (36 kg), targeting baggage handling, construction and nursing.

name: Atalante X
desc: The first crutchless self-balancing walking exoskeleton. Atalante X balances itself across 12 powered joints, freeing the patient’s hands entirely during gait therapy. CE-marked, deployed in rehab clinics across Europe and the US.
actuator_type: 12 powered joints (hips, knees, ankles), self-balancing dynamic walking

name: Eve
desc: Eve is Wandercraft's personal exoskeleton — billed as the world's first self-balancing exoskeleton for personal use that works hands-free, without crutches or a walker. Built by the Paris-based robotics firm (founded 2012, 30+ patents) on the same proven platform as its FDA-cleared Atalante X rehabilitation system, Eve has a fully powered lower body with 12 actuated degrees of freedom across the hips, knees and ankles, using AI-driven dynamic balance to let people with severe mobility impairments — such as spinal cord injuries or MS — stand and walk in everyday settings. Users typically need about five training sessions. Unveiled as a prototype in 2023, Eve entered clinical trials in 2025 (including at the James J. Peters VA Medical Center and the Kessler Institute) and was carried in the 2024 Paris Olympic torch relay; commercial availability is targeted for around 2026, backed by a strategic partnership with Renault Group.

name: X-ble Shoulder
desc: Hyundai's X-ble Shoulder is a passive industrial wearable that supports overhead work, reducing shoulder-muscle load; part of Hyundai Robotics' wearable robot line (alongside earlier VEX/CEX) aimed at factory ergonomics.

name: MATE-XT
desc: A passive, batteryless shoulder exoskeleton from Comau weighing ~3 kg. MATE-XT mirrors arm movements with spring support across 8 levels and resists dust, UV and water for outdoor use in agriculture, construction and shipbuilding.

name: Paexo Shoulder
desc: One of the lightest industrial exoskeletons at just 1.9 kg. Ottobock’s Paexo Shoulder is passive, transferring the weight of raised arms from the shoulders to the hips during overhead assembly. Deployed at Volkswagen.
control_method: Mechanical weight transfer to hips (no battery)

name: MyoPro
desc: A powered arm brace controlled by the wearer’s own body. MyoPro reads EMG signals from a weakened arm and drives a powered elbow and hand to complete the intended motion.
control_method: EMG signals from the wearer’s own arm

name: Ascend
desc: A featherweight exoskeleton that runs on air. Roam’s Ascend uses lightweight pneumatic actuation instead of motors, sensing movement to assist the knee — aimed at osteoarthritis and general mobility.

name: Carbonhand
desc: A soft robotic glove that adds strength to a human grip. Carbonhand’s fingertip sensors detect grasping, then artificial tendons add up to ~20% more force — used medically for weak hands and industrially to prevent strain.
control_method: Fingertip pressure sensors + artificial tendons (SEM technology)

name: REX
desc: A self-supporting exoskeleton that stands on its own — no crutches required. REX bears its full weight independently and is joystick-driven, letting users with significant paralysis stand, walk and exercise hands-free.
actuator_type: Self-supporting powered legs, joystick control (no crutches)

name: Stretch 3
desc: Hello Robot's Stretch 3 is a lightweight (~24.5 kg) mobile manipulator built for research and assistive robotics - a wheeled base with a telescoping lift arm and dexterous wrist/gripper, fully ROS 2 native. Designed for in-home and lab manipulation studies at a fraction of the cost of traditional research arms.

name: Husky UGV
desc: The Clearpath Husky is a rugged medium-sized unmanned ground vehicle widely used in robotics research (including Mars robotics work at NASA/MIT). Large payload and power capacity, all-terrain differential drive, fully ROS 2 supported - the go-to outdoor research UGV.

name: Jackal UGV
desc: The Clearpath Jackal is a compact, weatherproof unmanned ground vehicle with onboard computer, GPS and IMU, used for outdoor autonomy, mapping and demining research. Comprehensive ROS API; popular in academia.

name: Dingo
desc: The Clearpath Dingo is a lightweight indoor mobile robot for research and education, available in differential or omnidirectional drive, used for navigation, mobile manipulation and mapping studies.

name: Ridgeback
desc: The Clearpath Ridgeback is an indoor omnidirectional mobile base designed to carry manipulators and heavy payloads, using mecanum-style wheels for precise forward, lateral and twisting motion - a common base for mobile-manipulation research.

name: Warthog UGV
desc: The Clearpath Warthog is a large amphibious all-terrain UGV for rugged outdoor research - capable on land, mud, snow and water - with high payload and ROS support for field robotics.

name: TurtleBot 4
desc: TurtleBot 4 is the world's leading low-cost open-source ROS 2 mobile robot, built on iRobot's Create 3 base with a Raspberry Pi 4, 2D LiDAR and OAK-D camera. The de-facto entry platform for learning ROS 2; available in Lite and Standard.

name: TurtleBot 3
desc: TurtleBot 3 (ROBOTIS, 2017) is a small, affordable, highly modular ROS mobile robot for education and research, available in Burger and Waffle Pi variants, with 360° LiDAR and Dynamixel actuators - a SLAM/navigation learning staple.

name: Human Support Robot (HSR)
desc: Toyota's Human Support Robot (HSR) is a compact, cylindrical mobile manipulator with a folding arm and omnidirectional base, developed for assistive and human-support research. It anchors the RoboCup@Home Domestic Standard Platform League.
cameras: RGB-D head camera + stereo + wide-angle cameras

name: Fetch
desc: The Fetch mobile manipulator (Fetch Robotics, now Zebra) pairs a round mobile base with a 7-DOF arm and adjustable-height torso, widely used in manipulation and warehouse-automation research; typically paired with the Freight base-only platform.

name: PR2
desc: The Willow Garage PR2 (Personal Robot 2) was the seminal dual-arm mobile-manipulation research platform that catalysed the ROS ecosystem. Two 7-DOF arms, an omnidirectional base and rich sensing - hugely influential, now discontinued but historically pivotal.

name: iCub
desc: An open-source, child-size humanoid testbed for embodied-cognition and AI research, designed by the EU-funded RobotCub Consortium (2004–2009) and built by the Italian Institute of Technology in Genoa. About 104 cm and 22 kg, iCub has 53 actuated degrees of freedom — 7 per arm, 9 per hand (across 19 underactuated joints), 6 per leg, plus torso, neck and eyes — and a rich sensor suite: stereo camera eyes, microphones, IMU, joint force/torque sensors and a capacitive tactile skin of ~2,000 sensing points. It runs Debian Linux with the YARP middleware and is fully open-source under GPL. Roughly 30 iCubs are in labs worldwide; a jet-powered flying variant (iRonCub) has even been explored.
actuator_type: Kollmorgen RBE brushless motors + harmonic drives; cable drives; SEA in knee/ankle; tendon-driven hands
frame_material: Ergal aluminium alloy, steel and plastic
chipset: Onboard Intel Core 2 Duo + PC104 (CAN-bus to motor/sensor boards); off-board 30–40-core cluster
power_source: Umbilical (power + Gigabit Ethernet); battery backpack on 2.5+
manufacturer_history: RobotCub Consortium (EU FP6, €8.5M, 2004–2010), coordinated by Giulio Sandini & Giorgio Metta at IIT; first release 2008. Software middleware YARP ('Yet Another Robot Platform').

name: ALOHA 2 (Stationary)
desc: Trossen's ALOHA platform (based on the Stanford ALOHA project) is a low-cost bimanual teleoperation-and-imitation-learning system using paired leader/follower WidowX arms - a key platform for robot-learning and dexterous-manipulation research.

name: Reachy 2
desc: A fully open-source bimanual humanoid from France's Pollen Robotics (acquired by Hugging Face in April 2025), launched October 2024 as a body for embodied-AI research. Reachy 2 stands 136–166 cm, weighs 50 kg, and pairs two 7-DoF bio-inspired arms — built on Pollen's Orbita 2D/3D compliant joints — each lifting ~3 kg through a parallel torque-controlled gripper. An expressive head (asymmetric eyes and antennas) plus stereo RGB, an Orbbec RGB-D and a ToF sensor give rich perception, and a three-omniwheel mobile base with RPLIDAR S2 handles navigation. VR teleoperation runs at ~125 ms glass-to-glass latency; the platform is ROS2-based with a Python SDK, LeRobot and MuJoCo/Gazebo support, and ships in single/dual-arm and stationary/mobile configurations. 100+ deployed across 20 countries.
cameras: 2x IMX296 global-shutter RGB (stereo) + Orbbec Gemini 336 RGB-D + Luxonis OAK ToF

name: Nova Carter
desc: Nova Carter is NVIDIA's reference autonomous mobile robot for research and development on Isaac, integrating the Nova Orin sensor/compute architecture (multi-camera, LiDAR) for mapping, navigation and embodied-AI experimentation.

name: Stuntronics
desc: An autonomous, self-correcting aerial-performer robot — effectively a robotic stunt double — from Walt Disney Imagineering, built to make superhero characters fly in park attractions. Slung from a wire like a trapeze artist, the ~90 lb humanoid figure (three body sections joined by two flexible, pneumatically actuated joints) reads its own motion in mid-air with an onboard accelerometer/gyroscope IMU and three laser rangefinders, then tucks or untucks to control its rotation, pose and centre of mass — nailing flips, twists and even a quintuple somersault before sticking a targeted, feet-first landing in a heroic pose. It grew out of Imagineering's BRICK and Stickman research projects and has been used as a flying Spider-Man double at Avengers Campus.
capabilities: Flips, twists, tucked landing, mid-air heroic poses (to quintuple somersault)

name: Vyloo
desc: A set of three small, autonomous animatronic alien creatures (the avian Vyloo from Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2) from Walt Disney Imagineering's 'Automatronics' / Autonomous Characters research — among Disney's first park animatronics that actually respond to and interact with guests rather than looping a scripted show. Perched on a self-contained log/pod in the queue of Guardians of the Galaxy - Mission: BREAKOUT! at Disney California Adventure, each Vyloo has its own personality driven by decision-making algorithms (how long to hold eye contact, how fast to turn its head, whether to 'fall asleep'). Cameras and sensors let them track whether guests look at or talk to them and follow people with their gaze, conveying mood through simple 'squash-and-stretch' gestures, head cocks and kissy faces. Everything runs onboard, making them unusually modular. First shown ~2018 under the project name 'Tiny Life'.
ai_model: Personality algorithms + animation blending + computer vision
behavior: Squash-and-stretch, head cocking, gaze-following, kissy faces
deployed_at: Guardians of the Galaxy - Mission: BREAKOUT! (Disney California Adventure)

name: RoboCoaster
desc: A passenger-carrying amusement ride built from a KUKA industrial robot arm — the concept was invented by Gino De-Gol (RoboCoaster Ltd, England) and realised with KUKA in 2001 from the adapted KR500 robot, debuting in 2002 with ten units sold to Legoland Denmark. A gondola of two to four seats is mounted to the wrist of a 6-axis arm, giving riders full six-degrees-of-freedom motion (360-degree pitch, yaw and roll well beyond a normal hexapod motion base) at up to ~2 g. Riders pick their own intensity from level 1 (gentle single-axis rotation) to level 5 (wild, inverted), and multiple stored motion profiles can be swapped at the press of a button. KUKA's certified passenger robots (KR 600 R2830 for up to 3 riders, KR 700 R2510 for up to 4) are TUV-certified to EN 13814 with redundant PLe brakes and optical encoders sampling arm position every 32 ms. Deployed in theme parks, VR motion simulators (RoboSim 4-D) and dark rides worldwide, including Epcot's 'Sum of All Thrills'.

name: Kime
desc: A humanoid robotic bartender/barista from Spain's Macco Robotics (Seville). Kime stands about two meters tall with dual articulating arms that pour a beer in under 8 seconds and mix a cocktail in around 30 — up to ~120 drinks an hour across beers, cocktails, juices and soft drinks. It engages customers by touchscreen (and mobile-app ordering) in their preferred language, takes cashless payments, and wears an antimicrobial, food-grade shell with automated cleaning routines. Built for 'plug-and-play' integration with existing bar equipment and offered with swappable beverage modules and custom branding, it's aimed at bars, restaurants, events and promotional activations. The current v5 was demonstrated in Seville hospitality trials in 2026.

name: Cecilia
desc: Billed as the world's first interactive robotic bartender, Cecilia.ai (from Israel's GKI hospitality-tech group) is an arcade-console-sized kiosk about seven feet tall, fronted by a large touchscreen showing a 3D-animated female bartender who chats, tells jokes, recommends drinks and displays promos when idle. Guests order by voice (contactless) or touchscreen; conversational AI with voice recognition — scripted plus machine learning — keeps the banter going, in up to 40 languages. Behind the screen, an articulating arm dispenses precisely measured pours from 12 ingredient containers (~70 L total) to make up to 120 cocktails an hour, delivered through a slot. It can't garnish or make ice, but adds brandable side LEDs (disco mode included), cashless payment, and a business-intelligence dashboard of popular drinks and peak times. Seen at stadiums, airport and VIP lounges, cruises and events.

name: EX Robots Humanoid Android
desc: A series of hyper-realistic humanoid androids from China's EX Robots (Dalian Tiasi Technology Development Co.), known for their lifelike human appearance. A mechanical metal body is wrapped in 3D-printed silicone skin over the face, hands and feet, and micro-motor actuators drive both the flexible joints and the facial 'muscles' to reproduce nuanced expressions, eye contact and gestures. Patented joint designs give an extensive range of motion. Control is via preset behaviour programs, smartphone/tablet apps and guided modes, with onboard cameras and microphones for perception and voice interaction. EX Robots is pioneering mass-production of customisable androids for service, entertainment, rescue and science-education roles.

name: GoBe
desc: GoBe (Blue Ocean Robotics) is an enterprise telepresence robot with autonomous navigation, HD video and a tall display, marketed around cutting business travel and CO2 - each unit can offset several tons of travel emissions per user annually. Used in offices, factories and healthcare.
use_cases: Telepresence for offices, healthcare & education (autonomous navigation + mapping)

name: OhmniCare
desc: OhmniCare (OhmniLabs, now part of Symbotic) is a healthcare-focused telepresence robot that replaced the original Ohmni in 2024, with a fully emotive neck, 4K video and one-click connection, designed for remote clinical rounds, tele-nursing and patient consults.
use_cases: Healthcare telepresence — remote patient visits & senior care

name: A2
desc: The AMY Robotics A2 is an autonomous-navigation telepresence robot with an adjustable-height display, HD camera and obstacle avoidance, used for remote office presence, healthcare rounds and remote inspection.
use_cases: Healthcare & office telepresence with autonomous navigation

name: PadBot P3
desc: The PadBot P3 (Inbot Technology) is a mid-size telepresence robot with a built-in HD display and camera (no tablet required), remote-driveable via app for home, office and education remote-presence use.

name: Ballie
desc: Ballie is Samsung's bright-yellow rolling home AI companion, powered by Google Gemini and Samsung's own models. It holds natural conversations, controls smart-home devices, greets visitors, projects content via a built-in projector, and checks on pets/family with front 4K and rear 2K cameras. Launch slated for 2026.

name: Q9 (CLOi AI Agent)
desc: LG's 'Self-Driving AI Home Hub' — a cute companion robot that rolls around the house on two gyroscopic one-wheeled legs, balancing itself while it moves. With bright expressive eyes, cameras, a microphone array and generative-AI voice conversation, Q9 acts as a mobile personal assistant and the physical face of LG's ThinQ smart home: it greets and chats with the family, reports on overnight energy use, sleep and temperature, delivers weather and reminders, and relays commands to LG appliances. LG frames it around 'Affectionate Intelligence' — AI meant to understand and empathize with users — and offers it on a subscription model. It's the forerunner to LG's CLOiD home humanoid (CES 2026).

name: Ropet
desc: A furry, big-eyed AI companion pet from Mengyou Intelligence — the first product from a company founded by He Jiabin, former head of ByteDance's PICO Beijing ID design team — launched via Kickstarter in late 2024 and shown at CES 2025. Ropet loves being stroked and reacts to voice, touch and gestures with cute animated-eye expressions and sounds. Cameras, microphones and sensors give it facial recognition (it knows its owner and reacts to your expressions), a 'mood radar', and the ability to recognise foods and objects held up to its face (dangle a toy hotdog and hotdogs flash across its eyes). ChatGPT integration makes it optionally conversational in 50+ languages, and its interchangeable fur, faces, eye colours and accessories make each one customisable.
customization: Interchangeable fur / face, eye colours, accessories

name: Moflin
desc: Moflin (Casio) is a small fluffy mood-syncing companion robot that uses emotional AI to develop a unique personality and bond with its owner over time, responding to handling with sounds and movement. ~5 h battery; aimed at stress relief and comfort.

name: Mirumi
desc: A palm-sized, furry companion robot from Tokyo's Yukai Engineering (the studio behind Qoobo and Nekojita FuFu), shown at CES 2025. Mirumi clips onto a bag handle or strap and does exactly one thing charmingly: it turns its single rotating head to 'peek' at nearby people. Using an internal IMU and a distance sensor, it scans its surroundings and, once it notices someone, fixes them with an innocent baby-like gaze — then acts bashful and hides its face, or gives a little bow when petted. Inspired by the warm feeling of catching a cute baby's eye in public, it has no voice or app; its whole purpose is to spark small moments of shared joy with strangers on a train or in a queue.
interaction: Touch + motion reactive (peeks, eye contact, bashful hiding, bows; no voice)

name: EMO
desc: EMO (Living.ai) is a desktop AI companion pet with 1,000+ expressions and movements; it tracks voices, recognises up to 10 people and objects, navigates the desk without falling, plays music and games, and acts as a small smart-home helper.
cameras: HD wide-angle camera (face recognition, up to 10 people) + 4-mic array

name: Jennie
desc: A hyper-realistic robotic Labrador puppy from Tombot, created after founder Tom Stevens had to rehome his mother's dog when she developed Alzheimer's. Designed with Jim Henson's Creature Shop, Jennie has soft realistic fur and lifelike head, eyebrow and tail motion driven by nine servo motors, with capacitive touch sensors across its body that trigger puppy-like reactions based on where and how it's touched, and authentic sounds recorded from 8–10-week-old Labradors. A microphone array lets it understand simple commands (tell it to 'speak' and it barks). Deliberately screen-free and low-tech, it's aimed at comfort for people with dementia, anxiety or sensory-processing needs; Tombot returned to CES 2026 positioning Jennie as an FDA-regulated robotic pet for clinical and long-term-care use, with 7,500+ preorders.

name: Astro
desc: Amazon Astro is a wheeled home robot combining Alexa, autonomous navigation, a periscope camera and visual/voice recognition for home monitoring, security patrols and companionship. Sold by invitation; positioned as a mobile household assistant.

name: B2-W
desc: The wheeled variant of Unitree's flagship B2 industrial quadruped, adding driven wheels for 6 m/s rolling speed on flat ground while retaining legged stair-climbing and rough-terrain ability. Built for logistics, security patrol and inspection, with heavy payload, long endurance and 5G/Wi-Fi connectivity.
actuator_type: Unitree QDD joint motors (360 N·m) + 12-inch pneumatic wheels (50 N·m)
npu: Optional NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX (up to 3 modules)

name: X30
desc: DEEP Robotics' flagship IP67-rated inspection quadruped for harsh, GPS-denied environments such as utility tunnels and substations. Adds higher perception density, longer endurance and all-weather operation over the X20, with multi-LiDAR SLAM, RGB/thermal imaging and auto-charge docks for round-the-clock patrols.

name: Lite3
desc: A compact, affordable quadruped aimed at universities and labs for locomotion, SLAM and reinforcement-learning research. Ships in Basic, Venture, Pro and LiDAR builds with ROS2-ready interfaces and open SDKs for rapid prototyping.
actuator_type: High-torque QDD joint modules (+50% torque density)
chipset: RK3588 (motion host) + NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX (perception, Pro/LiDAR)
estop: Soft e-stop (roll/pitch limit, overtemp, fall-down protection)

name: X20
desc: An IP66-rated industrial quadruped for all-weather autonomous inspection and public-safety patrol in substations, cable tunnels and hazardous sites. Configurable with sirens, beacons, dual-spectrum gimbals and two-way audio, with multi-LiDAR SLAM and auto-charge docks for continuous duty.

name: AlphaDog
desc: A consumer-focused 5G robot dog from Nanjing-based Weilan Intelligent Technology, marketed as the fastest robodog on the market at around 15 km/h. Full-metal legs and reinforcement-learning-based control let it adjust stride and height to terrain, climb stairs and recover balance. Sold in consumer C-Series and larger enterprise E-Series inspection variants.

name: B1
desc: The Unitree B1 was Unitree's first industrial-grade quadruped with IP68 protection and ~20 kg payload, used for inspection in harsh environments. Superseded by the more capable B2.
payload: 20 kg walking (250 kg static stair demo)
use_cases_note: Industrial inspection/patrol — Unitree's first waterproof industrial platform

name: FIFISH V-EVO
desc: The QYSEA FIFISH V-EVO is a prosumer underwater drone with full 360° omnidirectional movement, a 4K UHD 60 FPS camera, AI Vision Lock subject tracking, 5,000-lumen lights and FPV goggle control - rated to ~100 m for inspection, filming and research.
use_cases_note: Entry omnidirectional 4K drone (V6 lineage)

name: Explorer
desc: The Saildrone Explorer is a wind-and-solar-powered uncrewed surface vehicle with 12+ months of endurance, used for ocean-data collection, bathymetric mapping, fisheries and maritime-domain awareness with a minimal carbon footprint.
endurance: Up to 12 months at sea autonomous
sensors: Meteorological + oceanographic suite (ADCP, CTD, cameras, AIS)
achievements: First autonomous circumnavigation of Antarctica (2019); hurricane eye penetration (2021)
use_cases_note: Ocean data collection — NOAA/science/defense fleets

name: Surveyor
desc: The Saildrone Surveyor is a large (~20 m) uncrewed surface vessel for deep-ocean bathymetric and acoustic mapping - one mission mapped ~90,000 km² of deep water - offering ship-grade survey at a fraction of crewed-vessel cost.
use_cases: Autonomous ocean-floor mapping (multibeam sonar to 7,000 m)
sensors: Deep-water multibeam echosounder (seafloor mapping to full ocean depth), ADCP, met/ocean suite
use_cases_note: Autonomous hydrographic/bathymetric survey

name: X3
desc: The Blueye X3 is a professional underwater drone (ROV) with three guest ports for sensors/tooling (grippers, sonar, lasers), HD camera and ~305 m depth rating, used for inspection, aquaculture and research.
use_cases: Research & aquaculture (3 guest ports: sonar, grippers, sensors)

name: iBubble
desc: iBubble (Notilo Plus) is a wireless autonomous underwater camera drone that follows and films a diver hands-free using acoustic tracking, rated to ~60 m - aimed at recreational and professional dive filming.

name: M2 Pro
desc: The Chasing M2 Pro is a versatile underwater ROV with omnidirectional movement, 4K camera and accessory mounts (grabber arm, sonar), rated to ~150 m, used for filming, inspection and light recovery.
use_cases: Industrial underwater inspection to 150 m depth

name: BIKI
desc: BIKI (Robosea) is a compact bionic fish-shaped underwater drone that swims with a tail fin for quiet, low-disturbance filming, with a 4K camera and ~60 m depth rating - a consumer-oriented bionic aquatic robot.

name: Thermite RS3
desc: The Howe & Howe Thermite RS3 is a remote firefighting robot on industrial tank treads - 24 hp diesel, climbs ~70 deg slopes, and blasts up to ~2,500 gal/min of water or foam. Built for refinery, HAZMAT and industrial fires (BLEVEs).

name: Thermite RS1
desc: The Howe & Howe Thermite RS1 is a compact remote firefighting robot on tank treads with a diesel powerplant, designed to enter structures and industrial fires too dangerous for crews and deliver high-volume water/foam streams.

name: EMILY
desc: EMILY (Hydronalix) is a ~4-ft, ~12 kg remote-controlled rescue flotation robot reaching ~10 m/s (23 mph), used to reach drowning victims fast; it helped rescue 240+ refugees off the Greek coast and can act as a flotation platform for several people.

name: Velox
desc: Velox (Pliant Energy Systems) is an amphibious robot propelled by undulating silicone fins, able to swim, skate on ice and push through snow - suited to cold-water and ice rescues where humans cannot safely approach.
use_cases: Amphibious operations: swims, crawls, traverses ice & sand

name: Sigma
desc: Fotokite Sigma is a fully-autonomous tethered drone for first responders that launches from a vehicle and holds persistent aerial thermal/visual overwatch of an incident, giving commanders continuous situational awareness without a trained pilot.
feature: Persistent thermal/visual overwatch; no pilot needed
use_cases: Persistent aerial situational awareness for first responders (24 h flight, no pilot licence)

name: Snakebot
desc: The CMU Snakebot (Biorobotics Lab) is a many-jointed serpentine robot that crawls and climbs through rubble and pipes inaccessible to people or dogs - deployed after the 2017 Mexico City earthquake and used for infrastructure inspection.
use_cases: Search & rescue in rubble, pipes & confined spaces

name: MV-4
desc: The DOK-ING MV-4 is a compact remote-controlled demining machine using a flail/tiller to safely detonate and clear landmines, widely deployed for humanitarian mine clearance in former conflict zones.

name: TAF 35
desc: The Magirus TAF 35 is a remote-controlled tracked firefighting robot with a large turbine that atomises and projects water/foam at high volume over long distances - for tunnel fires, industrial blazes and scenarios too hazardous for crews.

name: Dino
desc: The Naïo Dino is a large-scale autonomous weeding robot for vegetable farms, straddling beds to mechanically remove weeds with interchangeable tools, RTK-GPS guided and fully electric.
use_cases: Autonomous mechanical weeding for vegetable row crops

name: MK-V
desc: The Monarch MK-V is a 70 hp fully-electric driver-optional smart tractor: up to ~14 h battery (5-6 h recharge), IP65, 4WD, swappable battery packs and onboard power outlets, with camera-based autonomy and per-acre data collection. Suited to vineyards, orchards, dairy and solar-farm vegetation management; cuts ~2 t CO2/year on a 50-acre farm.

name: Solix Ag Robot
desc: The Solinftec Solix is a lightweight, solar-powered, 100% autonomous field robot that scouts crops (corn, soy, wheat, cotton), detects pests and disease, and applies targeted spot-spraying - reportedly cutting herbicide use by up to ~98%.

name: ARA
desc: The Ecorobotix ARA is an ultra-high-precision smart sprayer with six cameras and 156 nozzles achieving ~6x6 cm spray resolution, applying plant-by-plant microdoses and cutting chemical use by 70-95%. Tractor-towed, with 20+ crop-specific AI algorithms.
use_cases: AI plant-by-plant precision spraying (6 m boom, ~6x6 cm targeting)

name: FD20
desc: The FarmDroid FD20 is a fully solar-powered autonomous robot that both seeds and mechanically weeds row crops. It records each seed's RTK-GPS position (8 mm) at sowing, so it can weed between and within rows before plants even emerge. ~1,250 kg (low soil compaction), 18-24 h/day CO2-neutral operation, ~6 ha/day, 50+ crop types; the +Spray option cuts chemicals up to 94%.

name: E-Series
desc: The Agrobot E-Series is an AI-vision strawberry-harvesting robot with up to 24 independent robotic arms that identify ripe berries and pick them with ~1 cm tolerance, avoiding unripe fruit and minimising bruising for premium markets.
actuator_type: Up to 24 independent picking arms with AI ripeness vision

name: Astronaut A5
desc: The Lely Astronaut A5 is an automatic (robotic) milking system that lets cows be milked voluntarily on demand; a robotic arm with 3D laser-guided teat detection attaches the cups while the system tracks per-cow yield and health data.

name: Origin
desc: The Cruise Origin (GM) was a purpose-built, steering-wheel-free shared robotaxi. Development was wound down after GM ended Cruise's robotaxi program in 2024 - included here as a notable discontinued milestone in the robotaxi category.
use_cases: Shared autonomous ride-hailing (program wound down 2024; design never mass-deployed)

name: Gen-7 Robotaxi
desc: Pony.ai's seventh-generation Robotaxi entered mass production in 2025 - the first to use 100% automotive-grade components with a ~70% lower autonomous-driving-kit BOM. Pony.ai runs fully-driverless service across China's four tier-one cities.
config: Built on GAC & BAIC platforms; automotive-grade
feature: ~70% lower autonomous-kit BOM vs prior gen
cameras: Multi-sensor kit: LiDAR + radar + cameras (100% automotive-grade)
use_cases: Driverless robotaxi (Toyota, GAC & BAIC vehicle platforms, mass production 2025)

name: Autonomous Shuttle (Sienna)
desc: May Mobility operates autonomous microtransit shuttles (Toyota Sienna platform) for on-demand and fixed-route public transit in several US cities, moving toward driver-out L4 operation in defined service zones.
use_cases: Public microtransit shuttle service (multi-passenger autonomous transit)

name: Aurora Driver (Autonomous Truck)
desc: The Aurora Driver is a self-driving system for Class 8 freight trucks; Aurora launched commercial driverless freight runs on Texas highways (Dallas-Houston) in 2025, hauling loads with no human in the cab.
use_cases: Driverless freight (Aurora Horizon subscription; launched commercial driverless 2025)

name: Kodiak Driver
desc: The Kodiak Driver is a self-driving system for long-haul and off-road trucking; Kodiak delivered driverless commercial trucks for customers (including Permian Basin oilfield routes) and focuses on autonomous freight at scale.
use_cases: Driverless freight hauling (vehicle-agnostic, 2.5M+ test miles; Bosch manufacturing partnership)

name: Mission Master SP
desc: Low-profile 8x8 all-electric autonomous UGV (Silent Partner) built for forward and last-mile resupply, silent watch and carriage of section sensors or weapon systems. Weighs 1,134 kg, carries up to 1,000 kg (300 kg amphibious) and reaches 40 km/h, using Rheinmetall's PATH autonomy kit for follow-me, teleoperation and supervised autonomy. Networked with Rheinmetall's soldier system and C2 software; selected for trials by Japan's JGSDF and several NATO armies.

name: Titan
desc: A fully modular hybrid unmanned ground vehicle jointly developed by QinetiQ North America and Estonia's Milrem Robotics, built to 'lighten the load' for dismounted troops. Titan pairs Milrem's THeMIS (Tracked Hybrid Modular Infantry System) mobility base - two tracked drive modules linked by a mission payload frame - with QinetiQ's Tactical Robot Controller (a pocket 6.5-inch controller) and Robotic Applique Kit for autonomy, night-vision/thermal cameras and comms, operable in manned or unmanned modes at line-of-sight ranges over 800 m. It measures about 2.0 x 2.1 x 1.0 m with a curb weight near 907 kg and carries up to ~680 kg (with a 2,000 lb pull force). Its diesel-electric hybrid drive gives ~100 km range / up to 72 h endurance, or a run-silent all-electric mode good for 20+ km over ~2 hours. Its open architecture accepts modules for logistics/resupply, CASEVAC litters, earth-moving, route clearance, CBRN/RSTA and remote weapon stations. It contended in the US Army SMET and UK Dstl Last-Mile Resupply programs.
propulsion: Diesel-electric hybrid (10 kW JP8 generator + AGM/Li-ion)
control: QinetiQ TRC + RAK; manned or unmanned
program: US Army SMET; UK Dstl Last-Mile Resupply

name: Optio-X20
desc: The KNDS/Nexter Optio-X20 is a tracked robotic combat platform (and the Ultro-600 robotic mule sibling) evaluated by European armies for logistics and armed support roles, carrying up to ~600 kg.
use_cases: Remote weapon platform, ISR, cargo (20-tonne class tracked UGV)

name: Ripsaw M5
desc: Fifth-generation Ripsaw — a tracked Robotic Combat Vehicle developed by Team Ripsaw (Textron Systems, Howe & Howe and Teledyne FLIR) for the US Army's RCV-Medium effort. Hybrid diesel-electric drivetrain, flat open architecture and configurable armour, with a 10.5-tonne combat weight, ~3,600 kg payload and 65 km/h top speed. Can mount a Kongsberg MCT-30 turret (30/40 mm Bushmaster), carry the R80D SkyRaider UAS and uses the SUMIT 360° EO/IR perception suite.
use_cases: Robotic combat vehicle (US Army RCV-M candidate)
made_in: USA (Textron Systems / Howe & Howe — Team Lynx)

name: Gereon RCS
desc: The ARX Robotics Gereon RCS is a lightweight tracked UGV for European armed forces, used for logistics, reconnaissance and as a mobile sensor/effector carrier; designed for scalable, software-defined autonomy.
use_cases: Logistics, casualty evacuation, ISR (scalable modular platform)

name: TRX (Tracked Robot 10-ton)
desc: General Dynamics Land Systems' medium-class tracked unmanned ground vehicle, unveiled at AUSA 2021 and entered as GDLS's contender in the US Army's Robotic Combat Vehicle (RCV) program. As its name suggests, the TRX is designed around a 10-ton class: roughly a 5-ton curb weight plus up to a 5-ton payload on a flat modular deck. Because there's no crew to armour, it uses lightweight materials and a hybrid-electric drive that lowers its thermal signature, enables near-silent running and powers onboard electronics, while keeping pace with fast Armoured Brigade Combat Teams. Its open, payload-agnostic architecture lets the Army swap mission modules quickly, and it's built for manned-unmanned teaming as a 'wingman' to crewed vehicles. Derived from GDLS's MUTT program, published mission roles include tactical resupply, counter-UAS/short-range air defence, obstacle breaching, indirect fire, electronic warfare and ISR; a SHORAD variant can autonomously launch and recover small UAS.
uas: Autonomous launch/recovery of small UAS (SHORAD variant)

name: PROBOT
desc: Compact wheeled logistics UGV able to carry around 750 kg of supplies or evacuate casualties while following a squad autonomously or under teleoperation. Built with an open architecture for mission modules including ISR masts, RWS and CBRN sensors, and integrated with Roboteam's control suite shared across its robot family.

name: Skypod
desc: The Exotec Skypod is a goods-to-person warehouse robot that drives on the floor and climbs storage racks up to ~12 m to retrieve bins, combining high-density storage with fast picking. Travels ~4 m/s; deployed by major retailers and 3PLs worldwide.
use_cases: Goods-to-person warehouse fulfillment (climbs racks to 12 m)

name: HaiPick A42
desc: The Hai Robotics HaiPick A42 is an autonomous case-handling robot that retrieves multiple totes/cartons from high racks (up to ~10 m) and delivers them to pick stations, pioneering the ACR category for dense, flexible warehouse storage.

name: Ranger
desc: The GreyOrange Ranger family are goods-to-person and sortation AMRs that move racks or totes to operators, orchestrated by GreyOrange's GreyMatter fulfilment software for retail and e-commerce warehouses.
use_cases: Warehouse goods-to-person & sortation AMR fleet (GreyMatter software)

name: Palion Tow Tractor
desc: The Seegrid Palion Tow Tractor is a vision-guided (camera-based, infrastructure-free) autonomous tow tractor for material movement in manufacturing and warehousing, part of Seegrid's Palion line alongside pallet trucks and lift trucks.

name: Vecna RPL (Robotic Pallet Lift)
desc: Vecna Robotics builds autonomous pallet trucks and tuggers for warehouse material handling, with the Pivotal orchestration platform and a human-in-the-loop remote support model for handling edge cases.

name: MiR1200 Pallet Jack
desc: The MiR1200 Pallet Jack (Mobile Industrial Robots, a Teradyne company) uses AI-powered 3D vision to autonomously locate, pick and deliver pallets, carrying up to ~1,200 kg - extending the MiR AMR line into pallet handling.

name: Pegasus
desc: Amazon Robotics Pegasus is a compact drive unit with a conveyor top that carries individual packages across a sortation floor and tips them into the correct chute, improving package-sorting accuracy in Amazon fulfilment centres.
actuator_type: Drive unit with conveyor top module
use_cases: Package sortation in Amazon fulfillment centers

name: FoxBot
desc: The Fox Robotics FoxBot is an autonomous trailer-unloading forklift that automatically unloads palletised freight from trucks at the dock, addressing one of the most labour-intensive and injury-prone warehouse tasks.
use_cases: Autonomous trailer unloading & dock work (robotic forklift)

name: inVia Picker
desc: The inVia Picker is a goods-to-person robot that autonomously retrieves totes from standard shelving and brings them to pick stations, offered under a robotics-as-a-service model for e-commerce fulfilment.

name: da Vinci 5
desc: The Intuitive da Vinci 5 (FDA-cleared March 2024) is the fifth-generation multiport robotic-assisted surgery system, adding first-of-its-kind Force Feedback, a new 3D display and 150+ enhancements over da Vinci Xi. Used across most surgical specialties; going international through 2025.
key_feature: Force Feedback technology; ~10,000x compute of da Vinci Xi
actuator_type: Force-feedback instrument arms (first in da Vinci line)

name: Ottava
desc: Ottava is Johnson & Johnson MedTech's soft-tissue surgical robot, uniquely integrating four arms into the operating table for a low profile and flexible setup. First US clinical cases (incl. gastric bypass) were completed in 2025, with an FDA submission expected in early 2026.
approach: Four arms integrated into the OR table
regulatory: Investigational - first US clinical cases done; FDA submission expected early 2026
use_cases: Multi-specialty soft-tissue surgery (6 arms integrated into the OR table; clinical trials underway)

name: Maestro
desc: The Moon Surgical Maestro is an accessible surgical-assistance robot that works with standard laparoscopic instruments, adding two robotic arms to hold and position the camera and tools - designed to fit existing OR workflows affordably. FDA-cleared and CE-marked.
key_feature: Two assistive arms that fit existing OR workflow
use_cases: Collaborative laparoscopic surgery (works with existing instruments; FDA-cleared & CE-marked)

name: Mazor X Stealth
desc: The Medtronic Mazor X Stealth Edition is a spine surgical robot combining preoperative planning with robotic guidance and integrated navigation for precise pedicle-screw and implant placement.
use_cases: Robotic-guided spine surgery with StealthStation navigation & predictive analytics

name: Senhance
desc: The Asensus Senhance is a digital laparoscopic surgical system with reusable instruments, haptic force feedback and eye-tracking camera control, aiming to lower per-procedure cost while adding digital intelligence to surgery.
key_feature: Haptic force feedback + eye-tracking camera control
use_cases: Digital laparoscopic surgery with reusable instruments

name: CORI
desc: The Smith+Nephew CORI Surgical System is a compact handheld robotic platform for partial and total knee replacement, using real-time bone mapping (no preoperative CT) and a robotics-assisted bur for precise resurfacing.

name: CyberKnife S7
desc: The Accuray CyberKnife S7 mounts a linear accelerator on a robotic arm to deliver highly targeted radiation to tumours from many angles, with real-time motion tracking that adjusts for patient and tumour movement.
actuator_type: Robotic manipulator with linear accelerator, real-time motion tracking (Synchrony)

name: Monarch Platform
desc: The Monarch Platform (J&J MedTech, originally Auris Health) is a robotic flexible-endoscopy system using a controller-driven scope for peripheral lung biopsy (bronchoscopy) and kidney-stone removal (urology), with navigation guidance.

name: PUDU T300
desc: The PUDU T300 is an industrial-grade autonomous delivery robot for factories and warehouses, carrying heavy loads with high precision and integrating with lifts and automatic doors for end-to-end material flow.

name: PUDU CC1 Pro
desc: The AI-powered edition of Pudu Robotics' flagship commercial floor cleaner — a 4-in-1 robot that sweeps, scrubs, vacuums and dust-mops in a single pass. The Pro adds proactive intelligence: it automatically detects stains and surface changes, adjusts cleaning intensity on the fly, and self-monitors to prevent secondary contamination. Its VSLAM+ and LiDAR fusion navigation maps and cleans complex spaces with no floor QR codes or markers, and it runs up to 8 hours per charge (3-hour recharge) at speeds up to ~1.2 m/s. With 15 L clean and 15 L dirty water tanks (auto fill/empty), autonomous docking and auto dust-tank disposal, and auto-resume after low battery, it's built for hands-off operation in hotels, multifamily housing, schools, offices, gyms and assisted-living facilities. About 629 x 552 x 695 mm and ~75 kg; listed around $24,000 with RaaS/lease options.
navigation: VSLAM+ & LiDAR fusion (PUDU SLAM, no QR codes)

name: HolaBot
desc: The Pudu HolaBot is a heavy-load (~60 kg) delivery and bussing robot with large enclosed shelves, used for food running and dish return in busy restaurants; summoned via call bells and capable of dish-collection cycles.

name: KLEENBOT C30
desc: The KEENON KLEENBOT C30 is a commercial floor-cleaning robot combining sweeping, scrubbing and drying with autonomous navigation for malls, airports and offices.
use_cases: Commercial floor cleaning (sweep, vacuum, dust mop — 61 cm width, 19,000 Pa suction, 2,500 m² per charge)

name: Whiz
desc: The SoftBank Whiz is an autonomous commercial vacuum-sweeping robot (BrainOS-powered) for offices, hotels and retail, learning routes by being driven once then repeating them autonomously; SoftBank's flagship after refocusing from the Pepper humanoid.
use_cases: Commercial vacuum cleaning (up to 1,500 m² per charge)

name: Neo
desc: The flagship of Avidbots (Kitchener, Ontario) and one of the most widely deployed autonomous floor-scrubbing robots — used across airports, warehouses (DHL, DSV) and malls, where it reportedly removes up to 80% of manual cleaning labour hours. Powered by Avidbots Autonomy, Neo maps and cleans a site on its own with dynamic path planning, real-time obstacle avoidance and 360-degree visibility from a market-leading sensor suite, no operator required. It offers a 24 in or 32 in cleaning path with disc or cylindrical heads, a ~132 L (35 gal) solution tank, coverage up to ~3,900 m2/hr, and up to six hours of run time per AGM battery — extendable by simply swapping batteries. It accepts standard low-foaming floor detergents.

name: T7AMR
desc: Tennant Company's autonomous ride-on robotic floor scrubber, built on its T7 micro-rider and made self-driving by Brain Corp's vision-based BrainOS platform (learn-and-repeat routes with real-world obstacle avoidance). It cleans a 650 mm (26 in) path with two 0.45 kW brush motors at 225 rpm and up to 86 kg of down-pressure to lift embedded grime, fed by equal 110 L solution and recovery tanks for theoretical productivity up to 4,250 m2/hr. The 24 V machine runs ~4 hours on lead-acid (up to 6.5 hours on lithium-ion, or a 9.2 kWh Li-Ion pack), cleans as quietly as 70 dBA for daytime use, and uses ec-H2O NanoClean to cut water and detergent. It measures 1650 x 850 x 1450 mm, weighs ~492 kg, and reports fleet KPIs weekly.

name: K5
desc: The Knightscope K5 is a large autonomous outdoor security robot that patrols parking lots, campuses and malls, streaming 360° video, reading licence plates and detecting anomalies, offered on a Robot-as-a-Service subscription.

name: CLOi ServeBot
desc: LG's autonomous serving and delivery robot (model LDLIM21), launched in the US in early 2022 and named one of Time's Best Inventions of 2022 — notable as the world's first commercial service robot to earn UL 3300 safety certification for open, dynamic environments. Standing 1,339 mm tall on a compact 510 x 510 mm footprint, it carries up to 30 kg across three open shelves (10 kg each) and moves at up to 1 m/s, running as long as 11 hours on its 23,000 mAh battery (0-100% in 5 hours). It fuses LiDAR, a 3D camera, ToF and bumper sensors for obstacle avoidance, with a ToF sensor on each shelf so it knows when an item is taken and moves to the next stop. A 9.2-inch touchscreen shows cartoon eye animations and handles setup, voice and music, and cloud connectivity enables remote monitoring and free OTA updates. Used in restaurants, hotels, retail and healthcare.

name: Gen3 Delivery Robot
desc: The Serve Robotics third-generation sidewalk delivery robot (spun out of Uber) runs Level 4 autonomy on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin brain with Ouster LiDAR, ~11 mph top speed, ~14 h battery and ~15 gal insulated cargo (holds 4x 16" pizzas). Serve deployed its 2,000th robot in 2025 across LA, Miami, Dallas, Chicago and Atlanta with Uber Eats and DoorDash.

name: Coco Bot
desc: Coco operates pink insulated sidewalk delivery robots for restaurant orders, using a remote-piloted-plus-autonomy model for safe urban navigation; widely deployed in Los Angeles and other US cities.

name: Delivery Robot
desc: Avride (spun out of Yandex's self-driving group) builds six-wheeled autonomous sidewalk delivery robots deployed with Uber Eats and Grubhub, alongside its autonomous-vehicle work; operates in several US cities.

name: Ottobot Yeti
desc: The Ottonomy Ottobot is a fully-autonomous delivery robot used both indoors (airports, retail) and outdoors (curbside, sidewalk), with contextual-AI navigation and multi-compartment cargo for parcels, food and pharmacy.

name: Neolix Delivery Vehicle
desc: Neolix builds compact driverless delivery vans for last-mile logistics, retail-on-wheels and contactless delivery, deployed at scale across Chinese cities for parcel and grocery distribution.
use_cases: Level-4 urban unmanned delivery vehicle (retail, logistics, vending)

name: Ingenuity
desc: Ingenuity was NASA/JPL's Mars helicopter - the first powered, controlled flight on another planet (Apr 2021). Just 1.8 kg with counter-rotating rotors and solar charging, it flew 72 times over ~3 years (vs a 5-flight plan), covering ~17 km, before rotor-blade damage grounded it in Jan 2024.
achievement: First powered, controlled flight on another planet

name: Nova-C (Odysseus)
desc: The Intuitive Machines Nova-C "Odysseus" was the first US lunar lander since Apollo and the first commercial soft landing on the Moon (IM-1, Feb 2024). A ~1,900 kg hexagonal-cylinder lander (100 kg payload) that touched down near the lunar south pole, tipping on landing but returning data.
achievement: First US lunar landing since Apollo; first commercial soft landing
payload_instruments: SCALPSS, ROLSES, NDL LIDAR, ILO-X, LN-1

name: Astrobee
desc: Astrobee is NASA's system of cube-shaped free-flying robots (Bumble, Honey, Queen) aboard the ISS, using electric impeller fans to fly weightlessly and cameras/sensors to navigate the Kibo module - assisting astronauts and hosting student programming challenges.

name: SORA-Q (LEV-2)
desc: SORA-Q (LEV-2) is JAXA's baseball-sized (~250 g) transformable lunar rover deployed by the SLIM "Moon Sniper" lander (Jan 2024). It splits open into a two-wheeled crawler to image the lander and terrain - co-developed with toy maker Tomy, Sony and Doshisha University.

name: CADRE Rovers
desc: CADRE (Cooperative Autonomous Distributed Robotic Explorers) is a set of small shoebox-sized NASA rovers designed to operate together autonomously as a team on the Moon, demonstrating multi-robot coordination; manifested on the IM-3 mission.
objective: Autonomous multi-robot coordination on the Moon
use_cases: Cooperative multi-robot lunar exploration (3 autonomous shoebox-sized rovers mapping in formation; Intuitive Machines IM-3 delivery)

name: CIMON
desc: CIMON (Crew Interactive Mobile Companion) is a free-floating, AI-powered spherical assistant aboard the ISS, built by Airbus for DLR with IBM Watson voice AI - it talks with astronauts, displays procedures and floats via internal fans.
cameras: Front camera + microphones for crew interaction

name: Canadarm3
desc: Canadarm3 is Canada's AI-enabled robotic system for NASA's Lunar Gateway - a smart, largely autonomous arm (built by MDA) that will maintain, repair and inspect the Gateway station in lunar orbit without constant human control.

name: European Robotic Arm (ERA)
desc: The European Robotic Arm (ERA) is a ~11 m symmetrical robotic arm on the ISS Russian segment that can "walk" end-over-end between fixed base points to move payloads and assist spacewalks; built by Airbus for ESA.

name: VEX IQ
desc: A tool-less, snap-together robotics platform from VEX Robotics for grades 4–8, widely used in classrooms and the VEX IQ Robotics Competition. At its core is the IQ Robot Brain with a colour screen and twelve Smart Ports that auto-detect and interchangeably drive Smart Motors (each with a built-in processor, quadrature encoder and current monitor) and sensors — Optical (colour/light/gesture), laser Distance, Touch LED and Bumper — with a 6-axis gyro/accelerometer built into the 2nd-gen Brain. A game-controller-style handheld drives it wirelessly over VEXnet/Bluetooth. Students program in VEXcode IQ using Blocks, Python or C++ across browser, Windows, Mac and ChromeOS, with automatic firmware updates via VEXos.

name: VEX GO
desc: An affordable snap-together STEM construction system from VEX Robotics aimed at ages 7–11, designed so young students can tinker, make mistakes and try again. The education kit packs 296 structural and motion components with a GO Robot Brain, three motors, three electromagnets, an eye (optical) sensor, an LED bumper switch, a rechargeable battery and storage cases. Kids code it with block-based VEXcode GO (Scratch-style) right in the browser at codeGO.vex.com — no installation — on tablets, Chromebooks, Macs or PCs, supported by VEX STEM Labs cross-curriculum lesson plans spanning language arts, math, coding and engineering.
curriculum: VEX STEM Labs (language arts, math, coding, engineering)

name: mBot2
desc: The Makeblock mBot2 is an upgraded entry-level coding robot built on the CyberPi controller with Wi-Fi, supporting Scratch and Python; popular as a school class-pack for line-following, obstacle avoidance and AIoT projects.

name: mBot Ranger
desc: The Makeblock mBot Ranger is a 3-in-1 transformable robotics kit (tank, self-balancing car, three-wheel racer) with block-based mBlock and Arduino programming for intermediate STEM learners.
use_cases: 3-in-1 STEM build: tank / three-wheel racer / self-balancing robot

name: Cue
desc: An award-winning coding robot from Wonder Workshop (makers of Dash & Dot), built to carry students from block-based code into state-machine and text-based programming. Aimed at ages 11+, Cue ('Coding Utility Engine') has four selectable 'hero' avatar personalities with enhanced conversational AI and witty text-message-style chat. The wheeled robot moves expressively with RGB LED lights and a speaker, sensing its surroundings with IR proximity/distance sensors, microphones and an accelerometer, and connects over Bluetooth LE to the Wonder and Cue apps. Students program it in the block-based Wonder language and in JavaScript/Blockly. No longer produced, but still supported by Wonder Workshop.

name: JIMU Robot
desc: UBTECH JIMU Robot kits (e.g. AstroBot, BuilderBots) are snap-together robotic building sets with servos, sensors and a controller, programmed via the Blockly-based app to build and animate creations - blending construction play with coding.

name: ROSMASTER X3
desc: The Yahboom ROSMASTER X3 is an advanced education robot supporting ROS2, SLAM, LiDAR and machine-learning modules on a mecanum-wheel base - a testbed bridging classroom STEM and real robotics research/Jetson development.
cpu: NVIDIA Jetson Nano / Orin NX options

name: T1
desc: Booster Robotics' compact open-source developer humanoid and the model that won the 2025 RoboCup 'AdultSize' soccer league, adopted by 50+ teams and labs (Purdue, UC Berkeley, CMU, Tsinghua). Standing about 1.2 m and weighing 30 kg, it has 23 base DOF (6 per leg, 4 per arm, 1 waist, 2 head) driven by custom hollow-axis motors with dual encoders and full-force (torque/velocity/position) control up to 130 N·m. Dual compute — a 14-core Intel i7-1370P plus NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin 32 GB (~200 TOPS) — runs onboard AI, with an Intel RealSense RGB-D camera, 3D LiDAR, 9-axis IMU and mic array. Fully open SDK on ROS2 with Isaac Sim / MuJoCo / Webots support and up to ~2 h walking per charge.
chipset: Intel i7-1370P + NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin 32GB

name: CL-1
desc: The LimX Dynamics CL-1, debuted late 2023 by the Shenzhen startup (founded 2022), is one of the few humanoids capable of dynamic stair climbing via real-time terrain perception — the capability behind its viral warehouse-stairs video. At 1,650 mm, it was developed from LimX's point-foot biped P1 as a locomotion research platform, using proprietary hollow direct-drive actuators for deep squats, slope walking and push-recovery, with vision-LiDAR terrain perception at up to 4 km/h. Per LimX and The Robot Report, CL-1 was purely a bipedal platform and was never fitted with functional/articulated hands — later warehouse demos used simple paddle end-effectors to move totes. Hand-specific spec sections are therefore not applicable and omitted. Richer figures (31 DOF, 7-DOF arms, AGX Orin) belong to the later CL-3/Oli, not CL-1, and are excluded. Applicable-but-unpublished CL-1 fields are flagged 'Info not found' for outreach.
feature: Real-time terrain perception; dynamic stair climbing
actuator_type: Proprietary high-performance hollow direct-drive actuators (deep squats, push-recovery)
ai_model: Proprietary motion-control + RL; VideoGenMotion (video-based motion learning)
note: Company backed by ~$200M funding incl. NIO Capital; Oli ($22,730 full-size) is the commercial follow-up
vision: Integrated vision-LiDAR; active terrain perception of discrete terrain
capabilities: One of few humanoids capable of dynamic (real-time perception) stair climbing; slope walking; push-recovery; seamless indoor/outdoor; deep squats; up to 4 km/h
developed_by: LimX Dynamics (founded 2022, Shenzhen)
predecessor: LimX P1 (point-foot biped — CL-1 developed from it)
payload_kg: Heavy-object lifting demonstrated (exact kg not published)

Timeline: X1 quadruped prototype (Aug 2022, achieved forward stair-climbing Sept 2022); W1 wheeled-legged robot (Sept 2023); CL-1 humanoid first public dynamic test (Dec 2023); TRON 1 multi-modal biped (Oct 2024); TRON 2 multi-form embodied robot (Dec 2024); Oli general-purpose humanoid (Jul 2025); Luna interactive humanoid + COSA agentic OS (2026). Backed by Alibaba, JD.com, and others; ~200M RMB angel/pre-A. Awards incl. iF Design 2024.
end_effector: Simple paddle end-effectors (grip totes/boxes) — no articulated hand; CL-1 was purely a locomotion research platform

name: DR01
desc: The DEEP Robotics DR01 (Dr.01) is a full-size bipedal humanoid from Hangzhou's DEEP Robotics — the quadruped specialist (Lynx, X30) that entered the humanoid race positioning DR01 as an 'embodied intelligence explorer,' a platform to accelerate AI and big-data training for embodied intelligence. It walks at over 1.6 m/s and navigates 18 cm steps, 25° slopes and uneven, discrete terrain, swiftly recovering balance under unknown disturbances like slippery surfaces and external forces — demonstrations include stair climbing, walking across steel bars, and staying upright while pushed or pulled. It's built on DEEP Robotics' self-developed J60 lightweight joints and J100 high-torque joints, and its 'Fusion Perception' integrates self-perception with environmental perception through a learning algorithm that couples sensing and control, rather than relying on scripted gaits. Through AI and big-data training, DR01 can autonomously generate new behavioural skills as environments and tasks change. NOTE: locomotion specs from DEEP Robotics official; exact height/weight/DOF/payload not prominently published for DR01 and are flagged for outreach rather than guessed.
actuator_type: Self-developed J60 lightweight joints + J100 high-torque joints
ai_model: Learning algorithm combining sensing + control; AI/big-data training generates new skills autonomously
vision: Fusion Perception — combines self + environmental perception for discrete-terrain traversal
capabilities: Robust biped: >1.6 m/s walking, 18 cm steps, 25° slopes, uneven/discrete terrain; balance recovery under slippery surfaces & external push/pull; walks across steel bars; autonomous skill generation via training
developed_by: DEEP Robotics (Hangzhou Yunshenchu Technology) — also makes Lynx/X30 quadrupeds

name: Adam
desc: Adam is the flagship full-size humanoid from Beijing-based PNDbotics, a full-stack developer of modular humanoid platforms (project started June 2023). Standing about 1.6 m and weighing ~60 kg, Adam is driven by 25 proprietary PND quasi-direct-drive (QDD) force-controlled actuators delivering up to ~360 N·m of leg torque, and is notable as one of the first humanoids with a biomimetic pelvis for more natural, stable gait. An Intel i7 (NUC) plus PND Robot Control Unit runs a deep-reinforcement-learning and imitation-learning stack trained in NVIDIA Isaac Gym with sim-to-real transfer, giving human-like walking, terrain traversal and disturbance recovery. Its modular, standardized architecture (with an open SDK) lets developers swap actuators, end-effectors and compute. Adam has had a high-profile demo run — playing keytar live at the VOYAGEX music festival, synced dancing at WAIC 2025, and completing the 100 m obstacle race at the 2025 World Humanoid Robot Games as the only full-size humanoid to finish. Prototype pricing is around US$120,000; sibling variants include Adam Lite, Adam-U (data-collection) and Adam SP.
cpu: Intel i7 NUC + PND real-time control unit
ai_model: Deep RL + imitation learning (NVIDIA Isaac Gym sim-to-real)

name: PM01
desc: EngineAI’s lightweight open humanoid platform (CES 2025). At 1.38 m and 40 kg with 24 DoF and 320° waist rotation, the PM01 pairs an Intel N97 with NVIDIA Jetson Orin and ships fully open-source (ROS/ONNX, MuJoCo, Isaac) for developers. Founded by Zhao Tongyang, former lead of XPENG’s humanoid program.
actuator_type: Custom electric actuators, self-developed joint modules, dual encoders
cpu: Dual compute: Intel N97 (x86) + NVIDIA Jetson Orin
cameras: Intel RealSense D435i depth camera + multi-array microphones
sdk: Open-source: ROS/ONNX, MuJoCo sim2sim, Isaac training
records: World's first humanoid standing front flip (Feb 2025)
note: Compact performance/research platform

name: SE01
desc: EngineAI’s flagship full-size humanoid, unveiled October 2024 — claimed as the first humanoid to achieve a natural human-like gait via an end-to-end neural network. At 170 cm and 55 kg with 32 DoF, it uses self-developed harmonic/planetary/ball-screw joints rated to 186 N·m, an aerospace-aluminum 10-year frame, and quick-swap batteries. Founded by Zhao Tongyang (ex-XPENG PX5 lead).
perception: Engine Sense 360 deg LiDAR + depth camera
actuator_type: Self-developed harmonic, planetary & ball-screw joints; dual encoders; cross-roller bearings; forced-air joint cooling
use_cases: Commercial & educational (CCTV New Year Gala debut)
cameras: Depth camera + multi-mic array + LiDAR 360° (Engine Sense)
ai_model: End-to-end neural network (RL + imitation learning) — first humanoid with natural human-like gait
gait: Bio-inspired neural-network gait (among most natural in class)
note: One of most aggressive full-size launch prices ever (unified commercial/edu)

name: MagicBot Z1
desc: The MagicBot Z1 is MagicLab's compact, high-agility bipedal humanoid, unveiled in July 2025 and shown again at CES 2026. At about 1.4 m (136.9 cm) and 40 kg it has a human-child footprint that slips through tight indoor spaces, with 24 degrees of freedom in the standard build expandable to ~50 when fitted with optional sensors, arms and the 11-DOF MagicHand S01 (which adds five-fingered grasping up to ~3-5 kg per arm). In-house high-torque joints exceed 130 N·m with up to 320 degrees of travel, giving it acrobatic agility — fast motion, deep back-bends, and fall/prone recovery under disturbance. A 360-degree sensor suite (3D LiDAR, depth and binocular fisheye cameras, head tactile sensing) feeds a VLN navigation stack, with Wi-Fi 6 / Bluetooth 5.2, an 8-core CPU and a quick-release 10,000 mAh battery good for ~2 hours. MagicLab markets it as an open, developer-friendly platform for research, education and dynamic applications; its full-size sibling MagicBot Gen1/G1 targets industry. No public price.

name: Isaac
desc: Isaac, from Weave Robotics (San Francisco, YC S24, founded 2024 by ex-Apple engineers who led Siri and shipped Apple Watch Double Tap), is a wheeled dual-arm home robot built to automate everyday chores — making beds, sorting clutter, folding laundry and putting things away. Deliberately un-humanoid to reach the home faster than general-purpose bipeds, it rolls on a motorized wheeled base and is fingerless (grippers, not hands), with a telescopic body that rises from about 0.9 m stowed to 1.75 m to reach furniture, beds and shelves. Its rounded head with expressive digital eyes and fabric-covered panels are tuned for living spaces. The key idea is hybrid autonomy: Isaac runs autonomously most of the time, but when it hits a task it can't finish, a remote human operator briefly teleoperates via its camera feeds and then hands control back — ensuring reliability across messy real homes. Cameras physically disable via hardware controls for privacy, and capabilities expand through OTA updates. It launched at $7,999 (or $449/month), succeeding the stationary laundry-folding Isaac 0, with California deliveries from fall 2026. NOTE: specs from Weave official + launch coverage; exact DOF/payload/battery not formally published, flagged.
cameras: Onboard cameras with hardware controls to physically disable when not needed (privacy)
display_face: Rounded head with expressive digital eyes
ai_model: Hybrid autonomy — autonomous most tasks; remote human operator can teleoperate via camera feeds for hard tasks, then hand back
teleoperation: Hybrid: remote operator guides difficult tasks via onboard cameras
capabilities: Wheeled dual-arm home robot: makes beds, sorts clutter, folds laundry, tidies & puts items away; telescopic reach for furniture/beds/shelves; hybrid autonomy + teleop fallback; OTA skill updates
developed_by: Weave Robotics (YC S24; founders ex-Apple Siri/Watch, CMU)

name: A1
desc: Galaxea AI's A1 is a high-precision robotic arm/manipulation platform, part of Galaxea's lineup (with the R1 wheeled humanoid) targeting embodied-AI data collection and general manipulation.
use_cases: Robotic manipulation & embodied-AI research platform (mobile + tabletop variants)

name: GoMate
desc: The third-generation embodied-intelligence humanoid from Chinese automaker GAC (Guangzhou Automobile Group), unveiled December 2024. Its signature is an industry-first variable wheel-leg base that switches between a stable four-wheel mode (1.4 m tall, for stairs, slopes and obstacles) and an agile two-wheel mode (1.75 m tall, smaller footprint) — a design GAC says cuts energy use by over 80%. It has 38 DOF driven by in-house axial-flux joint motors (up to 1000 N·m) and coin-sized servo drives, an all-solid-state battery good for ~6 hours, GAC's pure-vision autonomous-driving algorithm plus FIGS-SLAM for centimetre positioning, and cloud multimodal AI for millisecond voice response. Pilot use began 2025 with small-scale production targeted for 2026.
actuator_type: Axial-flux joint motors + miniature low-voltage servo drives (<30 mm)

name: Platform 2 (P2 Zip)
desc: Zipline's Platform 2 (P2 Zip) is an autonomous delivery drone that hovers and lowers a tethered "droid" on a line to place packages precisely on doorsteps, extending Zipline's long-range medical/retail delivery network to homes.
actuator_type: Hybrid VTOL fixed-wing + tethered delivery droid

name: Wing Delivery Drone
desc: Wing (an Alphabet company) operates fixed-wing/multirotor hybrid autonomous delivery drones that carry small packages from local hubs to homes, with commercial operations in the US, Australia and beyond.

name: CRX-25iA
desc: The FANUC CRX-25iA extends the CRX collaborative family into heavy territory: 25 kg rated payload (up to 30 kg with the wrist oriented downward) across a class-leading 1,889 mm reach — the longest in the CRX line — from a 135 kg arm. Repeatability is ±0.05 mm, and the platform keeps every CRX hallmark: joint torque sensing with sensitive contact detection for fenceless ISO 10218-1 collaboration, the 8-years-zero-maintenance design, drag-and-drop Tablet TP programming with lead-through teaching, dual J6 tooling ports, and full FANUC ecosystem integration (iRVision, force sensors, ROBOGUIDE, ROS-Industrial). The reach-payload combination targets palletizing to full pallet height and tending large machinery that smaller cobots physically can't cover.
controller: FANUC R-30iB Mini Plus — compact controller, standard 120/230 V single-phase
teach_pendant: Tablet Teach Pendant — drag-and-drop icon programming + lead-through teaching
ft_sensor: Built-in torque sensing — sensitive contact detection in every joint

tool_io: Tool: 2 DI / 2 DO (M8) + 2 quick-change J6 connection ports for EOAT
ai_model: iRVision integration — built-in FANUC vision & force-sensor ecosystem

name: TM30S
desc: The Techman TM30S is the heavy-duty flagship of Techman's TM AI Cobot series — 30 kg rated payload (35 kg maximum in palletizing, wrist-favourable) across 1,702 mm reach, which Techman claims as the best reach-to-weight ratio in its category. Like the TM25S it is vision-native, with a built-in 5 MP autofocus camera driving TMvision AI object recognition and AOI, plus an integrated force/torque sensor at the end for precise force control and adaptability in complex tasks — a combination aimed squarely at semiconductor wafer-box loading (loads up to 35 kg), heavy palletizing, push-stacking and automotive assembly. It shares the S-series platform: ±0.03 mm repeatability, 450°/s 6th-axis speed, TÜV-certified safety with force limiting and body-part-specific zones, an IP54 control cabinet, and TMflow 2 flow-based programming with TMscript and TMcraft (C#/WPF) extensibility plus an official TM ROS driver.
axes_config: 6-axis AI collaborative arm with built-in vision
cameras: Built-in 5 MP autofocus vision system — TMvision, AI object recognition
