name: Dolphin Premier
desc: Corded commercial-grade Dolphin pool robot with dual scrubbing motors, Multi-Media/NanoFiltration, active waterline cleaning, a weekly smart timer and a 3-year warranty — a frequent top pick for inground pools.
filter: Multi-Media (4 options: oversized leaf bag, NanoFilters, standard, ultra-fine)
awards: USA Today Best Robotic Pool Cleaner

name: Dolphin Sigma
desc: Premium Dolphin robotic pool cleaner with dual drive motors, gyroscope navigation, oversized filtration and 360° waterline scrubbing for large inground pools.

name: Freedom
desc: Cordless robotic pool cleaner from Polaris offering floor, wall and waterline cleaning with app control, part of Polaris's Freedom / VRX iQ+ robotic range.

name: Cyber 1200 Pro
desc: Ofuzzi's flagship cordless robotic pool cleaner, focused on affordable, floor-only cleaning for flat-bottom pools up to 1,076 sq ft. Dual 50 W motors and twin suction inlets give 1.5x the pickup of earlier models, while a dual-path navigation system with adjustable 0–40° thrust nozzles and a 'halfway-turn-back' routine keeps the pool centre from becoming a dead zone. A 6,600 mAh battery runs up to ~130 minutes on a 3-hour charge, and it auto-parks at the wall for hook retrieval. No wall climbing (max 15° slope), no app — a status LED ring and power knob are the only controls.
use_cases: Above-ground and in-ground pools up to 1,076 sq ft

name: Clear UV
desc: Cordless pool robot notable as one of the first with a built-in UV-C lamp to help sanitize water while it cleans the pool floor and walls.

name: PC10
desc: An affordable cordless robotic pool cleaner from AIRROBO with a tread-based design and central scrubbing rollers reminiscent of higher-end units. A triple-motor system cleans the floor, walls and waterline, selectable via a single top-mounted switch across three modes (floor, wall/waterline, or both). A 5,200 mAh battery gives about two hours of runtime and recharges in ~2.5 hours; it self-parks near a wall at the end of its cycle for retrieval with the included hook. No app or remote — just the mode switch and a colour-coded LED bar.

name: VRX iQ+
desc: Corded 4WD robotic in-ground pool cleaner with the Polaris iQ app for scheduling and control, Vortex Vacuum debris pickup, active waterline scrubbing and tangle-free swivel cable.

name: Roomba Mini
desc: Billed as the world's smallest robot vacuum, the Roomba Mini is roughly half the size of a standard Roomba so it can reach corners and gaps larger robots miss. It navigates and maps with iRobot's ClearView LiDAR (working even in the dark), produces up to 70x the suction of the classic 600 series, and pairs with a downsized AutoEmpty Dock. A disposable mop-pad system lets it either vacuum or mop. iRobot's first new robot since its acquisition by Picea Robotics.

name: Cyber10 Ultra
navigation: Auto-retracting LiDAR + RGB camera + 3D structured light
desc: Dreame's most ambitious robot yet (IFA 2025): a CyberDex Hyper-Flex robotic arm (5 DOF, extends 33 cm, lifts 500 g) that clears clutter, 30,000 Pa Vormax suction, ProLeap 6 cm tiered-threshold climbing, all-in-one dock and Matter support.

name: Aqua10 Roller
navigation: dToF LDS LiDAR + 3D structured light + AI camera
mop_type: AquaRoll fresh-water roller mop (1100 g ground pressure)
desc: Dreame's first roller-mop line: an AquaRoll continuously-washed roller squeegees dirty water into an on-board tank while vacuuming at 30,000 Pa Vormax, with DuoBrush detangling, AutoSeal carpet guard and a PowerDock that hot-cleans the roller at 100°C.
camera: Twin AI cameras + LED fill light
brush_type: HyperStream DuoBrush (bristled-rubber + TPU rubber, 11.81 in hair)
edge_cleaning: AutoSeal roller guard + extendable side brush & mop

name: L60 Pro Ultra
desc: Well-reviewed L-series flagship praised for powerful vacuuming, outstanding obstacle avoidance and exceptional threshold climbing, with a premium all-in-one dock that self-empties, washes and dries.

name: Omni C20
desc: Ultra-slim (3.35 in) vacuum-and-mop that drops the LiDAR turret for a low-profile point-laser array, with 7,000 Pa suction, dual-pad MopMaster mopping and a full Omni station that empties dust and washes/dries the mop pads at a mid-tier price.

name: E20
desc: A 3-in-1 that converts between robot, cordless stick and handheld vacuum modes with a detachable unit — one machine to replace both a robot and a stick vac. Vacuum-only (no mopping).

name: E28
desc: E-series robot with a HydroJet live-rinse roller mop and a dock that washes and dries the roller, plus an integrated detachable portable deep cleaner for upholstery and spot cleaning.
dock_type: All-in-One Station (+ FlexiOne portable deep cleaner)

name: CordZero R5
desc: LG's all-in-one robot vacuum-mop with dual spinning mops and a station that empties dust and washes/dries the pads, controlled through the LG ThinQ smart-home app.

name: A30 Pro
desc: Value LiDAR robot vacuum-mop with an auto-empty dock — a budget alternative frequently compared with the MOVA S10.

name: Nautilus CC Supreme
desc: Top of the Nautilus line: Wi-Fi with the MyDolphin Plus app, dual split brushes, top-load filters and active waterline cleaning for inground pools up to 50 ft, with a remote and weekly scheduler.

name: Explorer E70
desc: Premium Wi-Fi Dolphin with three motors, anti-tangle swivel, ultrafine dual-layer top-load basket and 5,000 GPH flow, adding pickup mode and a temperature sensor in the app. Inground pools up to 50 ft; includes a caddy.

name: Dolphin Cayman
desc: A high-value corded robotic pool cleaner from Maytronics' Dolphin line, cleaning floors and climbing walls (no waterline). Guided by SmartNav 2.0 pool mapping and driven by efficient 24 V DC motors, it filters over 4,000 GPH through a top-access MaxBin cartridge (optionally upgraded with NanoFilters), and its HyperBrush scrubs twice as fast as standard Dolphin brushes on HyperGrip rubber tracks. Runs independently of the pool pump with a weekly timer for daily automation. The 2025 Max-Series redesign added a larger Gen-2 MaxBin.
surface_finish: All pool surfaces (vinyl, fiberglass, tile, concrete)
use_cases: In-ground and above-ground pools up to ~33 ft

name: AquaVac 650
desc: Hayward's robotic cleaner for inground pools, scrubbing floor, walls and waterline with app control and smart-steering navigation.

name: Prowler 930
desc: A corded robotic in-ground pool cleaner in Pentair's Prowler family that scrubs and vacuums floors, coves, walls and up to the tile/waterline. Uses two brushes with an active brush spinning twice as fast for extra scrubbing power, a top-access filter basket with customizable filtration, and self-programming smart navigation. Runs independently of the pool's pump (no booster needed) and is Bluetooth-enabled. Superseded by the Wi-Fi 930W.

name: Dolphin M600
desc: High-end Dolphin for inground pools with three motors, anti-tangle swivel, multi-layer ultrafine filtration and 4,500 GPH flow, with waterline cleaning and a weekly set-and-forget timer.

name: Prowler 730
desc: The above-ground member of Pentair's Prowler robotic pool-cleaner family. A corded, plug-and-play cleaner that scrubs and vacuums the floor and cove of above-ground pools with a top-access filter basket, running independently of the pool's filtration system. Self-programming navigation and an included caddy make it a drop-in-and-go cleaner.

name: W120-T
desc: A corded automatic window-cleaning robot in Mamibot's iGLASSBOT W120 family. Adheres to glass with a suction fan (up to 3,000 Pa) and cleans framed or frameless glass, mirrors, tiles and smooth walls, wet or dry, using AI path planning in Z, N or Z-to-N patterns. Includes edge detection, a backup battery and safety rope for power-loss protection, and returns to its start point when done. Controlled by one-touch button, remote or the iGLASSBOT app.
estop: Edge detection + backup battery + safety rope

name: Auto-Empty C10
desc: The slimmest Eufy robot (2.85 in), a vacuum-only model with a bagged self-empty dock — ideal for basic vacuuming with hands-off dust disposal and a rock-bottom profile for low furniture.

name: Deebot N30 Pro Omni
mop_type: OZMO Turbo dual spinning mops (edge-extend, auto-lift)
desc: Mid-range OMNI-station Deebot bringing flagship-style automation — auto-empty, hot mop wash, hot-air dry and self-refill — to a more accessible price, with LiDAR mapping and AI obstacle avoidance.

name: Explorer E50
desc: Wi-Fi Dolphin Explorer for inground and above-ground pools up to 50 ft, with a dual-layer top-load filter basket, waterline cleaning and the MyDolphin Plus app — the step below the E70.

name: Surfer S1
desc: A cordless, solar-powered robotic pool skimmer that glides across the water surface collecting floating leaves, pollen, insects and other debris into a 5 L top-load basket. Twin brushless paddle-wheel motors drive it while ultrasonic detectors recognise and avoid pool walls for edge-to-edge coverage, and Aiper's Sunseeker algorithm steers it toward sunlight to recharge. Dual charging (solar plus DC adapter) keeps it running up to ~12 hours per charge, and the Aiper app adds remote piloting, battery and water-temperature monitoring, and OTA updates.

name: D9
desc: Pudu's first full-size bipedal humanoid (from the BellaBot/KettyBot service-robot maker): 170 cm, 65 kg, 42 DoF with dual 7-DoF arms and the DH11 11-DoF dexterous hand, walking at 2 m/s, climbing stairs/slopes, carrying 20+ kg, with 3D semantic mapping and multimodal AI interaction.

name: D7
desc: Pudu Robotics' first general embodied-intelligence semi-humanoid, unveiled in September 2024. It pairs a human-like upper body and bionic arms with a fully omnidirectional wheeled chassis, bridging delivery robots and manipulation platforms for tasks like operating elevators, transporting and sorting items in service and light-industrial settings. Each arm uses 5 rotational and 2 linear joints for 30 DOF (expandable to 50 with a dexterous hand), a 65 cm reach, 10 kg payload and 0.1 mm endpoint repeatability. A 200 TOPS compute platform runs a layered planner/controller intelligence stack, and a 1 kWh+ battery gives 8+ hours per charge.
hand_type: Bionic arms (dexterous hand attachment optional, 30->50 DOF)
ai_model: Multi-layered embodied intelligence (high-level planner + low-level controller)

name: Kaleido 9
desc: The Kawasaki Kaleido 9, unveiled at iREX 2025 in Tokyo, is the ninth generation of Kawasaki's RHP Kaleido humanoid line (in development since 2015). At 1,900 mm and 99 kg, it's taller and heavier than earlier Kaleidos but far more capable: engineers significantly reinforced the waist and leg joints to solve the classic bipedal problem of balancing under load, enabling it to lift 30 kg. A new sensor suite — LiDAR plus enhanced stereo cameras — lets it build 3D maps and navigate autonomously in dynamic settings, and it supports VR remote control for disaster-response scenarios and can learn to operate tools like cleaning equipment. Kawasaki's roadmap targets simple factory tasks by 2030, complex assembly by 2040, and full disaster response beyond. It represents Kawasaki's bid to turn 50+ years of industrial-robot expertise into a practical working humanoid. NOTE: figures from Kawasaki official + iREX 2025 reporting; verified.
actuator_type: Electric servo; reinforced waist & leg joints for balance under load
vision: LiDAR + enhanced stereo cameras — 3D mapping & autonomous navigation
scene_understanding: 3D environment mapping for autonomous navigation in dynamic settings
capabilities: 9th-gen Kaleido: reinforced lower body for balance under load; lifts 30 kg; learns to operate cleaning/other tools; LiDAR+stereo autonomous navigation; VR-teleop for disaster response
developed_by: Kawasaki Heavy Industries (debuted iREX 2025, Tokyo)

name: Kaleido X
actuator_type: Electric servo; magnesium-alloy skeleton + 3D-printed resin exterior (weight-saving)
desc: Kawasaki's Kaleido (RHP — Robust Humanoid Platform) is the humanoid line from one of the world's oldest industrial-robot makers, in development since 2015 and first shown in 2017. This generation stands 1,780 mm at 85 kg with 32 DOF and unusually high industrial upper-body strength — handling loads up to 60 kg — while achieving fully untethered bipedal walking on an onboard battery. Kawasaki hit that stand-alone operation without weight gain through aggressive engineering: a magnesium-alloy skeleton (lighter than aluminium) and 3D-printed resin exterior panels replacing metal, plus integrating the previously external ~30 kg controllers into compact in-body drivers. It demonstrated stand-ups, pull-ups and two-handed grasping, with stereo-camera vision and object recognition. Kawasaki aims Kaleido at disaster response and dangerous industrial tasks, leveraging 50+ years of factory-robot heritage. NOTE: figures from Kawasaki official + IEEE records for this Kaleido generation; the newer Kaleido 9 is a separate DB entry.
capabilities: Untethered bipedal walking on onboard battery; stand-up motions; pull-ups; two-handed grasping; heavy upper-body strength
developed_by: Kawasaki Heavy Industries (RHP — Robust Humanoid Platform, since 2015)

name: Lingxi X2-N
desc: A hybrid-mobility variant of AGIBOT's compact Lingxi X2 (AGIBOT / Zhiyuan Robotics, Shanghai; the world's #1 humanoid producer by 2025 shipments), debuted at CES 2026 with a Tai Chi demonstration. The X2-N transforms its feet into wheels to switch between bipedal walking and wheeled rolling, using proprioceptive feedback — joint torque, pressure sensors and gyros rather than cameras — to adapt in real time, climb stairs and traverse ramps with light loads. It shares the X2 chassis (~1.31 m, ~35 kg, ~28 DoF) with AGIBOT's Xyber-Edge 'cerebellum' controller and Xyber-DCU decision unit, and is programmable through the ROS2-based AimDK_X2 framework in Python or C++.
company_note: World's #1 humanoid maker by volume (5,100+ units 2025, ~39% share, Omdia)
form_factor: X2 variant for light logistics + inspection (mixed indoor)
use_cases_note: Light logistics, inspection

name: Bumi
desc: The Noetix Bumi is a compact, consumer-priced bipedal humanoid from Beijing's Noetix Robotics — designed to bring genuine legged locomotion to classrooms, makerspaces and homes at a price previously reserved for wheeled toys. Standing 980 mm and about 17 kg with 21 DOF, it delivers stable walking, dynamic dance routines, voice interaction and a full graphical programming environment in a kid-safe, easy-to-carry chassis. Its proprietary N-shaped TIX force-controlled joint modules produce up to 70 N·m peak knee torque for stable walking and dynamic recovery, and it sees via a structured-light depth camera, running 2-3 hours per charge. Bumi gained international attention as one of four Chinese humanoids in China's 2026 Spring Festival Gala, performing live alongside human actors before 700M+ viewers — validating its reliability for unscripted interaction. It's the entry point to Noetix's lineup, sharing joint architecture with the larger N2 (which placed second in the world's first humanoid half-marathon), and ships in eight versions from Lite to Jetson-Orin-powered EDU-Max. NOTE: specs from Noetix/verified sources; the EDU-tier Jetson Orin is real (not a generic placeholder), confirmed per official version list.
note: Related to Dora lightweight line (1 m/s, 3 depth cameras) — verify SKU naming Bumi vs Dora
actuator_type: Proprietary Noetix force-controlled joint modules (N-shaped TIX joints); up to 70 N·m peak knee torque
capabilities: Compact consumer biped: stable bipedal walking, dynamic dance routines, voice interaction, graphical programming; performed live at China 2026 Spring Festival Gala (700M+ viewers); shares TIX joint architecture with larger N2 (2nd in world's first humanoid half-marathon)
developed_by: Noetix Robotics (Beijing)

name: Q5
desc: The RobotEra Q5 is a wheeled service humanoid from Beijing's ROBOTERA (founded 2023), a super-humanoid built for professional service scenarios. At 1,650 mm and 65 kg with 44 full-body DOF — including the agile 11-DOF XHAND Lite (StarMotion 'Elf Hand') for precise manipulation — it can squat to pick up objects, twist its waist, shake hands and lift up to 10 kg with a single arm. High-precision bionic 7-axis joints and harmonic-drive actuators give it smooth motion; a lithium battery with BMS powers it; and a sensor suite of Livox Mid-360 LiDAR, IMU, stereo RGB cameras and torque sensors drives LiDAR-visual fusion navigation. It supports full-body teleoperation through gloves and VR (plus 2.4G wireless), recognises 37+ languages, and learns new tasks from human demonstration videos, improving via a closed loop of teleoperation, data collection and model iteration shared with RobotEra's STAR1 platform. It targets commercial services, cultural tourism, hotels, elderly care and education. NOTE: full spec cross-verified from RobotEra official + databases (165cm/65kg/44DOF/10kg/XHAND-Lite 11-DOF).
ai_model: RobotEra embodied-AI stack (shares core with STAR1); learns tasks from human demo videos
use_cases_note: Hospitality/service scenarios
actuator_type: High-precision bionic 7-axis joints; harmonic drive actuators
locomotion: Wheeled base (waist twist, squat to pick up)
teleoperation: Full-body teleoperation via gloves + VR; 2.4G wireless control
capabilities: Wheeled service humanoid: squats to pick, twists waist, shakes hands, 10 kg single-arm lift; LiDAR-visual navigation; learns from demo video; 37+ languages; guidance, commentary, delivery
developed_by: Beijing ROBOTERA Technology (shares components with STAR1)

name: Harley (哈利)
desc: Hisense's first humanoid service robot, debuted at CES 2026 as part of the company's full-scenario smart-home showcase (alongside the R1/A2 humanoid and the Beta home-companion robot). Harley has 31 degrees of freedom, giving it lifelike gestures and interactions aimed at on-site customer engagement. As a new debut, Hisense has not yet published detailed hardware specifications.

name: Hea
desc: Hea is home-appliance giant Haier's humanoid robot, developed for home and service scenarios and positioned to leverage Haier's vast smart-home appliance ecosystem — part of the broader trend of Chinese consumer-hardware majors (Xiaomi, Honor, Midea) entering embodied AI. NOTE: Haier publishes very limited public specifications for Hea at this development stage — height, weight, DOF, payload, sensors, actuators and battery are all UNpublished and flagged for outreach rather than invented. Only the manufacturer, category and stated purpose are confirmed; this is deliberately a thin-but-honest entry pending Haier releasing real spec data.
capabilities: Haier's humanoid for home/service scenarios; leverages Haier's smart-home appliance ecosystem
developed_by: Haier (home-appliance giant)

name: Alfie
desc: Alfie, from UK startup Prosper Robotics, is a home butler robot being developed to handle domestic chores — tidying and everyday household tasks — with a mobile base for navigating homes and a teleoperation-assisted approach in early deployment to ensure tasks get completed while its autonomy matures. It sits in the emerging 'practical home robot' category alongside Weave's Isaac and 1X's NEO, betting on domestic usefulness as the entry point for consumer robotics. NOTE: Prosper publishes limited hard specs for Alfie (height/weight/DOF/payload/battery not formally released — it's development-stage) — those fields are flagged for outreach rather than invented; category, approach and purpose confirmed from Prosper.
hand_type: Two arms, pincher hands + modular toolbox (50-100 attachments)
capabilities: Home butler robot for domestic chores — tidying, household tasks; designed for real home deployment
developed_by: Prosper Robotics (UK)

name: Memo
desc: Memo, from Sunday Robotics, is a pre-commercial home robot positioned as a high-end domestic appliance rather than a factory machine, powered by Sunday's proprietary ACT-1 manipulation model. As of late 2025 it's in a '2026 Founding Family' beta: about 50 households receive individually numbered, hand-built units (each costing roughly $20,000 to build today) while Sunday iterates on reliability, safety and service, targeting a future retail price under $10,000 once it can manufacture at scale. Sunday is betting on a large installed base of home robots trained by its ACT-1 model over the coming decade — the same 'useful in the home first' thesis driving Weave, 1X and Prosper. NOTE: Sunday publishes minimal hardware specs for Memo at this pre-commercial stage (height/weight/DOF/payload not formally released) — those are flagged for outreach, not invented; program structure, pricing strategy and ACT-1 model confirmed from Sunday.
ai_model: Sunday ACT-1 model (home-task manipulation; large installed-base learning strategy)
capabilities: Pre-commercial home robot for domestic tasks; hand-built beta units; iterating on reliability, safety & service via 'Founding Family' program (~50 households, individually numbered)
developed_by: Sunday Robotics

name: RoBee
desc: Billed as the first certified Italian cognitive humanoid, RoBee is built by Oversonic Robotics (Brianza, founded 2020) for real industrial work — manufacturing, intralogistics, healthcare and hazardous environments. It stands 175 cm, weighs 80 kg and has 40 joints, moving on an omnidirectional wheeled base at up to 1.2 m/s with up to 8 hours of autonomy and inductive charging. Bimanual arms with a 90 cm reach carry ~10 kg and use humanoid hands, grippers or pneumatic end-effectors to sub-millimetre accuracy. A cognitive AI stack handles computer vision, face/object recognition, emotion adaptation, voice and cloud fleet management, with ERP/MES integration and R (industry), M (medical) and F (intralogistics) variants.
hand_type: Humanoid hands / grippers / pneumatic end-effectors (sub-mm accuracy)
ai_model: Cognitive AI (computer vision, face/object recognition, emotion adaptation)

name: Mirokaï
desc: A whimsical social-service humanoid from Paris-based Enchanted Tools, founded by Jerome Monceaux (co-creator of Aldebaran's Nao and Pepper). Mirokai pairs an expressive projected animated face with a patented omnidirectional ball-bot base, gliding through hotels, airports, hospitals and museums to welcome, guide and carry. High-speed torque-controlled arms achieve a 97% grasping success rate, carrying 1.5 kg per hand and pulling up to 15 kg. Multi-LLM AI drives fluid multilingual conversation with GDPR-compliant face tracking; roughly 50 units shipped from a 2024 pilot line at $30,000 each.

name: Roboy
actuator_type: Tendon-driven series-elastic actuators (myorobotic — motors + spring + tendon mimicking muscles)
desc: Roboy, from Devanthro (originating at TU Munich / Fortiss in 2013), is an open-source tendon-driven musculoskeletal humanoid built to mimic the human muscle-tendon system rather than use conventional rigid joints. Its 'myorobotic' actuation pairs electric motors with springs and tendons to emulate biological muscles, giving compliant, human-like movement, and the project has iterated through multiple generations exploring biologically-inspired robotics, telepresence avatars and prosthetics research. Devanthro develops Roboy as an open platform (ROS-based) with an active research and maker community, positioning it alongside other musculoskeletal efforts like Clone's Myofiber androids and the University of Tokyo's Kengoro. NOTE: Roboy exists in several research generations with varying configurations; Devanthro publishes limited fixed spec tables (exact DOF/height/weight vary by build) — those are flagged for outreach rather than guessed; the tendon-driven myorobotic architecture, open-source status and research focus are confirmed.
capabilities: Open-source tendon-driven musculoskeletal humanoid mimicking human muscle-tendon system; research into biologically-inspired robotics, telepresence avatars & prosthetics; ongoing generations since 2013
developed_by: Devanthro (the Roboy project; origin at TU Munich / Fortiss)

name: Wanda
desc: A mass-produced, full-size general-purpose service humanoid from UniX AI (founded 2024, Suzhou). Wanda pairs a differential-drive wheeled base — chosen for stable, long-duty-cycle indoor operation over bipedal locomotion — with what UniX calls the world's first mass-produced 8-DoF bionic arms and adaptive grippers. It stands up to 168 cm with a 260 mm torso lift (reaching 1,800 mm), carries 12 kg across both arms with 0.5 mm repeatability, and runs 8–16 hours per charge. Its embodied-AI stack centres on 'UniTouch' visuo-tactile intelligence plus imitation learning for long-horizon household and service tasks (laundry, dishwashing, tidying, reception).
actuator_type: In-house harmonic-reducer + brushless DC servo, dual-encoder

name: Mornine
desc: A full-size service humanoid from AiMOGA, the robotics subsidiary Chery established in early 2025. The Mornine M1 went on commercial sale in April 2026 via JD.com at RMB 285,800 (~$41,860), one of the first humanoids sold direct to the public online. It stands 167 cm, weighs 70 kg and has 40 degrees of freedom (excluding its dexterous hands), walking up to 1 m/s on a 0.7 kWh battery good for about two hours. Built for sales, reception and training, it supports dual-arm coordinated tasks, speaks 10+ languages, integrates conversational AI (including ChatGPT), and can even autonomously open car doors — reflecting its origins pitched at automotive dealerships, where it first deployed in Malaysia in March 2025.

name: Andi
desc: A bipedal service humanoid in prototype development from OrionStar, the Beijing service-robotics company spun out of Cheetah Mobile (founded 2016, maker of the Lucki delivery robot and Greeting Mini). Andi is aimed at service and commercial applications and builds on OrionStar's established AI ecosystem — voice interaction, visual navigation and the OrionOS open platform. As a prototype, detailed hardware specifications have not yet been published.

name: Ginger
desc: A cloud-connected humanoid service robot from Dataa Robotics (formerly CloudMinds), first shown as the XR-1 at MWC 2019 and a 2020 Red Star Design Award winner. Its intelligence runs largely in the HARIX cloud brain over 5G, giving image, object, posture, face and emotion recognition, multilingual multi-round dialogue and cloud-scheduled multi-robot collaboration. Thirty-four smart compliant actuators drive expressive gestures and visually-guided grasping with eye-hand coordination, while a three-wheeled omnidirectional base with self-balancing and cloud SLAM/VSLAM handles autonomous navigation. Used for reception, guidance, elderly care, education and retail.

name: Alex
desc: Alex, from Boardwalk Robotics (Pensacola, Florida), is a 19-DOF upper-body manipulation humanoid unveiled August 2024 — deliberately legless, mounting on a stable or mobile base to prioritise safety and high-speed dexterity over bipedal locomotion. Its custom in-house actuators drive rapid joints at up to 9 rad/s with a 10 kg continuous payload, paired with vision and force sensing and onboard real-time control, for tasks like cleaning, organizing, pick-and-place and factory work. Boardwalk developed Alex's manipulation systems leveraging its collaboration with the Institute for Human Machine Cognition (IHMC), renowned for bipedal robotics (the two also built the Nadia research humanoid together). In December 2024 Foundation Robotics acquired Boardwalk, inheriting the engineering team and the Alex hardware — which was rebranded and further developed into the Foundation Phantom MK1, with Boardwalk's years of cycloidal-actuator work becoming Phantom's core differentiator. NOTE: not to be confused with IHMC's separate 29-DOF fully-electric bipedal 'Alex' research robot; this is Boardwalk's commercial upper-body Alex. Specs verified from Boardwalk/databases.
actuator_type: Custom in-house actuators — rapid joints up to 9 rad/s
dof_note: 19-DOF humanoid upper torso (no legs)
controller: Proprietary high-speed manipulation control; onboard compute (real-time control + sensor fusion)
capabilities: High-speed upper-body manipulation humanoid (no legs — mounts on stable/mobile base); cleaning, organizing, pick-and-place, factory work; developed with IHMC bipedal expertise
developed_by: Boardwalk Robotics (collaborated with IHMC on Nadia; acquired by Foundation Robotics Dec 2024)
successor: Foundation Phantom MK1 (Alex platform rebranded & developed into Phantom)

name: Bot Handy
desc: A household-assistant robot concept from Samsung Research, first shown at CES 2021 and upgraded at CES 2022. Bot Handy pairs a wheeled mobile base with a tall, slim body and a single highly-articulated arm that pivots at shoulder, elbow and wrist, ending in a clamp-like hand. Cameras in its head and hand feed AI object recognition that distinguishes materials and weights so it can apply the right grip force — letting it pick up laundry, load dishwashers, set tables and pour drinks. A digital face with expressive eyes handles interaction, and mobility plus elevation extend its working reach in 3D space. Shown as a development concept rather than a shipping product.

name: DR02
desc: Unveiled by Hangzhou's DEEP Robotics in October 2025, the DR02 is billed as the world's first full-size humanoid with IP66 whole-body dust- and water-jet protection, letting it work in rain, humidity, dust and cold/hot sites where lab humanoids fail. It stands 175 cm with 68 cm arms sized to human tools and spaces, walks at 1.5 m/s (sprinting to 4 m/s), climbs 20 cm stairs and 20-degree slopes, and carries 10 kg per arm (20 kg total). A 275 TOPS compute unit with LiDAR, depth and wide-angle cameras drives real-time mapping and obstacle avoidance, and a modular quick-detach design lets forearms, arms and legs be swapped (left/right interchangeable) to minimise downtime.

name: T170A (Yao Guang)
desc: The Ti5 Robot T170A (Yao Guang) is a full-size bipedal humanoid notable for its exceptional strength-to-weight ratio — standing 1.7 metres yet weighing only 50 kg, thanks to Ti5's signature ultra-light joint modules. That light build plus industry-leading leg-joint torque density makes it agile and energy-efficient, capable of dynamic feats like single-leg jumps. It perceives its surroundings through an advanced LiDAR system and binocular cameras for clear obstacle understanding, and processes AI tasks in real time on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin for precise, smooth motion. Equipped with dexterous bionic hands, the T170A targets applications from laboratory research to administrative support, offering a powerful yet easy-to-use platform. NOTE: height/weight/sensors/compute from Ti5/verified sources; exact DOF, payload and battery figures not prominently published and are flagged for outreach rather than guessed.
actuator_type: Ti5 ultra-light joint modules — industry-leading leg-joint torque density (single-leg jumps)
capabilities: Lightweight agile biped (high strength-to-weight): single-leg jumps via high torque-density leg joints; dynamic movement; real-time Jetson AGX Orin AI; lab research + administrative support
developed_by: Ti5 Robot

name: Elf
desc: The BXI Elf, from China's BXI Robotics, is a human-sized open-source programmable bipedal robot aimed at embodied-AI research and sim-to-real deployment. Standing 1.45 m and just 32 kg for easy handling, it has 25 DOF (legs 2×6 with hip z/y/x, knee and dual-axis ankle; arms 5×2; 3-DOF waist) driven by BXI's own high-torque joint motors delivering up to 150 N·m at the hips and knees, and it can handle a payload over 25 kg. With an open SDK and ready-to-deploy architecture, it's designed as a testbed for algorithm development and sim-2-real transfer; BXI also sells the underlying high-performance joint motors and turnkey OEM solutions, and offers the updated Elf 3 generation. name: XMAN-R1
desc: The KEENON XMAN-R1, from Shanghai-based KEENON Robotics (founded 2010), is an embodied service humanoid developed entirely in-house for the real-world demands of hospitality and logistics. Grounded in KEENON's large-scale service-scenario data, it's designed to replicate the movement logic and postures of human service staff — with human-like proportions and adaptive kinematic knee flexion-extension matching — so it can take orders, prepare and deliver food, collect dishes, handle luggage and clean rooms while adapting to dynamic environments. It uses multimodal fusion perception, spatial awareness and domain-specific knowledge graphs to understand and execute high-level human commands, and is built to collaborate with KEENON's wider robot fleet (the DINERBOT T10 delivery robot, KLEENBOT C30 cleaner and S100). It's the research/interaction-oriented member of KEENON's XMAN service-humanoid line, alongside the commercial XMAN-F1 and the compact 136 cm, 100-TOPS XMAN-L1. NOTE: KEENON publishes limited hard specs for XMAN-R1 (exact height/weight/DOF/payload/battery) — those are flagged for outreach rather than invented; capabilities, perception stack, fleet integration and product-line context are confirmed.

name: Kangaroo
actuator_type: Custom linear actuators with integrated force sensors; closed/parallel kinematic chains (low leg inertia)
desc: Kangaroo, from Barcelona's PAL Robotics, is a bipedal humanoid robot purpose-built for research on agile and dynamic locomotion. Its signature engineering is mechanical: instead of conventional rotary joints, Kangaroo uses custom linear actuators with integrated force sensors arranged in closed/parallel kinematic chains, concentrating mass away from the legs to achieve very low moving inertia — which translates into high joint speeds and torques, better impact resilience and reduced energy consumption. It features 12 actuated degrees of freedom per leg and has demonstrated real-hardware jumping, showcasing the platform's robustness and resilience. PAL positions Kangaroo as a testbed for dynamic locomotion, reinforcement learning and embodied AI, complementing its established humanoid and mobile robots (TALOS, TIAGo, REEM, ARI). name: ergoCub
desc: ergoCub, from the Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia (IIT), is an ergonomically-designed collaborative humanoid — an evolution of IIT's famous iCub — built specifically to reduce musculoskeletal injuries among workers. Standing 1.5 m and 55.7 kg and able to carry about 10 kg, its geometry was optimised during design to minimise the combined energy/joint effort of human-robot lifting tasks. It incorporates an Intel RealSense depth camera and LiDAR for navigation, new-generation force-torque sensors that let it respond intuitively to external forces, and a flexible OLED 2K face screen for expressive interaction, all powered by an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Xavier alongside an 11th-gen Intel i7. It's the centrepiece of the ergoCub project, a collaboration between IIT and INAIL (Italy's workplace-accident insurer, which funded €5M over three years) aimed at cutting biomechanical risk for future workers through humanoids, wearables and AI. NOTE: full specs from IIT's official ergoCub page — museum-grade sourcing; Jetson AGX Xavier + i7 compute is real and published.

name: OP3
desc: An affordable, fully open-source miniature humanoid research/education platform from ROBOTIS — the successor to the widely-used DARwIn-OP / OP2. It has 20 DYNAMIXEL XM430 actuator modules (6-DoF legs x2, 3-DoF arms x2, 2-DoF neck) with current-based control on a 4.5 Mbps bus, an OpenCR (ARM Cortex-M7) real-time controller, and an Intel NUC Core i3 with 8 GB DDR4 and an M.2 SSD for onboard compute. A 9-axis IMU (gyro/accel/magnetometer), a Logitech C920 HD camera, dual mics and a speaker handle perception. The 2025 re-release is built ground-up for ROS2, and the 1,800 mAh LiPo can be hot-swapped by plugging in external power before removal (~30 min runtime). Popular in the RoboCup humanoid leagues.

name: Origin
desc: Origin, from Chinese startup AheadForm, is an ultra-realistic expressive robotic head that startled viewers with facial movements many described as eerily human — blinking, glancing and shifting gaze with lifelike subtlety. Its two differentiators are a custom brushless-motor system — compact, quiet and energy-efficient, giving the fine control needed for subtle eyebrow raises and gaze shifts, potentially cheaper to scale than servo-and-linkage approaches — and self-supervised AI algorithms integrated with high-DOF bionic actuation to drive micro-expressions. Where Hanson Robotics' Sophia leans on Frubber skin and broad, recognisable expressions, AheadForm focuses on the fleeting nuances of real human movement, and its 'Elf series' deliberately adopts slightly stylised, elf-like features (large ears, exaggerated expressiveness) as a design choice. Origin targets human-robot interaction research, expressive avatars and engagement applications. NOTE: AheadForm publishes limited formal spec tables (exact facial DOF, dimensions) — those are flagged for outreach; the brushless-actuation approach, self-supervised AI and design philosophy are confirmed from AheadForm coverage.

name: UR15
desc: The Universal Robots UR15 is the newest member of UR's flagship UR Series (alongside UR20 and UR30) and UR's fastest cobot yet — a 5 m/s maximum TCP speed paired with a 17.5 kg payload and 1,300 mm reach in a remarkably light 40.7 kg body. It hits a market sweet spot: high payload and long reach at high speed while staying collaborative, cutting cycle times for palletizing, machine tending and packaging. Its standout technology is OptiMove — an intuitive motion-programming system that simplifies setup while improving repeatability and delivering the smoothest high-speed, high-payload motion in UR's line — running on the AI-ready PolyScope platform. TÜV and UL 1740 certified and suited to higher-IP environments, the UR15 keeps UR's signature ease of use, small footprint and rapid redeployment. It complements the tried-and-tested e-Series with the extra speed and payload the flagship UR Series is built for.

desc: The Universal Robots UR7e is the medium-duty member of UR's proven e-Series, delivering a 7.5 kg payload and 850 mm reach at ±0.03 mm repeatability from a compact 20.6 kg arm on a Ø151 mm footprint. Introduced in 2025 as a renamed, payload-upgraded successor to the UR5e (UR's best-selling size), it fills the gap between the UR3e and UR12e while keeping the e-Series' defining strengths: a built-in tool-flange force/torque sensor (±50 N / ±10 Nm, precision ±3.5 N), 21 configurable safety functions certified PL d Cat. 3, 4 m/s TCP speed, IP54 sealing, and any-orientation mounting. It runs UR's industry-standard PolyScope software on a 12-inch touchscreen with freedrive teaching and the vast UR+ ecosystem of certified end-effectors and apps, plus Modbus TCP, EtherNet/IP, PROFINET/PROFIsafe and ROS/ROS2. With over 100,000 UR cobots delivered worldwide, the e-Series is the reference platform for collaborative automation; the UR7e targets machine tending, assembly, screwdriving and inspection where reach and accuracy matter in tight cells.

It keeps the full e-Series platform: a built-in force/torque sensor (±50 N / ±10 Nm), 21 configurable PL d Cat. 3 safety functions, 4 m/s TCP speed, IP54 sealing, and any-orientation mounting, all programmed through PolyScope on a 12-inch touchscreen with freedrive teaching and the UR+ accessory ecosystem. name: CRX-5iA
desc: The FANUC CRX-5iA is the entry model of FANUC's CRX collaborative family — 5 kg payload, 994 mm reach, ±0.03 mm repeatability from a 25 kg arm light enough to install without a crane. Like every CRX it carries FANUC's signature reliability claim: 8 years of zero maintenance, backed by the company's industrial track record. Built-in torque sensing in every joint gives sensitive contact detection for fenceless ISO 10218-1 collaboration, and programming is deliberately novice-friendly — drag-and-drop icons on the Tablet Teach Pendant plus lead-through teaching, running on the compact R-30iB Mini Plus controller from standard single-phase power. Two J6 connection ports quick-change end-of-arm tooling, and the FANUC ecosystem (iRVision, force sensors, ROBOGUIDE simulation, ROS-Industrial) plugs straight in. A food-grade variant adds NSF-H1 grease, white epoxy paint and rust/chemical-resistant plating.

desc: The FANUC CRX-10iA/L is the long-reach variant of the 10 kg CRX — 1,418 mm reach with a unique underflip motion that swings the arm beneath its own base, maximising flexibility in tight cells where a conventional wrist path can't fit. It shares the family DNA: ±0.04 mm repeatability, 40 kg installable-by-hand mass, joint torque sensing for fenceless contact-stop collaboration, 8-years-zero-maintenance design, Tablet TP drag-and-drop programming, and the R-30iB Mini Plus controller on standard single-phase power. It's the basis of two notable specials: the CRX-10iA/L Paint — the first and only cobot approved for painting under U.S. safety standards, serving liquid/powder coating and fiberglass dispensing — and a food-grade version with NSF-H1 grease, white epoxy paint and rust/chemical-resistant plating.

Programming stays drag-and-drop on the Tablet Teach Pendant with lead-through teaching, on the compact R-30iB Mini Plus controller. Dual J6 tooling ports, iRVision/force-sensor integration, ROBOGUIDE and ROS-Industrial complete the ecosystem, and a food-grade version (NSF-H1 grease, white epoxy, rust/chemical-resistant plating) serves wet and hygiene-critical environments.

name: LBR iisy 3 R760
desc: The KUKA LBR iisy 3 R760 is KUKA's accessible, plug-and-produce cobot — a 3 kg / 760 mm 6-axis arm at ±0.1 mm repeatability and 22.8 kg, built to get non-experts from unboxing to a running basic application in about 30 minutes. Integrated joint torque sensors make it sensitive enough for fenceless collaboration with hand guiding, certified PL d Cat. 3, and it's the entry point to a family spanning 3, 6, 8, 11 and 15 kg payloads. Its real platform advance is software: the LBR iisy runs KUKA's newest operating system, iiQKA.OS, on the compact KR C5 micro control box with the smartPAD-Pro, and the iiQKA 'Robotics Republic' ecosystem lets users bolt on grippers, vision and other components app-store style for rapid repurposing. KUKA leans on decades of industrial componentry for the durability claim, positioning the iisy as reliable industrial technology in an approachable collaborative package.

name: LBR iiwa 14 R820
desc: The KUKA LBR iiwa 14 R820 is the world's first series-produced sensitive robot — 'LBR' for Leichtbauroboter (lightweight robot), 'iiwa' for intelligent industrial work assistant — and one of the most influential research and HRC platforms ever made. Its defining feature is joint torque sensors in all seven axes, giving instant whole-arm contact detection with axis-specific torque accuracy of ±2% of maximum torque, so it can perform force-controlled contour-finding, delicate joining and compliant insertion without crushing or shearing hazards, fenceless, certified to PL d Cat. 3. The 14 kg / 820 mm redundant 7-axis arm weighs 29.9 kg, carries IP54 sealing, mounts in any orientation, and routes pneumatic and electrical supply internally to a DIN ISO 9409-1-50-7-M6 media flange. It runs from the KUKA Sunrise Cabinet, programmed in Java via Sunrise.Workbench or by hand guiding — and its 1 kHz Fast Robot Interface (FRI) made it the de-facto standard arm for robotics-research labs worldwide. A 7 kg / 800 mm sibling (LBR iiwa 7 R800) shares the platform.

name: GoFa 5 (CRB 15000)
desc: The ABB GoFa 5 is the founding model of ABB's GoFa CRB 15000 collaborative family — 5 kg payload across 950 mm wrist reach (1,050 mm to flange) with best-in-class ±0.02 mm repeatability and TCP speeds to 2.2 m/s, which ABB bills as roughly 50% faster than same-class cobots. Torque and position sensors in every joint drive SafeMove power-and-force limiting certified PL d Cat. 3 with up to 16 configurable safety zones, wrapped in rounded no-pinch geometry with an interaction status light. The 28 kg, IP54 arm on a 165×165 mm base mounts in any direction and runs from ABB's OmniCore controller with RobotWare 7 — programmed by grabbing the arm anywhere (lead-through), Wizard graphical blocks on the FlexPendant, RAPID, or RobotStudio offline with ~99% sim-to-real fidelity. The Ultra Accuracy option cuts path accuracy to 0.03 mm — over 10× tighter than rival cobots — for gluing, sealing and laser applications. ISO Class 4 cleanroom rated; Pro variant adds PROFINET.

Its IP67 sealing — a step above the GoFa 5's IP54 — suits dusty and moisture-prone floors across a 5–45 °C range, and the 51 kg arm on a ~200×200 mm base mounts in any orientation. The platform is pure GoFa: joint-integrated torque/position sensing feeding PL d Cat. 3 SafeMove with 16 configurable zones, interaction status light, grab-anywhere lead-through, Wizard blocks, RAPID and RobotStudio offline programming on the OmniCore controller. The Ultra Accuracy option (0.03 mm path / 0.1 mm absolute) opens sealing, laser welding and precision cutting across its wide envelope. ISO Class 4 cleanroom; Pro variant adds PROFINET.

name: SWIFTI CRB 1100
desc: The ABB SWIFTI CRB 1100 collapses the cobot/industrial-robot divide: built on the IRB 1100 industrial platform, it delivers a TCP speed above 5 m/s — five times faster than typical 4 kg cobots — and ±0.01 mm repeatability, up to ten times tighter than the collaborative norm, while remaining fenceless. Safety is speed-and-separation rather than contact-based: SafeMove paired with a safety laser scanner slows or halts the arm before a human can reach it, with an interaction light signalling status, certified PL d Cat. 3. The 4 kg / 580 mm arm (a 475 mm / 4.32 m/s variant exists) carries four integrated air supplies for vacuum grippers and runs from the OmniCore controller, programmed via a clip-on lead-through device, Wizard graphical blocks, the SafeMove Configurator app, RAPID or RobotStudio. It targets intermittent-collaboration tasks — assembly, kitting, polishing — where industrial speed matters but a human must occasionally step in.

name: PoWa
desc: ABB's high-speed collaborative-robot family, launched first for the Chinese market in July 2025 (built at ABB's Shanghai Mega Factory) and globally in 2026. PoWa - a name meant to evoke 'power' - closes the gap between light traditional cobots and rigid industrial robots, delivering industrial-grade speed and payload in a compact, fenceless package. The family spans six payload categories from 7 kg to 30 kg with a best-in-class top speed of up to 5.8 m/s and, ABB says, the longest reach and highest arm load in its class (7-10 kg on the lower arm / Axis 3, easing tool and cable mounting for arc welding). It runs ABB's OmniCore controller with built-in Power-and-Force Limiting and Speed-and-Separation Monitoring for safe shared workspaces, carries IP65/IP67 protection and ISO Class 4/5 cleanroom compatibility, and can be unboxed and running in about 60 minutes via no-code Wizard programming, arm-side buttons and plug-and-play tooling (RobotStudio / AppStudio).

name: Racer-5 COBOT
desc: The Comau Racer-5 COBOT is, by Comau's account, the only collaborative robot that automatically switches from full industrial speed to collaborative speed the instant a human operator enters its working area — letting one machine replace two (a fast industrial arm and a separate cobot). It pairs a 5 kg payload and 809 mm reach with ±0.03 mm repeatability and up to 6 m/s Cartesian speed in non-collaborative mode, throttling to ≤500 mm/s when collaborating, with Safe Collision Detection certified PL d Cat. 3 by TÜV Süd for fenceless operation. Made entirely in Comau's Turin plant with a rigid construction for lasting precision, it routes electrical and air connections at the forearm to avoid external harnesses, signals its mode via an LED status stripe, and offers Comau's arm-mounted MI.RA vision system for pick-and-place. A Racer-5-0.63 industrial variant (627 mm) completes the family, targeting automotive, electrification and general-industry assembly, dispensing and machine tending.

name: LS6-B SCARA
desc: The Epson LS6-B is a value-focused 4-axis SCARA robot built for factories that need reliable high-speed assembly at a budget price — 6 kg payload, up to 600 mm reach (500/600/700 mm arm lengths available), ±0.015 mm repeatability and a 200 mm Z-stroke, with high acceleration/deceleration for fast cycle times. Epson leans on its RC+ development environment (SPEL+ 7.0 language) and low-cost RC90 controller to make it easy to program, with integrated options for Epson Vision, fieldbus interfaces, teach pendants and customizable GUIs. An ISO 4 Clean version suits dust-critical and cleanroom applications. It targets the price/performance sweet spot for mechanical and electrical assembly, pick-and-place, kitting and dispensing where throughput matters and budget is tight — part of Epson's position as one of the world's highest-volume SCARA makers.
teach_pendant: Epson teach pendant (optional)

name: COBOTTA
desc: The DENSO COBOTTA, launched in 2018, is an all-in-one desktop collaborative robot built around portability and out-of-the-box simplicity — a 4 kg unit with the controller integrated into the arm, a 0.5 kg payload (0.7 kg with axis 5 vertical) and 342.5 mm reach, small enough to carry between benches. It targets labs, life-sciences and education, where its visually-oriented COBOTTA World tablet app lets non-programmers build pick-and-place tasks in minutes, while experts can use PacScript through the Remote TP virtual pendant or Python via ORiN/b-CAP. Safety is inherent-by-design with proprietary torque sensors monitoring torque and speed continuously on every axis, certified to ISO 10218-1 / ISO/TS 15066, and an electric gripper and 2D camera integrate directly onto the arm for force-controlled gripping and image-recognition tasks. Developed as an open platform, it slots readily into existing systems and has become a common research and laboratory-automation arm.
controller: Integrated controller (built into arm — no external cabinet)
ft_sensor: Proprietary torque sensors at each axis (functional safety)
safety_functions: Inherently safe design; continuous torque & speed monitoring on all axes
teach_pendant: COBOTTA World app (tablet, visual) + Remote TP virtual pendant
cameras: Integrated camera option (2D image recognition on-arm)

name: COBOTTA PRO 900
desc: The DENSO COBOTTA PRO 900 is the smaller of DENSO's high-speed PRO cobots — 6 kg payload, 900 mm reach, ±0.03 mm repeatability and a 2,100 mm/s TCP speed that puts it on par with 5- and 6-axis industrial robots during high-speed operation (the larger PRO 1300 pushes 12 kg and 2,500 mm/s). Its productivity-and-safety balance comes from proprietary high-rigidity torque sensors on lightweight slim axes for continuous torque/speed/area monitoring, plus a distinctive touch-sensing soft cover — silicon cushioning with embedded high-sensitivity contact sensors — that further cuts collision risk; with an added safety scanner it can safely ramp to industrial speeds when no one is near. DENSO reworked direct teaching so complex precision tasks like assembly can be memorised by track and fine-tuned to 0.1 mm, and paired it with a Blockly visual environment so novices can build high-precision applications. Pneumatic and I/O wiring route internally to the flange. NOTE: reach recorded as 900 mm per model designation; some aggregators list 1066 mm — flagged for datasheet confirmation.
ft_sensor: Proprietary high-rigidity torque sensors at each axis + touch-sensing soft cover (silicon-embedded contact sensors)
safety_functions: Continuous torque/speed/area monitoring; touch-sensing soft cover; safety-scanner speed boost to industrial levels when clear
teach_pendant: Direct teaching (0.1 mm fine-tuning) + Blockly visual environment
tool_io: Pneumatic + I/O wiring routed internally to flange
variants: COBOTTA PRO 1300 (12 kg, 1300 mm reach class, 2500 mm/s, ±0.04 mm)

name: MELFA ASSISTA (RV-5AS-D)
desc: The Mitsubishi Electric MELFA ASSISTA (RV-5AS-D) is Mitsubishi's collaborative robot, fusing the company's decades of industrial-robot experience with cobot-style ease of use — a 6-axis arm with 5 kg payload, 910 mm reach and a high ±0.03 mm repeatability at nominal load. It's designed to work hand-in-hand with people without fences or enclosures, using per-joint torque sensing for collision monitoring under ISO 10218-1 / ISO/TS 15066, an LED ring for at-a-glance status, and Direct Teaching buttons for point teaching without a pendant. Programming is deliberately open and intuitive via RT VisualBox's drag-and-drop visual environment (no-code), MELFA BASIC VI for depth, and RT ToolBox3, with a broad gripper and vision ecosystem including MELFA-Vision and the AI-driven MELFA SmartPlus option. Uncommon among cobots, it's engineered for food-safe environments, making it a fit for hygiene-sensitive pick-and-place, assembly, machine tending and inspection, as well as research and education.
ft_sensor: Torque sensing per joint (collision monitoring)
safety_functions: Collision monitoring; direct teaching; LED ring status indicator; ISO 10218-1 / ISO/TS 15066 compliant
teach_pendant: RT VisualBox / RT ToolBox3 (drag-and-drop) + Direct Teaching buttons
ai_model: MELFA SmartPlus — AI-based force sense, calibration & predictive maintenance (option)

name: CZ10
desc: The Nachi CZ10 is the collaborative robot from Nachi-Fujikoshi, one of Japan's oldest industrial-robot makers — a 6-axis, 10 kg-payload arm with a long 1,300 mm reach and ±0.08 mm repeatability, built on the company's welding and material-handling heritage. Its inherent-safety design maintains a 25 mm minimum clearance to prevent pinching, and torque sensors at every axis detect worker contact and stop the robot, third-party certified to ISO 10218-1 (plus TÜV and standard UL/CSA). An inline-wrist structure enables intuitive direct teaching, and wrist-integrated digital I/O (4 in / 3 out) with built-in φ4 air piping reduces installation wiring. The 61 kg arm carries IP65 protection (IP54 wire harness), operates 0–45 °C, runs at up to 180°/s joint speed (throttled to 250 mm/s in collaborative mode), and draws just 1.0 kVA with its CCZ controller. It mounts floor or inverted and targets machine tending, material handling, palletizing and dispensing.
joint_speed_max_dps: J1 120 / J2 120 / J3 180 / J4 180 / J5 180 / J6 180 °/s (250 mm/s max in collaborative mode)
ip_rating: IP65 (arm; wire harness IP54, controller IP20)
ft_sensor: Torque sensing at each axis; 25 mm minimum anti-pinch clearance (inherent safety)
safety_functions: Per-axis torque contact detection with stop; 25 mm anti-pinch space; LED green in collaborative mode; ISO 10218-1 3rd-party certified
teach_pendant: Nachi TP; direct teaching function
tool_io: Wrist digital I/O (4 in / 3 out) + built-in air piping (φ4); EtherCAT internal

name: YL012
desc: The Hyundai Robotics YL012 is the medium model of Hyundai's YL collaborative series — a 6-axis, 12 kg-payload cobot with a 1,305 mm reach, developed to operate directly alongside human workers. A Red Dot Design Award winner, its slim, organic, right-angle-free form isn't just aesthetic: all pneumatic, electrical and communication wiring is routed inside the arm joints for a clean profile that reduces snag points and interference in tight spaces, while cutting weight. LED flash lamps give 360° status visibility and an ergonomic handgrip with intuitive switches makes teaching quick and direct. It supports an unusually broad fieldbus set — PROFINET, EtherNet/IP, PROFIBUS, DeviceNet, CANopen, CC-Link (and IE Field), EtherCAT and Modbus TCP — for easy line integration, and its 12 kg reach suits palletizing, packaging, machine loading, polishing/deburring, gluing, injection-molding tending and inspection. A smaller YL005 (5 kg, 916 mm) completes the pair.
ft_sensor: Torque sensing per joint (collision detection)
safety_functions: Collision/crush-injury reduction; LED flash status lamps (360° visibility); ergonomic handgrip teaching
teach_pendant: Hi6 pendant + ergonomic handgrip switches
fieldbus: PROFINET / EtherNet-IP / PROFIBUS / DeviceNet / CANopen / CC-Link / EtherCAT / Modbus TCP
tool_io: Internal pneumatic + electrical + comms wiring routed through arm joints

name: CR10
desc: The Dobot CR10 is the high-reach model of Dobot's CR collaborative series — 10 kg payload across a long 1,525 mm reach with ±0.03 mm repeatability, from Dobot, China's #1 cobot exporter. Built for affordability and fast deployment (about 20 minutes to set up, one hour to production), it uses a plug-and-play design with simple wiring and quick accessory access, running on DC 48 V with a 4 m/s TCP speed and all joints spanning ±360°. Safety is a strength: 22 built-in features certified to ISO 13849 and ISO/TS 15066, five adjustable levels of collision detection, and optional DOBOT SafeSkin technology giving 15 cm proximity sensing and active protection. It's programmed through DobotStudio Pro (graphical and script), with Modbus/PROFINET/EtherNet-IP connectivity and a 32,000-hour MTBF. Part of a CR family spanning CR3 to CR16, the CR10 targets palletizing, loading/unloading and heavy material handling. NOTE: reach recorded as Dobot's official 1,525 mm; some aggregators list 1,300 mm (an earlier-gen figure).
ft_sensor: Collision detection — 5 adjustable levels; optional DOBOT SafeSkin (15 cm proximity sensing)
safety_pl: 22 built-in safety features; ISO 13849 / ISO/TS 15066 certified
safety_functions: 5-level adjustable collision detection; optional SafeSkin proximity active-protection; electromagnetic brakes

name: Nova 5
desc: The Dobot Nova 5 is a compact 6-axis collaborative robot with a 5 kg payload, 850 mm reach and a fine ±0.02 mm repeatability, designed by Dobot (China's #1 cobot exporter) for service, retail and light-industrial automation — it's a common choice for robotic coffee and beverage stations as well as light assembly and pick-and-place. It shares the Dobot cobot toolkit: adjustable collision detection with optional SafeSkin proximity sensing, IP54 sealing, electromagnetic brakes, and safety aligned to ISO 13849 / ISO/TS 15066, all programmed through the graphical DobotStudio Pro (plus script and Blockly) with Modbus, PROFINET and EtherNet/IP connectivity and a ROS driver. Its compact form and service-friendly design make it a fixture in customer-facing automation and education. NOTE: Dobot publishes core specs (payload/reach/repeatability); exact weight, joint speeds and power draw for the Nova 5 are logged as outreach rather than guessed.
ft_sensor: Collision detection (adjustable); optional SafeSkin
safety_functions: Adjustable collision detection; ISO 13849 / ISO/TS 15066 aligned; electromagnetic brakes
teach_pendant: DobotStudio Pro (graphical + script); drag teaching

name: ReBeL
desc: The igus ReBeL is the world's first cobot built around plastic strain-wave gears — a radical cost-and-weight play from the German motion-plastics specialist. At just 8.2 kg with a 2 kg payload, 664 mm reach and ±1 mm repeatability, it deliberately trades precision for affordability and low mass, using igus's self-lubricating tribo-polymer components in integrated joints (motor + strain-wave gearbox + absolute encoder) to hit a price point that opens robotics to SMEs, educators and developers. It runs from 24 V DC through the igus Robot Control (iRC) software — browser-based drag-and-drop programming — with a Python API, ROS driver and Modbus TCP/TCP-IP interfaces, and mounts on tables, mobile bases or gantries. It's not a high-accuracy industrial arm; its niche is accessible, lightweight automation for pick-and-place, inspection, lab work and light assembly where cost and simplicity matter more than sub-millimetre repeatability.
frame_material: Tribo-polymer (plastic) — world's first cobot with plastic strain-wave gears
actuator_type: Integrated motor + tribo-polymer strain-wave gearbox + absolute encoder per joint

name: Meca500
desc: The Mecademic Meca500 is, by the maker's account, the smallest and most compact six-axis industrial robot arm — and one of the most precise, with ±0.005 mm repeatability (five microns) that few arms of any size match. Reach is 330 mm from the flange (260 mm from wrist) with a 500 g rated payload (1 kg maximum under conditions), from a 4.6 kg body with the controller built inside. Its design philosophy is what sets it apart: rather than a stand-alone system with a pendant and its own software suite, the Meca500 is a plug-and-work slave component that integrates into any PC or PLC over Ethernet with no training courses, installs or add-on purchases — controlled by simple TCP/IP ASCII commands, a Python API, a web interface, or industrial fieldbuses (EtherCAT, PROFINET, EtherNet/IP) on the relevant variants. Powered by the PS200 module (90–250 VAC), offered in R3 and R4 revisions, it's a staple of precision electronics, semiconductor, lab-automation and micro-manipulation cells where footprint and accuracy dominate.
controller: Integrated controller (inside the arm) — plug-and-work slave component
api: TCP/IP ASCII command set + Python API

name: xArm 6
desc: The UFACTORY xArm 6 is the arm that made 5 kg-class manipulation affordable for labs and startups — 5 kg payload across 700 mm reach at ±0.1 mm repeatability and 1 m/s top speed, at roughly half the price of mainstream 6-axis rivals, which has made it one of the most common arms in mobile-manipulation and embodied-AI research stacks. Its aluminium and carbon-fiber structure is driven by outer-rotor brushless motors through industrial harmonic drives with 17-bit multi-turn absolute encoders, drawing a typical 200 W through the AC control box and mounting in any orientation (IP40, cleanroom-suitable). The software story is its second superpower: UFACTORY Studio's full GUI with drag-and-drop and simulation, open-source Python and C++ SDKs over Ethernet, Blockly, and official xarm_ros/ros2 packages, with a native ecosystem of grippers, vacuum tools and camera mounts. Collision detection and control-box e-stop cover safety basics for supervised light-industrial and research use.
actuator_type: Outer-rotor BLDC motors + industrial harmonic drives + 17-bit multi-turn absolute encoders
power_source: AC control box (500 W supply recommended)
controller: UFACTORY AC control box (xArm controller) — Ethernet, I/O

name: Lite 6
desc: The UFACTORY Lite 6 is a compact 6-axis tabletop arm built for benches where footprint and setup speed matter more than precision — 600 g payload across 440 mm reach at ±0.5 mm repeatability and 500 mm/s top speed, with the controller integrated so the whole system is arm-plus-Ethernet-cable. Its aluminium and carbon-fiber structure pairs direct-drive motors with harmonic drives to balance durability against cost (typical draw 150 W), and it inherits UFACTORY's full open software stack: Studio's drag-and-drop GUI, open-source Python and C++ SDKs, Blockly, and official ROS/ROS 2 support — which has made it a staple in university labs, imitation-learning rigs and light-automation pilots. UFACTORY itself notes the Lite 6 is not certified as a collaborative robot despite its safe desktop scale, an honest distinction most competitors skip. A Kit variant bundles the Lite Gripper and Lite Vacuum Gripper.
power_source: Integrated control box (350 W supply recommended)
variants: Lite 6 Kit (+ Lite Gripper + Lite Vacuum Gripper)

name: RO1
desc: The Standard Bots RO1 is an AI-native American-made cobot (built in Glen Cove, New York) that pairs class-leading hardware with GPT-level no-code programming — a best-in-class 18 kg payload across 1,300 mm reach at ±0.025 mm repeatability, positioned at roughly half the price of comparable arms with leasing from about $5/hour. Its arm uses six CAN-bus joints, each with two encoders, two independent torque-sensing methods and fail-safe brakes that engage on power loss — the basis of built-in collision detection and force limiting for fenceless work. Uniquely in its class it ships with an onboard 3D machine-vision system for object detection, screen reading and pick-without-programming, and can be programmed by natural language, a no-code touchscreen, or a Python API/SDK, learning new tasks from a single demonstration. It mounts without bolting into concrete for fast redeployment. Practical limits are documented openly: default tooltip speed 0.75 m/s, with speed reduced to 25% above 16 kg payload. Standard Bots (GE Appliances partner; $63M Series B) targets high-mix machine tending, inspection and palletizing up to 30 cases/min.
axes_config: 6-axis collaborative arm (CAN-bus joints, dual encoders each)
actuator_type: 6 CAN-bus joints — each with two encoders, dual torque-sensing methods, fail-safe brakes
ft_sensor: Dual torque-sensing per joint (collision detection + force limiting)
safety_functions: Built-in collision detection & force limiting; fail-safe brakes on power loss; fenceless collaborative operation

name: Gen3
desc: The Kinova Gen3 is one of the most widely used research manipulators in the world — an ultra-lightweight 7-axis arm (8.2 kg, 4 kg mid-workspace payload, 902 mm reach) chosen by hundreds of universities, startups and corporate labs for its portability and sub-30-minute setup. Its distinguishing features are research-grade: 1 kHz closed-loop low-level control, infinite-rotation joints, and Kinova smart actuators with integrated torque sensors plus current, voltage and temperature sensing for precise force control and rich state feedback. An optional Kinova Vision module integrates an Intel RealSense RGB-plus-depth camera directly at the end effector (30 cm–∞ colour, 18 cm–∞ depth) for perception work. It's driven through the Kortex API in C++ or Python with official ROS/ROS 2 kortex drivers, over Gigabit Ethernet from 24 VDC, and offered in 7-DoF, 6-DoF (891 mm) and Gen3 lite forms — the combination of light weight, torque sensing and open software making it a default arm for mobile-manipulation and imitation-learning research.
cameras: Optional Kinova Vision module — Intel RealSense: RGB (colour) + depth, 30 cm–∞ colour focal, 18 cm–∞ depth
ft_sensor: Integrated joint torque sensors (all actuators) + current/voltage/temperature sensing
actuator_type: Kinova smart actuators — integrated torque sensors, infinite joint rotation

name: OB7
desc: The Productive Robotics OB7 is an American-made (Carpinteria, California) 7-axis collaborative robot whose defining features are its extra joint and its no-code philosophy. The seventh axis gives it human-like dexterity to reach around obstacles and work in confined spaces that 6-axis arms can't, at a 5 kg payload and 1,000 mm reach. Its bigger differentiator is programming: OB7 is taught by demonstration — 'show, don't program' — so operators physically guide it through tasks with no code, no scripting and minimal training, which Productive Robotics markets as the simplest cobot to deploy. An optional OB7 Vision system adds camera-based part detection. Certified for fenceless collaboration (ISO 10218-1 / ISO/TS 15066), it targets CNC machine tending, assembly, pick-and-place, packaging and finishing for small and mid-size manufacturers, and comes in a family including longer-reach Stretch and higher-payload Max8/Max12 variants. NOTE: Productive Robotics publishes payload/reach/axis count and capability detail; exact weight, repeatability, joint speeds and IP rating are logged as outreach rather than invented.
axes_config: 7-axis collaborative arm (extra joint for human-like reach-around)
ft_sensor: Force sensing (collision detection)
safety_functions: Collision detection; fenceless collaborative operation; no-code teach-by-show

name: MOTOMAN HC20DTP
desc: The Yaskawa MOTOMAN HC20DTP is the largest cobot in Yaskawa's HC human-collaborative family — 20 kg payload across a 1,900 mm absolute reach (1,700 mm effective) at ±0.05 mm repeatability, from a rugged 140 kg aluminium-cast arm driven by Yaskawa's 200 V industrial servo drives. Built for fenceless palletizing and end-of-line packaging, it also handles harsh work — machine-tool loading, welding — thanks to IP67 sealing with a special drip-proof coating against coolants and dust, plus food-grade grease for food and pharma use. High-resolution torque sensors in each of its six joints enable fenceless human collaboration certified to PL d Cat. 3 with 25 distinct safety functions, including configurable envelopes, dual retract moves (Retract & Clamp-Release) and a Pushback function to move the arm aside during operation. Yaskawa targets easy entry: the tablet-based Smart Pendant guides programming and safety config with hand-guiding and Smart Frame, backed by Wizard programming, a plug-and-play accessory ecosystem, MotoSim offline simulation, and a choice of YRC1000 or compact YRC1000micro controllers.
power_source: 200 V Yaskawa servo drives; 1.5 kVA average

name: A2
desc: Unitree's 2025 flagship 'Stellar Explorer': 37 kg with hot-swappable dual 9,000 mAh batteries, carrying 25 kg continuously (100 kg standing) at up to 5 m/s, climbing 30 cm steps and 45° slopes, with front + rear LiDAR, IP56 body, Wi-Fi 6 and 20 km unloaded range.

name: A2-W (Stellar Hunter W)
desc: Wheeled variant of the A2 that swaps feet for powered wheels — rolling efficiency on flat ground, legged agility over steps and 45° slopes, with 12 dual-encoder joint motors, LiDAR + HD camera and 20–25 kg continuous payload.
runtime: 5+ h (3+ h with 25 kg payload, A2 platform)
note: A2 platform: class-leading endurance — ~2× Western rivals even with sensor loads

name: Go2-W
desc: Wheels-on-feet version of the popular Go2, blending rolling speed on smooth ground with legged climbing — same 4D LiDAR perception and app/SDK ecosystem as the standard Go2.
form_factor: Go2 with in-wheel motors on each leg (wheel-leg hybrid: flat-ground speed + obstacle crossing)
note: Wheeled variant of Go2 platform

name: Aliengo
desc: A mid-sized, fully electric 12-DoF quadruped from Unitree for research, education and controlled inspection, sitting between the compact A1 and the industrial B-series. Pairs dual depth cameras and VIO with a swappable 317 Wh battery and developer interfaces (dual Gigabit Ethernet, USB 3.0, ROS/Ubuntu).

name: Laikago
desc: Unitree's first commercial quadruped, launched in 2017 and named after Laika, the first dog in space. A 12-DoF electric platform driven by Unitree's own motors, it established the company's low-cost robot-dog lineage and was the predecessor to the A1 and Aliengo.
note: Unitree's FIRST quadruped — launched the low-cost quadruped era

name: Lynx (LYNX M20)
desc: Billed as the world's first industrial-grade wheeled-legged quadruped, the LYNX M20 fuses rolling speed with legged agility for power inspection, emergency response, logistics and exploration across mountains, wetlands and rubble. Hyper-flexible joints let it switch posture modes to cross pipelines, tunnels and stairs.

name: Lynx M20
desc: The world's first industrial wheeled-legged quadruped: 33 kg, 15 kg payload, 5 m/s lab speed (3 m/s operating), IP66, 96-line LiDAR with omnidirectional avoidance, 25 cm continuous stairs, 80 cm single obstacles and −20 to 55°C endurance — built for power-line inspection, mining and disaster response. M20 Pro from US$61,200.

name: MagicDog
desc: MagicLab's agile consumer-and-education quadruped — a Go2-class robot dog with AI interaction, gymnastic locomotion demos and an SDK for developers, from the Chinese embodied-AI startup also building humanoids.

name: MagicDog-W
desc: Wheeled-legged version of the MagicDog, adding hub-motor wheels for fast rolling travel while keeping legged obstacle negotiation.
note: Per-model specs sparse — verified platform only

name: W1
desc: The LimX W1 was LimX Dynamics' first wheeled-legged robot, released September 2023 — an early research platform that skates on wheels mounted at each leg-end while retaining the ability to stand, walk and climb like a legged robot. It demonstrated hybrid wheel-legged locomotion at up to 10 m/s (wheeled) with a 15 kg payload. As LimX's first-generation legged platform (preceding the TRON series and its humanoids), W1 has since been superseded and is no longer in the current product lineup, so detailed specifications are limited; unpublished fields are flagged for outreach rather than guessed. Verified specs and history from LimX's official site and company timeline.
actuator_type: Wheel-legged hybrid (wheels on each leg — rolls, walks, climbs)
note: Recategorised to Quadruped (was mis-surveyed as humanoid). First LimX wheeled-legged robot; limited public specs (early R&D platform, no current spec page) — unpublished fields flagged for outreach.

locomotion: Wheel-legged: skates on wheels, stands/walks on legs, climbs

Backed by Alibaba, JD.com, and others; ~200M RMB angel/pre-A. Awards incl. iF Design 2024.

name: Max
desc: Tencent Robotics X Lab's multimode quadruped, first shown in 2021 and optimised in 2022. A hybrid leg-wheel design lets it walk, run, jump and climb like a dog, then glide on wheels embedded in its leg joints. Driven by Tencent's proprietary low-latency 'keen nervous system' control, it performs backward somersaults, two-leg balancing and learns new gaits within hours, with terrain recognition accurate to under 2 cm.
actuator_type: Electric (3 per leg) with wheels on leg joints
form_factor: Wheel-legged hybrid (wheels on knees — walks, rolls, does flips)
